docs.title: spxa
docs.text:
Stochastic processes as first-class algebraic objects.

from spxa.zoo.levy import VarianceGamma, GammaProcess

X = VarianceGamma(sigma=0.2, nu=0.1, theta=-0.1)
Y = GammaProcess(a=1.0, b=2.0)

Z = X + 0.5 * Y
Z.triplet          # exact Lévy–Khintchine triplet
Z.cumulants(4)     # exact symbolic cumulants
Z.__story__()      # derivation trace

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Theory: Lévy–Khintchine — the bijection that makes arithmetic exact
  • Theory: Triplet arithmetic — the rules behind every operator
  • Theory: Beyond Lévy — fBM, Hawkes, OU-Lévy and the degradation policy
  • Theory: Model Morphing — exact interpolation between processes along triplet, generator, Fisher–Rao and Wasserstein paths
  • Theory: Information geometry — Fisher metric, α-connections, curvature, Rao distance and natural gradient
  • Theory: Rough paths & signatures — tensor algebra, log-signatures, the signature kernel and expected signatures
  • Theory: Rough volatility — Volterra fBM, rough Bergomi and the fractional Riccati equation of rough Heston
  • Theory: Copulas — Sklar, dependence measures, copula families, estimation and coupled simulation
  • Theory: Stochastic control — HJB, LQG, Merton, Almgren–Chriss, Avellaneda–Stoikov and finite-difference HJB
  • Theory: Estimation & calibration — exact MLE, GMM/ECF, filtering, surface calibration and inference
  • Process registry — all implemented processes with exactness levels and references
  • Contributing — how to add processes, operations, and core changes

docs.title: ExactnessLevel
docs.text:
from spxa.core import ExactnessLevel

An enum describing the analytical guarantee attached to a process or result. All arithmetic between two processes produces the minimum level of its operands.

Member Meaning ExactnessLevel.EXACT Lévy–Khintchine triplet known in closed form. Triplet arithmetic is analytically exact. ExactnessLevel.MOMENT_PROPAGATION No closed-form triplet. Finite moments tracked where computable. ExactnessLevel.SIMULATION_ONLY No analytical handle. Sample paths only.

Ordering: EXACT < MOMENT_PROPAGATION < SIMULATION_ONLY (where < means "more informative than").

ExactnessLevel.combine(a, b)  # → ExactnessLevel
# Returns the minimum (most degraded) of two levels.

Comparison operators <, <=, >, >= work as expected.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
from spxa.core import Process  # abstract base class

All stochastic processes in spxa inherit from Process. Every instance is immutable — operators return new process objects, never mutate in place.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
process.exactness    # → ExactnessLevel
process.triplet      # → LevyTriplet   (raises ExactnessError if not EXACT)
process.properties   # → ProcessProperties

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Z = X + Y            # sum of independent processes
Z = X - Y            # X + (-1)*Y
Z = c * X            # scalar multiplication, c ∈ ℝ \ {0}
Z = X * c            # same as c * X
Z = -X               # negation
Z = X @ T            # subordination: Z_t = X_{T_t}  (T must be a subordinator)
Z = sum([X, Y, ...]) # Python's built-in sum() works via __radd__

All operators propagate ExactnessLevel and ProcessProperties automatically. If ExactnessLevel degrades, SpxaDegradationWarning is emitted with a mathematical reason.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
process.cumulants(order: int) -> dict[int, float]
Return cumulants κ₁, …, κ_order of X₁ (per unit time). Available for EXACT and MOMENT_PROPAGATION. Keys are integers 1..order, values are floats.

process.char_func(u: float | np.ndarray, t: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
Evaluate E[e^{iuX_t}]. Available for EXACT. For processes with a closed-form formula this delegates to char_func_exact; otherwise uses Lévy–Khintchine numerical integration.

process.simulate(
    n_steps: int,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float = 1.0,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Simulate sample paths. Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1). All paths start at 0: paths[:, 0] == 0 always. For multivariate processes returns shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1, d).

process.__story__() -> str
Plain-text derivation trace: how this process was composed, with citations to Sato (1999) and other primary sources. Suitable for terminal printing.

process.__story_latex__() -> str
MathJax-ready LaTeX derivation. Returns a \begin{aligned}...\end{aligned} block. Use in Jupyter: 
from IPython.display import display, Math
display(Math(Z.__story_latex__()))

docs.title: LevyTriplet
docs.text:
from spxa.core import LevyTriplet

Immutable dataclass representing the Lévy–Khintchine triplet \((b, \sigma^2, \nu)\).

LevyTriplet(b: float, sigma_sq: float, nu: LevyMeasure)
Field Type Description b float Drift, defined w.r.t. truncation function h(x)=𝟙_{ sigma_sq float Gaussian variance σ² ≥ 0 nu LevyMeasure Lévy measure on ℝ{0}

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
triplet + other           # → LevyTriplet  (b adds, σ² adds, ν adds)
triplet.scale(c: float)   # → LevyTriplet  (image measure ν(·/c), drift corrected)

triplet.cumulant(n: int) -> float
# n-th cumulant of X₁:
#   κ₁ = b + ∫_{|x|>1} x ν(dx)
#   κ₂ = σ² + ∫ x² ν(dx)
#   κ_n = ∫ xⁿ ν(dx)  for n ≥ 3

triplet.char_exp(u: float | np.ndarray, t: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
# Evaluate E[e^{iuX_t}] = exp(t·ψ(u)) via numerical Lévy–Khintchine integration.
# For processes with char_func_exact, prefer that instead.

docs.title: LevyMeasure hierarchy
docs.text: from spxa.core import LevyMeasure, DensityLevyMeasure, CompoundLevyMeasure, ScaledLevyMeasure

docs.title: LevyMeasure (abstract base)
docs.text:
measure.density(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray   # Lévy density k(x): ν(dx)=k(x)dx
measure.total_mass() -> float                   # ν(ℝ\{0}), np.inf for infinite activity
measure.tail(x: float) -> float                 # ν((x,∞)) for x > 0
measure.moment(n: int) -> float                 # ∫ xⁿ ν(dx), n ≥ 1
measure.is_finite_activity() -> bool            # total_mass() < ∞
measure + other                                 # → CompoundLevyMeasure

docs.title: DensityLevyMeasure
docs.text:
Lévy measure specified by a density function. Used for all named processes (Gamma, NIG, VG, CGMY, etc.). The density, total mass, tail function, and moment formulas are provided at construction time.

DensityLevyMeasure(
    _density_fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    _total_mass: float,
    _tail_fn: Callable[[float], float] | None = None,
    _moment_fns: dict[int, Callable[[], float]] = {},
)

docs.title: CompoundLevyMeasure
docs.text: Sum of multiple Lévy measures. Produced by measure1 + measure2. All methods delegate to components.

docs.title: ScaledLevyMeasure
docs.text: Image measure ν_Z where Z=cX: ν_Z(B)=ν_X(B/c). Produced by LevyTriplet.scale(c).

docs.title: ProcessProperties
docs.text:
from spxa.core import ProcessProperties

A dataclass carrying mathematical properties of a process. Propagated automatically under all operations. Use process.properties to access.

Field Type Meaning has_stationary_increments bool X_{t+s}−X_s ∼ X_t in distribution has_independent_increments bool Increments on disjoint intervals independent is_martingale bool E[X_t | F_s] = X_s a.s. has_finite_variance bool Var(X_t) < ∞ has_finite_mean bool E[|X_t|] < ∞ self_similarity_index float \| None H such that X_{ct} ∼ c^H X_t tail_index float \| None α such that ν((x,∞)) ∼ x^{−α} is_subordinator bool Paths are non-decreasing a.s. hurst_index float \| None Hurst index (fBM only) notes list[str] Human-readable notes appended during composition

Propagation rules — automatically applied by operators:

Operation Stationary incr. Indep. incr. Martingale Subordinator X + Y X and Y both X and Y both X and Y both X and Y both c·X preserved preserved preserved (c≠0) c > 0 only X @ T always True always True False (check specific) False

docs.title: Exceptions and warnings
docs.text: from spxa.core import SpxaError, ExactnessError, SpxaDegradationWarning

docs.title: SpxaError
docs.text: Base class for all spxa exceptions.

docs.title: ExactnessError(SpxaError)
docs.text:
Raised when a method requiring a higher ExactnessLevel is called. Always includes a mathematical explanation of what is missing and why.

# Attributes
err.method    # str — name of the method that was called
err.required  # str — ExactnessLevel name required
err.actual    # str — ExactnessLevel name of the process
err.reason    # str — mathematical explanation

Common triggers: .triplet on a beyond-Lévy process; .char_func on SIMULATION_ONLY; .cumulants on SIMULATION_ONLY.

docs.title: SpxaDegradationWarning(UserWarning)
docs.text:
Emitted when an operation degrades ExactnessLevel. Always includes the mathematical reason (which Lévy property was violated and why).

import warnings
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    Z = fbm + bm   # emits SpxaDegradationWarning

docs.title: Zoo — Lévy processes
docs.text: All processes in spxa.zoo.levy have ExactnessLevel.EXACT. All inherit from Process and implement triplet, cumulants, char_func, and simulate.

docs.title: BrownianMotion
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import BrownianMotion

BrownianMotion(mu: float = 0.0, sigma: float = 1.0)

Standard Brownian motion with drift. Triplet: (μ, σ², 0) — no jump component.

Parameter Constraint Meaning mu ℝ Drift per unit time sigma > 0 Diffusion coefficient

Cumulants: κ₁ = μ, κ₂ = σ², κ_n = 0 for n ≥ 3.

Extra methods: 

bm.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)  # exp(iμtu − σ²tu²/2)

Properties: self-similarity index H=0.5; martingale iff μ=0.

Reference: Wiener (1923); Sato (1999), Example 8.3.

docs.title: GammaProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import GammaProcess

GammaProcess(a: float, b: float)

Pure-jump subordinator with independent Gamma increments. Lévy density: k(x) = a·x⁻¹·e^{−bx}·𝟙_{x>0}.

Parameter Constraint Meaning a > 0 Shape rate (jump frequency) b > 0 Inverse scale (jump size decay)

Cumulants: κ_n = a·(n−1)! / b^n.

Extra methods: 

gp.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float
gp.bernstein_function(lam: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
# Exact: φ(s) = a·log(1 + s/b)

Properties: is_subordinator=True; infinite activity.

Reference: Moran (1968); Cont & Tankov (2004), Table 4.2.

docs.title: VarianceGamma
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import VarianceGamma

VarianceGamma(sigma: float, nu: float, theta: float = 0.0)

Brownian motion with drift subordinated by a Gamma process. Infinite activity, finite variation. Standard model for equity log-returns.

Parameter Constraint Meaning sigma > 0 Volatility of BM component nu > 0 Variance rate of Gamma subordinator theta ℝ Drift of BM component (controls skewness)

Cumulants (Madan, Carr & Chang 1998): - κ₁ = θ - κ₂ = σ² + θ²ν - κ₃ = 2θ³ν² + 3σ²θν - κ₄ = 3σ⁴ν + 12σ²θ²ν² + 6θ⁴ν³

Extra methods: 

vg.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# ((1 − iuθν + σ²νu²/2))^{−t/ν}

Simulation: Gamma subordination: G ~ Gamma(Δt/ν, ν); ΔX = θG + σ√G·Z.

Reference: Madan, Carr & Chang (1998).

docs.title: NIG
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import NIG

NIG(alpha: float, beta: float, delta: float, mu: float = 0.0)

Normal Inverse Gaussian process. BM subordinated by an Inverse Gaussian process. Semi-heavy tails (exponential decay). Parameter space: α > |β|.

Parameter Constraint Meaning alpha > 0, > |β| Tail heaviness (larger → lighter tails) beta ∈ (−α, α) Asymmetry (β < 0 → left skew) delta > 0 Scale mu ℝ Location shift

Let γ = √(α² − β²).

Cumulants (Barndorff-Nielsen 1997): - κ₁ = μ + δβ/γ - κ₂ = δα²/γ³ - κ₃ = 3δα²β/γ⁵ - κ₄ = 3δα²(α²+4β²)/γ⁷

Extra methods: 

nig.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(t·(iμu + δ(γ − √(α² − (β+iu)²))))

Simulation: Inverse Gaussian subordination.

Reference: Barndorff-Nielsen (1997).

docs.title: GeneralizedHyperbolicProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import GeneralizedHyperbolicProcess, GeneralizedHyperbolic, GHProcess, GH

gh = GeneralizedHyperbolicProcess(
    lambda_param=1.0,
    alpha=2.5,
    beta=-0.5,
    delta=1.2,
    mu=0.05,
)

The Generalized Hyperbolic (GH) Lévy process (Barndorff-Nielsen 1977; Eberlein & Prause 2002) is generated by the 5-parameter Generalized Hyperbolic distribution, representing Brownian motion subordinated by a Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) process: $\(X_t = \mu t + \beta Z_t + \sqrt{Z_t} W_t, \quad Z_t \sim \mathrm{GIG}(\lambda, \delta, \gamma)\)$ where \(\gamma = \sqrt{\alpha^2 - \beta^2}\).

Parameter Constraint Meaning lambda_param (or lam) \(\mathbb{R}\) Subordinator shape (\(\lambda = -1/2\): NIG, \(\lambda = 1\): Hyperbolic) alpha $> 0, > \beta beta \(\in (-\alpha, \alpha)\) Skewness / asymmetry delta \(> 0\) Scale parameter mu \(\mathbb{R}\) Location / drift parameter

Key Properties & Subfamilies: - is_nig — True when \(\lambda = -0.5\) (Normal Inverse Gaussian) - is_hyperbolic — True when \(\lambda = 1.0\) (Hyperbolic) - subfamily — "NIG", "Hyperbolic", "Hyperbolic Cosine", or "General GH" - gamma — \(\gamma = \sqrt{\alpha^2 - \beta^2}\)

Characteristic Function & Cumulants: - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t) = \exp(t \psi(u))\) - char_exponent(u) — characteristic exponent \(\psi(u) = i\mu u + \lambda \ln\frac{\gamma}{\zeta(u)} + \ln\frac{K_\lambda(\delta \zeta(u))}{K_\lambda(\delta \gamma)}\) with \(\zeta(u) = \sqrt{\alpha^2 - (\beta + iu)^2}\) - cumulant_exact(order, t=1.0) — closed-form cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\) derived from GIG moments - cumulants(order=4, t=1.0) — dictionary of exact cumulants

Option Pricing: - drift_compensator() — martingale compensator \(\omega = -\psi(-i)\) (requires \(\alpha > |\beta + 1|\)) - call_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.0, q=0.0, s0=100.0) — European call option price via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.0, q=0.0, s0=100.0) — European put option price via Put-Call parity - implied_volatility(K, T=1.0, r=0.0, q=0.0, s0=100.0) — Black-Scholes implied volatility

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact Inverse Gaussian subordination for NIG; fast vectorized Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion for general GH

References: - Barndorff-Nielsen, O. E. (1977). Exponentially decreasing distributions and the normal distribution. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A, 353(1674), 401–419. - Barndorff-Nielsen, O. E. & Halgreen, C. (1977). Infinite divisibility of the hyperbolic and generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. Z. Wahrscheinlichkeit, 38, 309–312. - Eberlein, E. & Prause, K. (2002). The generalized hyperbolic model: Financial derivatives and risk measures. Mathematical Finance — Bachelier Congress 2000, 245–267.

docs.title: CGMY
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import CGMY

CGMY(C: float, G: float, M: float, Y: float)

Four-parameter pure-jump process. Nests VG (Y=0) and α-stable (G=M→0). Controls tail heaviness, jump activity, and asymmetry independently. Lévy density: C·e^{−Gx}/x^{1+Y}·𝟙_{x>0} + C·e^{−M|x|}/|x|^{1+Y}·𝟙_{x<0}.

Parameter Constraint Meaning C > 0 Jump intensity G ≥ 0 Right-tail decay rate M ≥ 0 Left-tail decay rate Y < 2 Fine structure: Y<0 finite activity, 0≤Y<1 infinite activity finite variation, 1≤Y<2 infinite variation

Cumulants (Carr et al. 2002, eq. 2): κ_n = C·Γ(n−Y)·(M^{Y−n} + (−1)^n·G^{Y−n}) — valid for n > Y.

Extra methods: 

cgmy.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float
cgmy.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(t·C·Γ(−Y)·((M−iu)^Y − M^Y + (G+iu)^Y − G^Y))

Reference: Carr, Geman, Madan & Yor (2002).

docs.title: AlphaStable
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import AlphaStable

AlphaStable(alpha: float, beta: float = 0.0, sigma: float = 1.0, mu: float = 0.0)

α-stable Lévy process. Only class of Lévy processes closed under addition and scaling. Power-law tails for α < 2.

Parameter Constraint Meaning alpha ∈ (0, 2] Stability index. α=2 → Gaussian, α=1 → Cauchy beta ∈ [−1, 1] Skewness. β=0 → symmetric sigma > 0 Scale mu ℝ Location

Moments: E[|X₁|^p] < ∞ iff p < α. Mean finite iff α > 1. Variance finite iff α = 2.

Extra methods: 

stable.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(t·(−σ^α|u|^α(1 − iβ·sign(u)·tan(πα/2)) + iμu))  for α ≠ 1

Properties: self_similarity_index = 1/α.

Simulation: Chambers–Mallows–Stuck (1976) algorithm — exact.

Reference: Samorodnitsky & Taqqu (1994); Nolan (2020).

docs.title: MeixnerProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import MeixnerProcess

MeixnerProcess(alpha: float, beta: float, delta: float, m: float = 0.0)

Pure-jump process with hypergeometric characteristic function and orthogonal polynomial structure (Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials are eigenfunctions of its generator).

Parameter Constraint Meaning alpha > 0 Scale beta ∈ (−π, π) Asymmetry. β=0 → symmetric delta > 0 Shape (jump intensity) m ℝ Location shift

Cumulants (Schoutens & Teugels 1998): - κ₁ = δα·tan(β/2) + m - κ₂ = δα²/(2cos²(β/2)) - κ₃ = δα³·sin(β/2)/(2cos³(β/2)) - κ₄ = δα⁴(2+cosβ)/(8cos⁴(β/2))

Extra methods: 

mx.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(imu)·(cos(β/2)/cosh((αu−iβ)/2))^{2δt}

mx.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float

Simulation: Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion.

Reference: Schoutens & Teugels (1998).

docs.title: PoissonProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import PoissonProcess

PoissonProcess(rate: float, jump_size: float = 1.0)

Homogeneous Poisson process with constant jump size. Finite activity, discrete jumps.

Parameter Constraint Meaning rate > 0 Arrival rate λ (jumps per unit time) jump_size ℝ{0} Size of each jump c

Cumulants: κ_n(X_t) = λ·c^n·t for all n ≥ 1.

Properties: is_subordinator=True iff jump_size > 0; finite activity.

Simulation: Poisson-distributed increment counts.

Reference: Kingman (1993); Sato (1999), Example 8.4.

docs.title: CompoundPoisson
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import (
    CompoundPoisson,
    NormalJump,
    ExponentialJump,
    DoubleExponentialJump,
    UniformJump,
    DiscreteJump,
)

CompoundPoisson(
    rate: float,
    jump_dist: JumpDistribution | str | float = None,
    **kwargs,
)

Compound Poisson process: \(X_t = \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\), where \(N_t \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda t)\) and \(\{Y_i\}\) are i.i.d. random jump sizes. Finite activity, pure jump.

Parameter Constraint Meaning rate > 0 Arrival intensity \(\lambda\) (jumps per unit time) jump_dist JumpDistribution, str, or float Jump size probability law (default: NormalJump(mean=0, std=1))

Supported Jump Distributions: - NormalJump(mean=0.0, std=1.0): Gaussian jump sizes \(Y \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)\) - ExponentialJump(rate=1.0): Positive exponential jump sizes \(Y \sim \text{Exp}(\beta)\) - DoubleExponentialJump(p=0.5, eta1=1.0, eta2=1.0): Asymmetric double-exponential (Laplace) jump sizes - UniformJump(low=-1.0, high=1.0): Continuous uniform jump sizes on \([a, b]\) - DiscreteJump(values, probs=None): Discrete point mass jump sizes \(\{v_k\}\) with probabilities \(\{p_k\}\)

Triplet: \((b = \lambda \mathbb{E}[Y \mathbf{1}_{|Y| \le 1}], \sigma^2 = 0, \nu = \lambda F_Y)\).

Cumulants: \(\kappa_n(X_t) = \lambda t \mathbb{E}[Y^n]\) for all \(n \ge 1\).

Characteristic function: \(\mathbb{E}[e^{iuX_t}] = \exp(\lambda t (\phi_Y(u) - 1))\).

Properties: - is_martingale=True iff \(\mathbb{E}[Y] = 0\). - is_subordinator=True iff jumps are strictly positive (\(Y > 0\)). - Finite activity: \(\nu(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}) = \lambda < \infty\).

Simulation: Exact vectorized increment simulation via Poisson thinning and jump compounding.

Reference: Kingman (1993); Cont & Tankov (2004), Section 3.4; Sato (1999), Example 8.4.

docs.title: InverseGaussianProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import InverseGaussianProcess

InverseGaussianProcess(mu: float, lam: float)

Subordinator with independent IG-distributed increments. Fundamental in NIG construction. Lévy density: √(λ/2π)·x^{−3/2}·exp(−λ(x−μ)²/(2μ²x)) for x > 0.

Parameter Constraint Meaning mu > 0 Mean of X₁ lam > 0 Shape; Var(X₁) = μ³/λ

Cumulants (Tweedie 1957, eq. 2.5): κ_n = (2n−1)!!·μ^{2n−1}/λ^{n−1} where (2n−1)!! = 1·3·5·…·(2n−1).

Explicitly: κ₁ = μ, κ₂ = 3μ³/λ, κ₃ = 15μ⁵/λ², κ₄ = 105μ⁷/λ³.

Extra methods: 

ig.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float
ig.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(t·(λ/μ)·(1 − √(1 − 2iuμ²/λ)))

ig.bernstein_function(lam: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
# Exact: φ(s) = (λ/μ)(1 − √(1 − 2μ²s/λ))

Properties: is_subordinator=True; infinite activity.

Reference: Tweedie (1957); Schilling et al. (2012), Example 3.12.

docs.title: TemperedStable
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import TemperedStable

TemperedStable(alpha: float, C: float, lam: float)

Pure-jump subordinator with Lévy density C·x^{−1−α}·exp(−λx) for x>0. All moments finite; infinite activity. Bridges between stable and Gamma.

Parameter Constraint Meaning alpha ∈ (0, 1) Stability index (controls small-jump behaviour) C > 0 Jump intensity lam > 0 Tempering (exponential decay of large jumps)

Cumulants (Rosiński 2007, Prop. 2.1): κ_n = C·Γ(n−α)/λ^{n−α} for all n ≥ 1.

Extra methods: 

ts.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float
ts.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# exp(t·C·Γ(−α)·((λ−iu)^α − λ^α))

ts.bernstein_function(lam: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
# Exact: φ(s) = −C·Γ(−α)·((λ+s)^α − λ^α)  [>0 since Γ(−α)<0 for α∈(0,1)]

Properties: is_subordinator=True; infinite activity; all moments finite.

Simulation: Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion.

Reference: Rosiński (2007); Schilling et al. (2012), Example 3.8.

docs.title: NegativeBinomialProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.levy import NegativeBinomialProcess

NegativeBinomialProcess(r: float, p: float)

Finite-activity pure-jump subordinator with NegBin-distributed increments. Discrete Lévy measure: ν = Σ_{k=1}^∞ (r·p^k/k)·δ_k. Equivalent to a Poisson process with Gamma-distributed rate.

Parameter Constraint Meaning r > 0 Shape (dispersion) p ∈ (0, 1) Success probability

Mean = rp/(1−p), Var = rp/(1−p)² > Mean (overdispersed).

Cumulants (Johnson et al. 2005, Table 5.2): - κ₁ = rp/(1−p) - κ₂ = rp/(1−p)² - κ₃ = rp(1+p)/(1−p)³ - κ₄ = rp(1+4p+p²)/(1−p)⁴

Extra methods: 

nb.cumulant_exact(n: int, t: float = 1.0) -> float
nb.char_func_exact(u, t=1.0)
# ((1−p)/(1−p·e^{iu}))^{rt}

Properties: is_subordinator=True; finite activity; integer-valued paths.

Simulation: numpy.negative_binomial(n=r·Δt, p=1−p) — exact.

Reference: Quenouille (1949); Johnson, Kemp & Kotz (2005), Chapter 5.

docs.title: MertonJumpDiffusion
docs.text:
from spxa import MertonJumpDiffusion, MertonProcess, Merton76

merton = MertonJumpDiffusion(drift=0.05, sigma=0.15, rate=1.5, jump_mean=-0.08, jump_std=0.12)

Merton (1976) jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with compound Poisson normal jump shocks:

\[X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i, \quad Y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_J, \sigma_J^2)\]

where \(W_t\) is standard Brownian motion, \(N_t \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda t)\), and \(Y_i\) are independent Gaussian jump sizes.

Parameter Constraint Meaning drift real, default 0.0 Continuous drift parameter \(\mu\) (alias: mu) sigma > 0, default 0.2 Continuous diffusion volatility \(\sigma\) (alias: vol) rate > 0, default 1.0 Jump arrival intensity \(\lambda\) (alias: lam, jump_rate) jump_mean real, default -0.05 Mean jump size \(\mu_J\) (alias: mu_j, mean_jump) jump_std > 0, default 0.15 Jump size standard deviation \(\sigma_J\) (alias: sigma_j, std_jump)

Exactness: EXACT (full Lévy–Khintchine triplet and analytical characteristic exponent).

Lévy Triplet: - \(\sigma^2 = \sigma^2\) - \(\nu(dx) = \lambda \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_J} \exp\left(-\frac{(x - \mu_J)^2}{2\sigma_J^2}\right) dx\) (finite activity, total mass \(\lambda\)) - \(b = \mu + \lambda \int_{-1}^1 x \, \mathcal{N}(x; \mu_J, \sigma_J^2) dx\) (exact closed-form error function integral)

Distributional Analytics: 

merton.char_exponent(u)            # ψ(u) = iμu - ½σ²u² + λ(exp(iu μ_J - ½σ_J²u²) - 1)
merton.char_func(u, t=1.0)         # exp(t ψ(u))
merton.cumulants(order=5)          # κ_1, ..., κ_5 in exact closed form
merton.expected_relative_jump      # k̄ = exp(μ_J + ½σ_J²) - 1

Merton (1976) Analytical Option Pricing: 

# Evaluates Merton's analytical series via Poisson mixture of Black–Scholes formulas
merton.call_price(K=100.0, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05, q=0.0)
merton.put_price(K=100.0, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05, q=0.0)

# Implied volatility inversion
merton.implied_volatility(K=100.0, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05)
merton.implied_vol_smile(strikes=[80, 90, 100, 110, 120], T=1.0, S0=100.0)

Simulation: 

# Exact simulation with zero discretization error for any step size Δt
paths = merton.simulate(n_steps=100, n_paths=1000, T=1.0)

References: - Merton, R. C. (1976). Option pricing when underlying stock returns are discontinuous. Journal of Financial Economics, 3(1–2), 125–144. - Cont, R. & Tankov, P. (2004). Financial Modelling with Jump Processes. Chapman & Hall/CRC. Section 3.5.

docs.title: KouJumpDiffusion
docs.text:
from spxa import KouJumpDiffusion, KouProcess, Kou72, Kou02

kou = KouJumpDiffusion(
    drift=0.05,
    sigma=0.15,
    rate=1.5,
    p=0.4,
    eta1=10.0,
    eta2=5.0,
)

The Kou (2002) model combines continuous Brownian diffusion with compound Poisson jump shocks whose sizes follow an asymmetric double exponential distribution: $\(X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\)$ with jump density \(f_Y(y) = p \eta_1 e^{-\eta_1 y}\mathbb{I}_{y \ge 0} + (1-p) \eta_2 e^{\eta_2 y}\mathbb{I}_{y < 0}\).

Exact Lévy Triplet: - triplet.b — analytical truncated drift \(b = \mu + \lambda \left[ \frac{p}{\eta_1}(1 - e^{-\eta_1}(1+\eta_1)) - \frac{1-p}{\eta_2}(1 - e^{-\eta_2}(1+\eta_2)) \right]\) - triplet.sigma_sq — diffusion volatility \(\sigma^2\) - triplet.nu — finite activity double-exponential jump measure with total mass \(\lambda\)

Distributional Analytics: - char_exp(u) — characteristic exponent \(\psi(u) = i \mu u - \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 u^2 + \lambda \left( \frac{p \eta_1}{\eta_1 - i u} + \frac{(1-p)\eta_2}{\eta_2 + i u} - 1 \right)\) - characteristic_function(u, t=1.0) — \(e^{t \psi(u)}\) - cumulants(order=5, t=1.0) — analytical cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_5\) - expected_relative_jump — \(\kappa = \frac{p \eta_1}{\eta_1 - 1} + \frac{(1-p)\eta_2}{\eta_2 + 1} - 1\)

Option Pricing & Volatility Smile: - call_price(strikes, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05, q=0.0) — European call prices via Gil–Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(strikes, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05, q=0.0) — European put prices via exact Put-Call parity - implied_vol_smile(strikes, T=1.0, S0=100.0, r=0.05, q=0.0) — Black–Scholes implied volatility inversion

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact simulation with zero discretization error

References: - Kou, S. G. (2002). A jump-diffusion model for option pricing. Management Science, 48(8), 1086–1101. - Kou, S. G. & Wang, H. (2004). Option pricing under a double exponential jump diffusion model. Management Science, 50(9), 1178–1192.

docs.title: Zoo — beyond Lévy
docs.text: Processes in spxa.zoo.beyond have ExactnessLevel.MOMENT_PROPAGATION. Calling .triplet always raises ExactnessError with a mathematical explanation.

docs.title: BatesProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import BatesProcess, BatesModel, Bates96, SVJ

bates = BatesProcess(
    v0=0.04,
    kappa=2.0,
    theta=0.04,
    sigma_v=0.30,
    rho=-0.60,
    rate=1.2,
    jump_mean=-0.06,
    jump_std=0.12,
    mu=0.05,
    s0=100.0,
)

The Bates (1996) model augments the Heston (1993) stochastic volatility model with log-normal Merton (1976) price jumps: $\(dS_t = (\mu - q - \lambda \bar{k}) S_t dt + \sqrt{V_t} S_t dW_t^S + S_{t-} (e^Y - 1) dN_t\)$ $\(dV_t = \kappa (\theta - V_t) dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V\)$ with correlation \(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^S dW_t^V] = \rho dt\), Poisson jump intensity \(\lambda\), jump size \(Y \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_J, \sigma_J^2)\), and martingale drift compensator \(-\lambda \bar{k}\) where \(\bar{k} = \mathbb{E}[e^Y - 1] = \exp(\mu_J + \frac{1}{2}\sigma_J^2) - 1\).

Structural Properties & Variance Analytics: - feller_ratio — Feller ratio \(\frac{2\kappa\theta}{\sigma_v^2}\) - is_feller_satisfied — True when \(2\kappa\theta > \sigma_v^2\) - expected_relative_jump — \(\bar{k} = \exp(\mu_J + \frac{1}{2}\sigma_J^2) - 1\) - drift_compensator — \(-\lambda \bar{k}\) - variance_mean(t) — analytical conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[V_t \mid V_0]\) - variance_var(t) — analytical conditional variance \(\mathrm{Var}(V_t \mid V_0)\) - expected_integrated_variance(t) — \(\mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^t V_s ds\right] = \theta t + (v_0 - \theta)\frac{1 - e^{-\kappa t}}{\kappa}\)

Characteristic Function & Cumulants: - char_func(u, t=1.0) — continuous Albrecher et al. (2007) characteristic function factored with compound Poisson jumps - asset_char_func(u, t=1.0) — characteristic function of \(\ln S_t\) - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — expected log-return - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — variance of log-return - conditional_cumulants(t=1.0, order=4) — cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\)

Option Pricing & Volatility Smile: - call_price(strikes, T=1.0, r=None, q=0.0) — European call pricing via Gil–Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(strikes, T=1.0, r=None, q=0.0) — European put pricing via exact Put-Call parity - implied_volatility(K, T=1.0, r=None, q=0.0) — Black–Scholes implied volatility inversion - implied_vol_smile(strikes, T=1.0, r=None, q=0.0) — implied volatility smile curve

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None, method="full_truncation") — simulated paths of log-price \(X_t\) - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None, method="full_truncation") — coupled paths of \((X_t, V_t)\)

References: - Bates, D. S. (1996). Jumps and stochastic volatility: Exchange rate processes implicit in Deutsche Mark options. Review of Financial Studies, 9(1), 69–107. - Heston, S. L. (1993). A closed-form solution for options with stochastic volatility. Review of Financial Studies, 6(2), 327–343. - Albrecher, H., Mayer, P., Schoutens, W., & Tistaert, J. (2007). The little Heston trap. Wilmott Magazine, 83–92.

docs.title: BNSModel
docs.text:
from spxa import BNSModel, BNSProcess, BarndorffNielsenShephard, BNS

bns = BNSModel(
    lambda_param=1.5,
    alpha=2.0,
    beta_bdlp=25.0,
    rho=-0.50,
    beta=-0.50,
    sigma0_sq=0.04,
    s0=100.0,
    rate=0.05,
    dividend=0.01,
)

The Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (BNS, 2001) model couples non-Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic variance with asset price jump-diffusion dynamics: $\(dX_t = (\mu + \beta \sigma_t^2) dt + \sigma_t dW_t + \rho dZ_{\lambda t}, \quad S_t = S_0 \exp(X_t)\)$ $\(d\sigma_t^2 = -\lambda \sigma_t^2 dt + dZ_{\lambda t}, \quad \sigma_0^2 > 0\)$ where \(Z_t\) is a compound Poisson Background Driving Lévy Process (BDLP) with arrival rate \(\alpha\) and exponential jump size \(\beta_{bdlp}\).

Parameters & Structural Properties: - lambda_param (or lam) — variance mean-reversion rate \(\lambda > 0\) - alpha (or a) — BDLP Gamma shape parameter \(\alpha > 0\) - beta_bdlp (or b) — BDLP Gamma rate parameter \(\beta_{bdlp} > 0\) - rho — leverage parameter \(\rho \le 0\) - beta — drift risk parameter \(\beta\) (default \(-0.5\)) - sigma0_sq (or v0) — initial variance \(\sigma_0^2 > 0\) - s0 — initial asset price \(S_0 > 0\) - rate — risk-free rate \(r\) - dividend — dividend yield \(q\) - stationary_variance_mean — stationary variance \(\mathbb{E}[\sigma_\infty^2] = \frac{\alpha}{\beta_{bdlp}}\) - stationary_variance_variance — stationary variance of variance \(\frac{\alpha}{\beta_{bdlp}^2}\)

Distributional Analytics & Moments: - variance_mean(t=1.0) — conditional variance expectation \(\mathbb{E}[\sigma_t^2 \mid \sigma_0^2] = \sigma_0^2 e^{-\lambda t} + \frac{\alpha}{\beta_{bdlp}}(1 - e^{-\lambda t})\) - variance_variance(t=1.0) — conditional variance of variance \(\frac{\alpha}{\beta_{bdlp}^2}(1 - e^{-2\lambda t})\) - integrated_variance_mean(t=1.0) — conditional integrated variance expectation \(\mathbb{E}[\int_0^t \sigma_s^2 ds]\) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{i u \ln(S_t / S_0)}]\)

Option Pricing & Volatility Smile: - call_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0) — European call option price via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0) — European put option price via exact Put-Call parity - implied_volatility(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0) — Black-Scholes implied volatility

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — asset price paths \(S_t\) - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — coupled asset and variance paths (s_paths, var_paths)

References: - Barndorff-Nielsen, O. E., & Shephard, N. (2001). Non-Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-based models and some of their applications in financial economics. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 63(2), 167–241. - Nicolato, E., & Venardos, E. (2003). Option pricing in stochastic volatility models of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck type. Mathematical Finance, 13(4), 445–466.

docs.title: CEVProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import CEV, CEVProcess, ConstantElasticityOfVariance
# or from top-level:
from spxa import CEV, CEVProcess, ConstantElasticityOfVariance

CEVProcess(
    mu: float = 0.0,
    sigma: float = 0.2,
    gamma: float = 0.5,
    s0: float = 100.0,
    r: float | None = None,
    q: float = 0.0,
)

The Constant Elasticity of Variance (CEV) diffusion satisfies the SDE: $\(dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma S_t^\gamma dW_t, \quad S_0 = s_0 > 0\)$ where \(\mu \in \mathbb{R}\) is the drift rate (under risk-neutral pricing \(\mu = r - q\)), \(\sigma > 0\) is the volatility scale parameter, and \(\gamma \ge 0\) is the elasticity power exponent.

Structural properties - elasticity — constant elasticity of return variance \(2(\gamma - 1)\) - vol_elasticity — elasticity of return volatility \(\gamma - 1\) - is_absorbed_at_zero — True when \(\gamma < 1\) (the origin is an attainable absorbing boundary) - feller_condition — True when \(\gamma \ge 1\) (the origin is strictly inaccessible) - regime — "equity_leverage" (\(\gamma < 1\)), "geometric_brownian" (\(\gamma = 1\)), or "commodity" (\(\gamma > 1\))

Local Volatility & Default Probability - local_volatility(S: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray — local percentage volatility \(\sigma_{\text{loc}}(S) = \sigma S^{\gamma - 1}\) - absorption_probability(T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None) -> float — analytical default/bankruptcy probability \(P(S_T = 0) = 1 - F_{\chi^2}(x; 1/(1-\gamma))\) for \(\gamma < 1\); \(0.0\) for \(\gamma \ge 1\)

Exact Option Pricing (Schroder 1989 / Cox 1975) - call_price(K: float, T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None) -> float — exact European call price via non-central chi-squared distribution - put_price(K: float, T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None) -> float — exact European put price satisfying put-call parity \(C - P = S_0 e^{-q T} - K e^{-r T}\) - price(K: float, T: float, option_type: str = "call", r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None) -> float — unified option pricer

Greeks - delta(K: float, T: float, option_type: str = "call", r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None, eps: float = 1e-4) -> float — \(\partial V / \partial S_0\) satisfying \(\Delta_{\text{call}} - \Delta_{\text{put}} = e^{-q T}\) - gamma_greek(K: float, T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None, eps: float = 1e-4) -> float — \(\partial^2 V / \partial S_0^2 > 0\) - vega(K: float, T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None, eps: float = 1e-4) -> float — \(\partial V / \partial \sigma > 0\)

Distributions & Moments - transition_cdf(k: float, T: float, r: float | None = None, q: float | None = None) -> float — cumulative distribution function \(P(S_T \le k \mid S_0)\) - conditional_mean(t: float, s0: float | None = None) -> float — conditional expectation \(E[S_t \mid S_0] = S_0 e^{\mu t}\) - conditional_variance(t: float, s0: float | None = None) -> float — conditional variance \(\text{Var}(S_t \mid S_0)\) (closed-form for \(\gamma \in \{0.5, 1.0\}\), quadrature propagation for general \(\gamma\)) - conditional_std(t: float, s0: float | None = None) -> float — conditional standard deviation

Simulation - simulate(n_steps: int, dt: float | None = None, time_horizon: float | None = None, n_paths: int = 1, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None, method: str = "exact") -> np.ndarray — vectorized path simulation with absorbing boundary condition at 0

docs.title: CIRProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import CIRProcess, CoxIngersollRoss

CIRProcess(kappa: float, theta: float, sigma: float, r0: float | None = None)

Cox–Ingersoll–Ross (CIR) square-root diffusion process: $\(dr_t = \kappa(\theta - r_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{r_t} dW_t, \quad r_0 \ge 0\)$

Aliases: CIRProcess, CoxIngersollRoss.

Parameter Constraint Meaning Default kappa > 0 Speed of mean reversion \(\kappa\) required theta > 0 Long-term mean level \(\theta\) required sigma > 0 Volatility parameter \(\sigma\) required r0 \(\ge 0\) Initial spot value \(r_0\) theta

Exactness level: MOMENT_PROPAGATION (state-dependent diffusion \(\sigma\sqrt{r_t}\); no Lévy–Khintchine triplet).

Structural Properties: - feller_ratio: float (\(2\kappa\theta / \sigma^2\)) - feller_condition: bool (\(2\kappa\theta \ge \sigma^2\); strictly inaccessible zero boundary when True) - degrees_of_freedom: float (\(d = 4\kappa\theta / \sigma^2\)) - stationary_shape: float (\(\alpha = 2\kappa\theta / \sigma^2\)) - stationary_scale: float (\(\sigma^2 / (2\kappa)\)) - stationary_rate: float (\(2\kappa / \sigma^2\)) - stationary_mean: float (\(\theta\)) - stationary_variance: float (\(\theta\sigma^2 / (2\kappa)\)) - stationary_skewness: float (\(2 / \sqrt{\alpha}\)) - stationary_kurtosis: float (\(6 / \alpha\), excess kurtosis) - asymptotic_yield: float (\(2\kappa\theta / (\kappa + \sqrt{\kappa^2 + 2\sigma^2})\))

Analytical Methods: 

# Conditional expectation and variance at horizon t
cir.conditional_mean(t: float, r0: float | None = None) -> float
cir.conditional_variance(t: float, r0: float | None = None) -> float
cir.conditional_std(t: float, r0: float | None = None) -> float

# Exact conditional cumulants derived from non-central chi-squared law
cir.conditional_cumulant(n: int, t: float, r0: float | None = None) -> float
cir.conditional_cumulants(t: float, order: int = 4, r0: float | None = None) -> dict[int, float]

# Stationary cumulants (order n >= 1)
cir.stationary_cumulant(n: int) -> float
cir.cumulants(order: int) -> dict[int, float]

# Autocovariance and autocorrelation at lag h >= 0
cir.autocovariance(h: float) -> float    # Var(r_∞) * exp(-κh)
cir.autocorrelation(h: float) -> float   # exp(-κh)

# Laplace transform & Characteristic function
cir.laplace_transform(u: float, t: float, r0: float | None = None) -> float
cir.char_func(u: float | complex, t: float = 1.0, r0: float | None = None) -> complex

# Exact transition and stationary probability densities
cir.transition_density(y: float | np.ndarray, t: float, r0: float | None = None, s: float = 0.0) -> float | np.ndarray
cir.stationary_density(y: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray

# Zero-coupon discount bond pricing & term structure yield curve
cir.bond_price(tau: float | np.ndarray, r0: float | None = None) -> float | np.ndarray
cir.bond_yield(tau: float | np.ndarray, r0: float | None = None) -> float | np.ndarray

Simulation: 

cir.simulate(
    n_steps: int,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float = 1.0,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    method: str = "exact",
) -> np.ndarray
Supports three methods: 1. "exact" (default): exact non-central chi-squared increments via rng.noncentral_chisquare (zero discretization bias). 2. "truncated_euler": Higham–Mao full truncation Euler–Maruyama scheme. 3. "reflected_euler": Reflected Euler–Maruyama scheme.

Reference: Cox, Ingersoll & Ross (1985); Feller (1951).

docs.title: JCIRProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import JCIRProcess, JCIR, JumpCIRProcess, JCIRModel

jcir = JCIRProcess(
    kappa=1.2,
    theta=0.05,
    sigma=0.15,
    lambda_j=0.8,
    mu_j=0.03,
    r0=0.04,
)

The Jump-Extended Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (JCIR) process augments square-root diffusion dynamics with positive compound Poisson exponential jump shocks: $\(dr_t = \kappa (\theta - r_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{r_t} dW_t + dJ_t, \quad r_0 \ge 0\)$ where \(J_t = \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\) with \(N_t \sim \mathrm{Pois}(\lambda_J t)\) and \(Y_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\mu_J)\) with \(\mu_J > 0\).

Parameters & Structural Properties: - kappa — mean-reversion speed \(\kappa > 0\) - theta — diffusion long-term target \(\theta > 0\) - sigma — volatility-of-rate \(\sigma > 0\) - lambda_j (or jump_intensity) — jump arrival intensity \(\lambda_J \ge 0\) - mu_j (or jump_mean) — mean exponential jump size \(\mu_J > 0\) - r0 — initial short rate \(r_0 \ge 0\) - feller_ratio — baseline Feller ratio \(\frac{2\kappa\theta}{\sigma^2}\) - feller_satisfied — whether \(2\kappa\theta \ge \sigma^2\) - stationary_mean — long-term rate expectation \(\theta_\infty = \theta + \frac{\lambda_J \mu_J}{\kappa}\) - stationary_variance — long-term rate variance \(\frac{\sigma^2 \theta_\infty + 2 \lambda_J \mu_J^2}{2\kappa}\)

Conditional Moments & Analytics: - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(r_0 e^{-\kappa t} + \theta_\infty (1 - e^{-\kappa t})\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\frac{\sigma^2(r_0 - \theta_\infty)}{\kappa}(e^{-\kappa t} - e^{-2\kappa t}) + V_\infty (1 - e^{-2\kappa t})\) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — conditional characteristic function \(\phi(u; t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{i u r_t} \mid r_0]\)

Term Structure & Bond Pricing: - bond_price(tau, r=None) — closed-form zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, t+\tau) = \exp(A(\tau) - B(\tau) r_t)\) via Riccati system integration - yield_curve(tau, r=None) — continuously-compounded yield \(y(t, t+\tau) = -\frac{\ln P(\tau)}{\tau}\) - forward_rate(tau, r=None) — instantaneous forward rate \(f(t, t+\tau) = -\frac{\partial \ln P}{\partial \tau} = B'(\tau) r_t + \kappa \theta B(\tau) + \frac{\lambda_J \mu_J B(\tau)}{1 + \mu_J B(\tau)}\)

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact simulation combining non-central chi-squared CIR transitions with Poisson compound exponential jumps

References: - Duffie, D., & Garleanu, N. (2001). Risk and valuation of collateralized debt obligations. Financial Analysts Journal, 57(1), 41–59. - Maghsoodi, Y. (1996). Solution of the extended CIR term structure and bond option valuation. Mathematical Finance, 6(1), 89–109. - Brigo, D., & Mercurio, F. (2006). Interest Rate Models - Theory and Practice. Springer Finance.

docs.title: JacobiProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import JacobiProcess, JacobiDiffusion, WrightFisherDiffusion, Jacobi

jp = JacobiProcess(
    kappa=1.5,
    theta=0.4,
    sigma=0.5,
    y_min=0.0,
    y_max=1.0,
    y0=0.3,
)

The Jacobi diffusion (Wright-Fisher diffusion with mutation) is a bounded continuous diffusion on interval \([y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\) (canonical \([0, 1]\)): $\(dY_t = \kappa (\theta - Y_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{\frac{(Y_t - y_{\min})(y_{\max} - Y_t)}{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}} dW_t, \quad Y_0 = y_0 \in [y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\)$

Because diffusion vanishes at the boundaries \(y_{\min}\) and \(y_{\max}\), the process remains naturally bounded.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - kappa — mean-reversion speed \(\kappa > 0\) - theta — long-term target \(\theta \in [y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\) - sigma — diffusion volatility parameter \(\sigma > 0\) - y_min — lower boundary (default 0.0) - y_max — upper boundary (default 1.0) - y0 — initial state \(y_0 \in [y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\) - alpha — Beta stationary shape parameter at lower boundary \(\alpha = \frac{2\kappa (\theta - y_{\min})}{\sigma^2 (y_{\max} - y_{\min})}\) - beta — Beta stationary shape parameter at upper boundary \(\beta = \frac{2\kappa (y_{\max} - \theta)}{\sigma^2 (y_{\max} - y_{\min})}\) - boundary_classification_lower — "entrance" (\(\alpha \ge 1\)) or "instantaneously_reflecting" (\(\alpha < 1\)) - boundary_classification_upper — "entrance" (\(\beta \ge 1\)) or "instantaneously_reflecting" (\(\beta < 1\)) - stationary_mean — stationary expectation \(\theta\) - stationary_variance — stationary variance \((y_{\max} - y_{\min})^2 \frac{\theta_{norm}(1 - \theta_{norm})}{1 + 2\kappa/\sigma^2}\)

Polynomial Moments & Stationary Distribution: - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[Y_t \mid Y_0]\) - conditional_second_moment(t=1.0) — exact conditional second moment \(\mathbb{E}[Y_t^2 \mid Y_0]\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_t \mid Y_0)\) - stationary_density(y) — exact Beta stationary probability density function - stationary_cdf(y) — exact Beta stationary cumulative distribution function

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — high-order Milstein path simulation with strict boundary compliance

References: - Ackerer, D., Filipović, D., & Turnes, M. (2018). The Jacobi stochastic volatility model. Finance and Stochastics, 22(3), 667–700. - Karlin, S., & Taylor, H. M. (1981). A Second Course in Stochastic Processes. Academic Press. - Filipović, D., & Larsson, M. (2016). Polynomial diffusions and applications in finance. Finance and Stochastics, 20(4), 931–972.

docs.title: RegimeSwitchingGBM
docs.text:
from spxa import RegimeSwitchingGBM, RSGBM, RegimeSwitchingBlackScholes, MarkovSwitchingGBM

rs_gbm = RegimeSwitchingGBM(
    mu=[0.08, -0.04],
    sigma=[0.15, 0.35],
    transition_rates=[[-0.5, 0.5], [1.0, -1.0]],
    s0=100.0,
    initial_regime=0,
)

The continuous-time Markov-modulated Geometric Brownian Motion (Hamilton 1989; Naik 1993; Guo 2001) couples asset price dynamics with an unobserved or observed macro-economic regime: $\(dS_t = \mu(Y_t) S_t dt + \sigma(Y_t) S_t dW_t, \quad S_0 > 0\)$ where \(Y_t \in \{0, 1, \dots, K-1\}\) is a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) with generator matrix \(Q\).

Parameters & Structural Properties: - mu — sequence of regime drift rates \((\mu_0, \dots, \mu_{K-1})\) - sigma — sequence of regime volatilities \((\sigma_0, \dots, \sigma_{K-1})\), with \(\sigma_i > 0\) - transition_rates — \(K \times K\) CTMC generator matrix \(Q\) (rows sum to 0) - s0 — initial asset price \(S_0 > 0\) - initial_regime — initial Markov regime \(Y_0 \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}\) - n_regimes — number of states \(K\) - stationary_distribution — stationary probability vector \(\boldsymbol{\pi}\) satisfying \(\boldsymbol{\pi} Q = \mathbf{0}\)

Matrix Exponential Analytics & Option Pricing: - transition_probabilities(t=1.0) — exact transition probability matrix \(P(t) = \exp(Q t)\) - conditional_moment(n, t=1.0) — exact \(n\)-th moment \(\mathbb{E}[S_t^n \mid S_0, Y_0] = S_0^n \sum_j [\exp(M_n t)]_{ij}\) where \(M_n = Q + \mathrm{diag}(n\mu + \frac{1}{2}n(n-1)\sigma^2)\) - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[S_t \mid S_0, Y_0]\) - conditional_second_moment(t=1.0) — exact conditional second moment \(\mathbb{E}[S_t^2 \mid S_0, Y_0]\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\mathrm{Var}(S_t \mid S_0, Y_0)\) - conditional_std(t=1.0) — conditional standard deviation - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact continuous characteristic function \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u \ln(S_t / S_0)}]\) via matrix exponentials - call_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0, discount_rate=None) — European call option price via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0, discount_rate=None) — European put option price via Put-Call parity

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — sample paths of asset price \(S_t\) - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — coupled sample paths (spot_paths, regime_paths)

References: - Hamilton, J. D. (1989). A new approach to the economic analysis of nonstationary time series and the business cycle. Econometrica, 57(2), 357–384. - Naik, V. (1993). Option valuation and hedging in a regime switching framework. The Journal of Finance, 48(5), 1969–1997. - Guo, X. (2001). Information and option pricings. Quantitative Finance, 1(1), 38–44. - Elliott, R. J., Aggoun, L., & Moore, J. B. (1994). Hidden Markov Models: Estimation and Control. Springer-Verlag.

docs.title: ChenModel
docs.text:
from spxa import ChenModel, ChenThreeFactor, ChenShortRate, ChenProcess

model = ChenModel(
    k=1.5,
    theta_bar=0.05,
    kappa=0.8,
    alpha=0.04,
    zeta_bar=0.02,
    lambda_param=1.0,
    beta=0.05,
    r0=0.04,
)

The Chen (1996) Three-Factor Short Rate Model couples the instantaneous short rate with both a stochastic central tendency (stochastic mean) and stochastic variance: $\(dr_t = k (\theta_t - r_t) dt + \sqrt{\zeta_t r_t} dW_{1,t}\)$ $\(d\theta_t = \kappa (\bar{\theta} - \theta_t) dt + \alpha \sqrt{\theta_t} dW_{2,t}\)$ $\(d\zeta_t = \lambda (\bar{\zeta} - \zeta_t) dt + \beta \sqrt{\zeta_t} dW_{3,t}\)$

Parameters & Structural Properties: - k — mean-reversion speed of the short rate towards \(\theta_t\) (\(k > 0\)) - theta_bar — long-term central tendency target \(\bar{\theta} > 0\) - kappa — mean-reversion speed of central tendency (\(\kappa > 0\)) - alpha — volatility parameter of central tendency (\(\alpha > 0\)) - zeta_bar — long-term variance factor level \(\bar{\zeta} > 0\) - lambda_param — mean-reversion speed of variance factor (\(\lambda > 0\)) - beta — volatility parameter of variance factor (\(\beta > 0\)) - r0, theta0, zeta0 — initial states - feller_theta — boolean check for Feller condition \(2\kappa\bar{\theta} \ge \alpha^2\) - feller_zeta — boolean check for Feller condition \(2\lambda\bar{\zeta} \ge \beta^2\) - stationary_mean_short_rate — stationary expectation \(\bar{\theta}\) - stationary_mean_volatility — stationary variance factor \(\bar{\zeta}\)

Moments & Term Structure Analytics: - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[r_t \mid r_0, \theta_0]\) - conditional_mean_central_tendency(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[\theta_t \mid \theta_0]\) - conditional_mean_volatility(t=1.0) — exact conditional expectation \(\mathbb{E}[\zeta_t \mid \zeta_0]\) - conditional_moments_system(t=1.0) — exact 10-dimensional matrix exponential moment system - conditional_second_moment(t=1.0) — exact conditional second moment \(\mathbb{E}[r_t^2]\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\mathrm{Var}(r_t)\) - bond_price(maturity=1.0) — zero-coupon bond price \(P(0, T)\) - yield_curve(maturities) — term structure zero yields \(y(T) = -\frac{\ln P(0, T)}{T}\)

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — sample paths of the short rate \(r_t\) - simulate_factors(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — coupled paths (r_paths, theta_paths, zeta_paths)

References: - Chen, L. (1996). Stochastic Mean and Stochastic Volatility - A Three-Factor Model of the Term Structure of Interest Rates and Its Application in Derivatives Pricing. Financial Markets, Institutions & Instruments, 5(1), 1–88. - Chen, L. (1996). A Three-Factor Model of Interest Rates. The Journal of Fixed Income, 6(3), 8–29.

docs.title: CBISubordinator
docs.text:
from spxa import CBISubordinator, CBIProcess, DawsonWatanabeProcess, ContinuousStateBranching

cbi = CBISubordinator(
    a=0.05,
    b=0.8,
    c=0.1,
    lambda_j=0.4,
    eta=20.0,
    x0=0.1,
)

The Continuous-State Branching Process with Immigration (CBI) / Dawson-Watanabe process (Kawazu & Watanabe 1971; Dawson & Li 2012) evolves on \([0, \infty)\) according to: $\(dX_t = (a - b X_t) dt + \sqrt{c X_t} dW_t + dJ_t, \quad X_0 \ge 0\)$ where \(a \ge 0\) is continuous immigration, \(b \ge 0\) is branching drift (decay), \(c > 0\) is branching diffusion, and \(J_t\) is a compound Poisson jump immigration subordinator with arrival rate \(\lambda_J \ge 0\) and exponential jump size distribution \(\mathrm{Exp}(\eta)\).

Parameters & Structural Properties: - a — continuous immigration rate (\(a \ge 0\)) - b — branching drift (\(b \ge 0\), subcritical if \(b > 0\), critical if \(b = 0\)) - c — branching diffusion coefficient (\(c > 0\)) - lambda_j — jump immigration rate (\(\lambda_J \ge 0\)) - eta — jump parameter (\(\eta > 0\), mean jump \(1/\eta\)) - x0 — initial state (\(X_0 \ge 0\)) - is_subcritical — True if \(b > 0\) - is_critical — True if \(b = 0\) - stationary_mean — stationary expectation \((a + \mu_J)/b\) - stationary_variance — stationary variance \(\frac{(a + \mu_J)c}{2b^2} + \frac{\sigma_J^2}{2b}\)

Exact Laplace & Moments Analytics: - riccati_v(lam, t) — exact closed-form solution \(v(t, \lambda) = \frac{\lambda e^{-bt}}{1 + \frac{c\lambda}{2b}(1 - e^{-bt})}\) - laplace_transform(lam, t=1.0) — exact Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t} \mid X_0]\) - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact expectation \(\mathbb{E}[X_t \mid X_0]\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact variance \(\mathrm{Var}(X_t \mid X_0)\) - extinction_probability(t=1.0) — analytical extinction probability \(\mathbb{P}(X_t = 0 \mid X_0) = \exp(-\frac{2b X_0}{c(e^{bt}-1)})\) for pure CSBP (\(a = 0, \lambda_J = 0\)) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact characteristic function \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_t}]\)

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — high-order Milstein path simulation with non-negative reflection

References: - Kawazu, K., & Watanabe, S. (1971). Branching processes with immigration and related limit theorems. Theory of Probability & Its Applications, 16(1), 36–54. - Dawson, D. A., & Li, Z. (2012). Stochastic equations, flows and measure-valued processes. The Annals of Probability, 40(2), 813–857. - Li, Z. (2011). Measure-Valued Branching Markov Processes. Springer. - Grey, D. R. (1974). Asymptotic behaviour of continuous time, continuous state-space branching processes. Journal of Applied Probability, 11(4), 669–677.

docs.title: HullWhiteProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import HullWhiteProcess, HullWhite, HW1F, ExtendedVasicek

hw = HullWhiteProcess(
    a=0.10,
    sigma=0.015,
    b=0.035,
    r0=0.025,
)

The Hull-White (1990) one-factor short-rate model (extended Vasicek) follows the Gaussian SDE: $\(dr_t = a(b - r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad r_0 \in \mathbb{R}\)$ where \(a > 0\) is the mean-reversion speed, \(b \in \mathbb{R}\) is the long-term reversion level (\(\theta = a \cdot b\)), and \(\sigma > 0\) is the short-rate volatility.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - a (or kappa) — mean-reversion speed \(a > 0\) - sigma — short-rate volatility \(\sigma > 0\) - b — long-term target rate level \(b \in \mathbb{R}\) - theta — drift parameter \(\theta = a \cdot b\) - r0 — initial short rate \(r_0 \in \mathbb{R}\)

Moments & Distributional Analytics: - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — expected rate \(\mathbb{E}[r_t \mid r_0] = b + (r_0 - b) e^{-at}\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — variance \(\mathrm{Var}(r_t \mid r_0) = \frac{\sigma^2}{2a}(1 - e^{-2at})\) - conditional_std(t=1.0) — standard deviation \(\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(r_t \mid r_0)}\) - stationary_mean — long-term stationary mean \(b\) - stationary_variance — long-term stationary variance \(\frac{\sigma^2}{2a}\) - integrated_mean(t) — expected integrated short rate \(\mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^t r_s ds \mid r_0\right]\) - integrated_variance(t) — variance of integrated short rate \(\mathrm{Var}\left(\int_0^t r_s ds \mid r_0\right)\) - autocovariance(t, s) — short-rate autocovariance \(\mathrm{Cov}(r_t, r_s \mid r_0)\) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — Gaussian characteristic function - conditional_cumulants(t=1.0, order=4) — cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\)

Term Structure & Zero-Coupon Bond Pricing: - B(t, T) — affine bond pricing exponent \(B(t, T) = \frac{1 - e^{-a(T - t)}}{a}\) - A(t, T) — affine bond pricing scale factor \(A(t, T)\) - bond_price(T, r=None, t=0.0) — zero-coupon bond price \(P(t, T) = A(t, T) \exp(-B(t, T) r_t)\) - yield_to_maturity(T, r=None, t=0.0) — continuously compounded spot yield \(y(t, T) = -\frac{\ln P(t, T)}{T - t}\) - instantaneous_forward_rate(T, r=None, t=0.0) — forward rate \(f(t, T) = -\frac{\partial \ln P(t, T)}{\partial T}\)

Derivatives Pricing: - bond_call_price(T, S, K, r=None, t=0.0) — Jamshidian (1989) closed-form European call option on zero-coupon bond \(P(t, S)\) expiring at \(T\) - bond_put_price(T, S, K, r=None, t=0.0) — Jamshidian closed-form European put option on zero-coupon bond \(P(t, S)\) - caplet_price(T, strike_rate, tau=0.5, r=None, t=0.0) — European interest rate caplet - floorlet_price(T, strike_rate, tau=0.5, r=None, t=0.0) — European interest rate floorlet

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None, method="exact") — exact Gaussian conditional transitions with zero time discretization error

References: - Hull, J., & White, A. (1990). Pricing interest-rate-derivative securities. Review of Financial Studies, 3(4), 573–592. - Hull, J., & White, A. (1993). One-factor interest-rate models and the valuation of interest-rate derivative securities. Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, 28(2), 235–254. - Jamshidian, F. (1989). An exact bond option formula. The Journal of Finance, 44(1), 205–209. - Vasicek, O. (1977). An equilibrium characterization of the term structure. Journal of Financial Economics, 5(2), 177–188.

docs.title: BlackKarasinskiProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import BlackKarasinskiProcess, BlackKarasinski, BKProcess, BKModel

bk = BlackKarasinskiProcess(
    a=0.15,
    sigma=0.20,
    b=-3.35,
    r0=0.03,
)

The Black-Karasinski (1991) short-rate model represents interest rates with a lognormal diffusion: $\(d(\ln r_t) = a(b - \ln r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad r_t = \exp(x_t) > 0\)$ where \(a > 0\) is the mean-reversion speed, \(b = \ln(\bar{r})\) is the long-term log-rate reversion level, and \(\sigma > 0\) is the log-rate volatility. Because \(r_t = \exp(x_t)\), interest rates are strictly positive across all horizons.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - a (or kappa) — mean-reversion speed \(a > 0\) - sigma — log-rate volatility \(\sigma > 0\) - b — long-term target of \(\ln r_t\) - r0 — initial spot rate \(r_0 > 0\) - x0 — initial log-rate \(\ln(r_0)\)

Distributional Analytics & Moments: - log_rate_mean(t=1.0) — expected log-rate \(\mathbb{E}[\ln r_t \mid x_0] = b + (x_0 - b) e^{-at}\) - log_rate_variance(t=1.0) — variance of log-rate \(\mathrm{Var}(\ln r_t \mid x_0) = \frac{\sigma^2}{2a}(1 - e^{-2at})\) - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — expected short rate \(\mathbb{E}[r_t \mid r_0] = \exp\left(\mu_x(t) + \frac{1}{2} \sigma_x^2(t)\right)\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — variance of short rate \(\mathrm{Var}(r_t \mid r_0) = \exp(2\mu_x(t) + \sigma_x^2(t))(\exp(\sigma_x^2(t)) - 1)\) - stationary_median — asymptotic median short rate \(e^b\) - stationary_mean — asymptotic stationary mean \(\exp\left(b + \frac{\sigma^2}{4a}\right)\) - stationary_variance — asymptotic stationary variance

Term Structure & Bond Pricing: - bond_price(T, n_paths=15000) — zero-coupon bond price \(P(0, T) = \mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^T r_s ds\right)\right]\) via Monte Carlo - yield_to_maturity(T, n_paths=15000) — spot yield \(y(0, T) = -\frac{\ln P(0, T)}{T}\)

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact OU simulation for log-rate followed by exponentiation - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — returns (r_paths, x_paths)

References: - Black, F., & Karasinski, P. (1991). Bond and option pricing when short rates are lognormal. Financial Analysts Journal, 47(4), 52–59. - Brigo, D., & Mercurio, F. (2006). Interest Rate Models — Theory and Practice. Springer Finance.

docs.title: SABRProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import SABRProcess, SABRModel, SABR

sabr = SABRProcess(
    alpha=0.25,
    beta=0.50,
    nu=0.40,
    rho=-0.30,
    f0=100.0,
)

The SABR (Stochastic Alpha, Beta, Rho) stochastic volatility model (Hagan et al. 2002) is a benchmark for modeling interest rate and equity smile/skew dynamics under the forward measure: $\(dF_t = \alpha_t F_t^\beta dW_t^F, \quad F_0 = f_0 > 0\)$ $\(d\alpha_t = \nu \alpha_t dW_t^\alpha, \quad \alpha_0 = \alpha > 0\)$ $\(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^F dW_t^\alpha] = \rho dt\)$

Parameters & Structural Properties: - alpha — initial volatility scale \(\alpha > 0\) - beta — CEV elasticity exponent \(\beta \in [0, 1]\) - nu (or vol_of_vol) — volatility of volatility \(\nu \ge 0\) - rho — forward-volatility correlation \(\rho \in [-1, 1]\) - f0 — initial forward level \(F_0 > 0\) - backbone — smile backbone regime ("normal", "lognormal", or "cev")

Hagan et al. (2002) Asymptotic Implied Volatility: - implied_volatility(K, T=1.0) — Black-76 implied volatility \(\sigma_B(K, T)\) via the Hagan et al. closed form with Obłój corrections - atm_volatility(T=1.0) — At-the-money (ATM) Black implied volatility \(\sigma_B(f_0, T)\) - implied_vol_smile(strikes, T=1.0) — array of implied volatilities across strikes

Option Pricing: - call_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.0) — Black-76 European call option price \(C(K, T)\) - put_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.0) — Black-76 European put option price \(P(K, T)\) via exact Put-Call parity

Forward & Volatility Moments: - expected_forward(t=1.0) — \(\mathbb{E}[F_t] = f_0\) (martingale property) - volatility_mean(t=1.0) — expected volatility \(\mathbb{E}[\alpha_t] = \alpha\) - volatility_variance(t=1.0) — variance of volatility \(\mathrm{Var}(\alpha_t) = \alpha^2 (e^{\nu^2 t} - 1)\) - log_volatility_mean(t=1.0) — expected log-volatility \(\mathbb{E}[\ln \alpha_t] = \ln \alpha - \frac{1}{2}\nu^2 t\) - log_volatility_variance(t=1.0) — variance of log-volatility \(\mathrm{Var}(\ln \alpha_t) = \nu^2 t\)

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None, method="log_euler") — coupled simulation returning forward price paths - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None, method="log_euler") — returns tuple (f_paths, alpha_paths)

References: - Hagan, P. S., Kumar, D., Lesniewski, A. S., & Woodward, D. E. (2002). Managing smile risk. Wilmott Magazine, September, 84–108. - Obłój, J. (2008). Fine tune your smile: Correction to Hagan et al.. Wilmott Magazine, May, 82–86.

docs.title: FractionalBrownianMotion
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import FractionalBrownianMotion

FractionalBrownianMotion(H: float, sigma: float = 1.0)

Centred Gaussian process with covariance Cov(B^H_s, B^H_t) = σ²/2·(s^{2H} + t^{2H} − |s−t|^{2H}). Not a semimartingale for H ≠ 0.5. No Lévy–Khintchine triplet.

Parameter Constraint Meaning H ∈ (0, 1) Hurst index. H=0.5 → standard BM sigma > 0 Scale (std dev at t=1)

Extra methods: 

fbm.variance(t: float) -> float
# σ²·t^{2H}

fbm.covariance(s: float, t: float) -> float
# σ²/2·(s^{2H} + t^{2H} − |s−t|^{2H})

Properties: self_similarity_index=H; hurst_index=H; has_independent_increments=False for H≠0.5.

Simulation: Davies–Harte circulant embedding — exact in distribution, O(n log n).

Reference: Mandelbrot & Van Ness (1968).

docs.title: SemiMarkovProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import SemiMarkovProcess

SemiMarkovProcess(
    transition_matrix,
    holding_time_distributions=None,
    holding_time_parameters=None,
    *,
    transition_holding_time_distributions=None,
    initial_state=0,
)

Finite-state semi-Markov process with a row-stochastic transition matrix P. The next state is selected according to the transition probabilities, and the holding time follows a specified distribution.

Unlike a continuous-time Markov chain, a semi-Markov process supports non-exponential holding times. The holding-time distribution can depend on the current state or on the transition (i, j).

Parameter Constraint Meaning transition_matrix Square, row-stochastic Transition probability matrix P holding_time_distributions Optional State-dependent holding-time distributions holding_time_parameters Required with state-dependent distributions Parameters for the holding-time distributions transition_holding_time_distributions Alternative configuration Maps transition (i, j) to its holding-time distribution and parameters initial_state Valid state index Initial state; defaults to 0

The * means that transition_holding_time_distributions and initial_state must be passed as keyword arguments. The state-dependent arguments must be provided together. The state-dependent and transition-dependent configurations cannot be mixed.

Supported holding-time distributions are exponential (rate), Weibull (shape, scale), and Gamma (shape, scale). All distribution parameters must be strictly positive and finite.

Extra methods:

process.simulate_events(
    T: float = 1.0,
    *,
    rng=None,
    max_transitions: int = 1_000_000,
) -> SemiMarkovEvents

process.simulate(
    n_steps: int,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float = 1.0,
    rng=None,
) -> np.ndarray
  • simulate_events(T, ...) returns transition times, visited states (including the initial state), and the simulation horizon.
  • simulate(n_steps, n_paths, T, rng) returns state paths on an evenly spaced time grid, with shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1).
  • rng accepts a NumPy Generator for reproducible simulation.
  • Events occurring exactly at the simulation horizon are included.
  • max_transitions limits simulation work and may raise RuntimeError if another transition is required within the requested horizon after the limit is reached.

Properties: Simulation-only process. Does not provide analytical moments or a Lévy triplet. It is generally not a Lévy process or subordinator; an absorbing process starting at zero is a constant-zero subordinator.

docs.title: Reference: Pyke (1961), “Markov Renewal Processes: Definitions and Preliminary Properties,” The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 32(4), 1231–1242.
HawkesProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import HawkesProcess

HawkesProcess(mu: float, alpha: float, beta: float)

Self-exciting point process with conditional intensity λ(t) = μ + α·Σ_{t_i<t} exp(−β(t−t_i)). Requires subcriticality: α < β (α/β < 1).

Parameter Constraint Meaning mu > 0 Background intensity alpha > 0, < β Excitation amplitude beta > 0 Exponential decay rate

Extra properties (on the instance): 

hawkes.mean_intensity        # float: μ/(1−α/β)
hawkes.asymptotic_variance_rate  # float: λ̄·(1+α/β)/(1−α/β)²
hawkes.fano_factor           # float: (1+α/β)/(1−α/β)² — always ≥ 1

Simulation: Ogata's thinning algorithm.

Reference: Hawkes (1971); Hawkes & Oakes (1974); Ogata (1981).

docs.title: HestonProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import Heston, HestonProcess

heston = Heston(v0=0.04, kappa=2.0, theta=0.04, sigma_v=0.3, rho=-0.7, mu=0.05, s0=100.0)

Two-dimensional affine stochastic volatility model (Heston 1993) coupling asset log-return \(X_t = \ln(S_t / S_0)\) with a Cox–Ingersoll–Ross (CIR) variance diffusion:

\[dX_t = \left(\mu - \frac{1}{2} V_t\right) dt + \sqrt{V_t} \, dW_t^S, \quad X_0 = 0$$ $$dV_t = \kappa (\theta - V_t) dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} \, dW_t^V, \quad V_0 = v_0$$ $$d\langle W^S, W^V \rangle_t = \rho \, dt\] Parameter Constraint Meaning v0 > 0 Initial instantaneous variance \(V_0\) (e.g. \(0.04 \implies 20\%\) initial volatility) kappa > 0 Speed of mean reversion for variance \(\kappa\) theta > 0 Long-term mean variance level \(\theta\) sigma_v > 0 Volatility of variance (vol-of-vol) \(\sigma_v\) (alias: sigma, xi) rho \([-1, 1]\) Spot-vol correlation \(\rho\) (controls skewness / leverage effect) mu real, default 0.0 Continuous drift rate \(\mu\) of log-return (often \(r - q\)) s0 > 0, default 1.0 Initial spot asset price \(S_0\)

Exactness: MOMENT_PROPAGATION (affine characteristic function is known analytically; no Lévy triplet exists due to state-dependent stochastic variance).

Feller Condition & Variance Analytics: 

heston.feller_ratio                # 2κθ / σ_v²
heston.is_feller_satisfied         # True if 2κθ > σ_v² (variance strictly positive a.s.)
heston.variance_mean(t)            # E[V_t | V_0] = θ + (v0 - θ) e^{-κ t}
heston.variance_var(t)             # Var(V_t | V_0)
heston.stationary_variance_mean    # θ
heston.stationary_variance_var     # θ σ_v² / (2κ)
heston.expected_integrated_variance(t) # E[∫_0^t V_s ds] = θ t + (v0 - θ)(1 - e^{-κ t})/κ

Continuous Characteristic Function & Cumulants: 

# Evaluates E[exp(i u X_t)] via Albrecher et al. (2007) formulation (avoids branch-cut discontinuities)
heston.char_func(u, t=1.0)
heston.asset_char_func(u, t=1.0)   # E[exp(i u ln S_t)]

heston.conditional_mean(t=1.0)     # E[X_t] = μ t - ½ E[∫_0^t V_s ds]
heston.conditional_variance(t=1.0) # Var(X_t)
heston.conditional_cumulants(t=1.0, order=4) # κ_1, κ_2, κ_3, κ_4 (leverage skew & fat tails)

Option Pricing & Implied Volatility Surface: 

# European call & put pricing via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion
heston.call_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.05, q=0.0)
heston.put_price(K, T=1.0, r=0.05, q=0.0)

# Black-Scholes implied volatility inversion
heston.implied_volatility(K=100.0, T=1.0, r=0.05)
heston.implied_vol_smile(strikes=[80, 90, 100, 110, 120], T=1.0)

Simulation: 

# Full Truncation scheme (Lord et al. 2010) preserving variance non-negativity
paths_x = heston.simulate(n_steps=100, n_paths=1000, T=1.0)

# Joint asset price and variance simulation
s_paths, v_paths = heston.simulate_joint(n_steps=100, n_paths=1000, T=1.0)

References: - Heston, S. L. (1993). A closed-form solution for options with stochastic volatility with applications to bond and currency options. The Review of Financial Studies, 6(2), 327–343. - Albrecher, H., Mayer, P., Schoutens, W., & Tistaert, J. (2007). The little Heston trap. Wilmott Magazine, 83–92. - Lord, R., Koekkoek, R., & van Dijk, D. (2010). A comparison of biased simulation schemes for stochastic volatility models. Quantitative Finance, 10(2), 177–194.

docs.title: SchobelZhuProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import SchobelZhuProcess, SchobelZhu, SchobelZhuModel, SZModel

sz = SchobelZhuProcess(
    sigma0=0.20,
    kappa=1.50,
    theta=0.20,
    tau=0.30,
    rho=-0.50,
    s0=100.0,
    rate=0.04,
    dividend=0.01,
)

The Schöbel-Zhu (1999) stochastic volatility model models instantaneous volatility \(\sigma_t\) as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Gaussian diffusion rather than CIR variance: $\(dS_t = (r - q) S_t dt + \sigma_t S_t dW_t^S, \quad S_0 > 0\)$ $\(d\sigma_t = \kappa (\theta - \sigma_t) dt + \tau dW_t^\sigma, \quad \sigma_0 \in \mathbb{R}\)$ $\(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^S dW_t^\sigma] = \rho dt\)$

Because volatility is mean-reverting and Gaussian, instantaneous variance \(v_t = \sigma_t^2 \ge 0\) is guaranteed non-negative.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - sigma0 (or v0) — initial volatility \(\sigma_0 \in \mathbb{R}\) - kappa — mean-reversion speed \(\kappa > 0\) - theta — long-term volatility target \(\theta\) - tau — vol-of-vol \(\tau > 0\) - rho — spot-volatility correlation \(\rho \in [-1, 1]\) - s0 — initial asset price \(S_0 > 0\) - rate — risk-free rate \(r\) - dividend — continuous dividend yield \(q\)

Distributional Analytics & Moments: - volatility_mean(t=1.0) — expected volatility \(\mathbb{E}[\sigma_t] = \theta + (\sigma_0 - \theta) e^{-\kappa t}\) - volatility_variance(t=1.0) — variance of volatility \(\mathrm{Var}(\sigma_t) = \frac{\tau^2}{2\kappa}(1 - e^{-2\kappa t})\) - variance_mean(t=1.0) — expected instantaneous variance \(\mathbb{E}[\sigma_t^2]\) - variance_variance(t=1.0) — variance of instantaneous variance \(\mathrm{Var}(\sigma_t^2)\) - stationary_variance_mean — long-term variance \(\theta^2 + \frac{\tau^2}{2\kappa}\)

Option Pricing & Characteristic Function: - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact continuous characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\) - call_price(K, T=1.0) — European call option price via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion - put_price(K, T=1.0) — European put option price via Put-Call parity - implied_volatility(K, T=1.0) — Black-Scholes implied volatility

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — returns asset price paths \(S_t\) - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — returns coupled tuple (s_paths, sigma_paths)

References: - Schöbel, R., & Zhu, J. (1999). An analytic model for option pricing with lognormal and non-lognormal volatility processes. Review of Derivatives Research, 3(1), 5–31. - Lord, R., & Kahl, C. (2007). Complex logarithm and implementation of the Heston and Schöbel-Zhu models. Journal of Computational Finance.

docs.title: SchwartzTwoFactor
docs.text:
from spxa import SchwartzTwoFactor, Schwartz97, Schwartz2F, SchwartzTwoFactorModel

s2f = SchwartzTwoFactor(
    s0=20.0,
    delta0=0.05,
    kappa=1.2,
    alpha=0.08,
    sigma1=0.30,
    sigma2=0.20,
    rho=0.60,
    rate=0.05,
)

The Schwartz Two-Factor (1997) commodity pricing model describes spot commodity price \(S_t\) coupled with mean-reverting convenience yield \(\delta_t\): $\(dS_t = (r - \delta_t) S_t dt + \sigma_1 S_t dW_1^Q(t), \quad S_0 > 0\)$ $\(d\delta_t = \kappa (\hat{\alpha} - \delta_t) dt + \sigma_2 dW_2^Q(t), \quad \delta_0 \in \mathbb{R}\)$ $\(\mathbb{E}[dW_1^Q dW_2^Q] = \rho dt\)$

Because \((X_t = \ln S_t, \delta_t)\) is a joint bivariate Gaussian diffusion system, futures prices, moments, and European options possess exact closed-form analytics.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - s0 — initial commodity spot price \(S_0 > 0\) (default 20.0) - delta0 — initial convenience yield \(\delta_0 \in \mathbb{R}\) (default 0.05) - kappa — convenience yield mean-reversion speed \(\kappa > 0\) - alpha — physical long-term convenience yield target \(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\) - sigma1 — spot price volatility \(\sigma_1 > 0\) - sigma2 — convenience yield volatility \(\sigma_2 > 0\) - rho — correlation \(\rho \in [-1, 1]\) between spot and convenience yield shocks - rate — risk-free interest rate \(r\) - lambda_yield — market price of convenience yield risk \(\lambda\) - alpha_hat — risk-neutral convenience yield target \(\hat{\alpha} = \alpha - \lambda/\kappa\) - stationary_yield_mean — long-term convenience yield target \(\hat{\alpha}\) - stationary_yield_variance — stationary convenience yield variance \(\frac{\sigma_2^2}{2\kappa}\)

Distributional Analytics & Moments: - yield_mean(t=1.0) — conditional convenience yield expectation \(\mathbb{E}[\delta_t \mid \delta_0] = \delta_0 e^{-\kappa t} + \hat{\alpha}(1 - e^{-\kappa t})\) - yield_variance(t=1.0) — conditional convenience yield variance \(\frac{\sigma_2^2}{2\kappa}(1 - e^{-2\kappa t})\) - log_spot_mean(t=1.0) — conditional expectation of \(\ln S_t\) - log_spot_variance(t=1.0) — conditional variance of \(\ln S_t\) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{i u \ln S_t}]\)

Commodity Futures & European Options: - futures_price(tau, s=None, delta=None) — exact closed-form futures price \(F(S_t, \delta_t, \tau)\) via Schwartz (1997) eq. (12) - futures_curve(maturities) — term structure of commodity futures across maturities - call_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0) — closed-form European call option price via Black-76 - put_price(strike, time_to_maturity=1.0) — closed-form European put option price via Black-76 satisfying exact Put-Call parity

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — spot price sample paths \(S_t\) - simulate_joint(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — coupled spot and convenience yield paths (s_paths, yield_paths)

References: - Schwartz, E. S. (1997). The stochastic behavior of commodity prices: Implications for valuation and hedging. The Journal of Finance, 52(3), 923–973. - Bjerksund, P. (1991). Contingent claims evaluation when interest rates and convenience yields are stochastic. Working Paper, Norwegian School of Economics.

docs.title: G2PlusPlusProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import G2PlusPlusProcess, G2PlusPlus, TwoFactorHullWhite

p = G2PlusPlusProcess(a=0.1, b=0.05, sigma=0.015, eta=0.01, rho=-0.3, r0=0.03)

The Two-Factor Hull-White (G2++) short-rate model decomposes interest rates into two correlated Gaussian factors: $\(r(t) = x(t) + y(t) + \phi(t)\)$ $\(dx(t) = -a x(t) dt + \sigma dW_1(t), \quad dy(t) = -b y(t) dt + \eta dW_2(t), \quad d\langle W_1, W_2 \rangle_t = \rho dt\)$

Exact Analytics: - bond_price(t, T, x_t=0.0, y_t=0.0) — analytical zero-coupon bond price \(P(t, T)\) - bond_yield(t, T, x_t=0.0, y_t=0.0) — zero-coupon yield curve - european_call_bond_option(t, T, S, K, x_t=0.0, y_t=0.0) — closed-form Brigo-Mercurio European bond option price - factor_covariance(t) — exact bivariate Gaussian factor covariance matrix - simulate(t_grid, n_paths=1, rng=None, return_factors=False) — exact vectorized factor simulation

docs.title: ThreeHalvesProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import ThreeHalvesProcess, ThreeHalves, ThreeHalvesModel

p = ThreeHalvesProcess(kappa=2.0, theta=0.04, epsilon=1.0, v0=0.04)

The 3/2 Stochastic Volatility model features super-linear volatility-of-variance: $\(dv_t = \kappa v_t (\theta - v_t) dt + \epsilon v_t^{3/2} dW_t, \quad v_0 > 0\)$
