docs.title: SquaredBesselProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import SquaredBesselProcess, BESQ, SquaredBessel

besq = SquaredBesselProcess(dim=3.0, x0=1.0)

The Squared Bessel process of dimension \(\delta \ge 0\), denoted \(\mathrm{BESQ}^\delta(x_0)\), is defined by: $\(dX_t = \delta dt + 2 \sqrt{X_t} dW_t, \quad X_0 = x_0 \ge 0\)$

It is a fundamental building block of continuous-state branching processes, the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) interest rate model, Heston variance dynamics, and the constant elasticity of variance (CEV) model.

Parameters & Structural Properties: - dim (or delta) — dimension parameter \(\delta \ge 0\) (default 2.0) - x0 — initial state \(X_0 \ge 0\) (default 1.0) - index (or nu) — index \(\nu = \frac{\delta}{2} - 1\) - boundary_classification — Feller boundary classification at \(0\): "entrance" (\(\delta \ge 2\)), "instantaneously_reflecting" (\(0 < \delta < 2\)), "absorbing" (\(\delta = 0\))

Distributional Analytics & Moments: - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional mean \(\mathbb{E}[X_t \mid X_0] = x_0 + \delta t\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\mathrm{Var}(X_t \mid X_0) = 4 x_0 t + 2 \delta t^2\) - conditional_cumulants(t=1.0, order=4) — exact closed-form cumulants \(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4\) to order \(n\) - laplace_transform(lmbda, t=1.0) — exact Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t}] = (1 + 2\lambda t)^{-\delta/2} \exp\left(-\frac{\lambda x_0}{1 + 2\lambda t}\right)\) - char_func(u, t=1.0) — exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t) = (1 - 2 i u t)^{-\delta/2} \exp\left(\frac{i u x_0}{1 - 2 i u t}\right)\) - transition_density(y, t=1.0) — exact transition density via non-central \(\chi^2\) - transition_cdf(y, t=1.0) — exact cumulative distribution function

Simulation: - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact path simulation with zero time-discretization error via scaled non-central chi-squared increments \(\frac{X_{t+\Delta t}}{\Delta t} \sim \chi^2(\delta, \frac{X_t}{\Delta t})\)

docs.title: BesselProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import BesselProcess, BES, Bessel

bes = BesselProcess(dim=3.0, r0=1.0)

The Bessel process of dimension \(\delta \ge 0\), denoted \(\mathrm{BES}^\delta(r_0)\), is the square root of a Squared Bessel process: $\(R_t = \sqrt{X_t}, \quad X_t \sim \mathrm{BESQ}^\delta(r_0^2)\)$ $\(dR_t = \frac{\delta - 1}{2 R_t} dt + dW_t, \quad R_0 = r_0 \ge 0\)$

Parameters & Analytics: - dim (or delta) — dimension parameter \(\delta \ge 0\) - r0 — initial value \(R_0 \ge 0\) - conditional_mean(t=1.0) — exact conditional mean via confluent hypergeometric function \({}_1F_1\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\delta}{2}; -\frac{r_0^2}{2t}\right)\) - conditional_second_moment(t=1.0) — exact second moment \(\mathbb{E}[R_t^2] = r_0^2 + \delta t\) - conditional_variance(t=1.0) — exact conditional variance \(\mathbb{E}[R_t^2] - (\mathbb{E}[R_t])^2\) - simulate(n_steps=100, dt=None, time_horizon=None, n_paths=1, rng=None) — exact non-central chi simulation \(R_t = \sqrt{X_t}\)

References: - Feller, W. (1951). Two singular diffusion problems. Annals of Mathematics, 54(1), 173–182. - Pitman, J., & Yor, M. (1982). A decomposition of Bessel bridges. Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete, 59(4), 425–457. - Revuz, D., & Yor, M. (1999). Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion. Springer, Chapter XI.

docs.title: OrnsteinUhlenbeck
docs.text:
from spxa import OrnsteinUhlenbeck, Vasicek
from spxa.zoo.beyond import OrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess, VasicekProcess

# All four names refer to the same process class
ou = OrnsteinUhlenbeck(theta=1.5, mu=0.05, sigma=0.03, x0=0.02)

Continuous-time Gaussian mean-reverting diffusion (Uhlenbeck & Ornstein 1930; Vasicek 1977) governed by the stochastic differential equation:

\[dX_t = \theta(\mu - X_t) dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad X_0 = x_0\] Parameter Constraint Meaning theta > 0 Mean-reversion speed (\(\theta > 0\)) mu real Long-term mean / central tendency (\(\mu \in \mathbb{R}\)) sigma > 0 Volatility / diffusion coefficient (\(\sigma > 0\)) x0 real, default 0.0 Initial state value (\(X_0 = x_0\))

Exactness: MOMENT_PROPAGATION (conditional law is Gaussian; no Lévy triplet as increments are serially correlated).

Timescales & Stationarity: 

ou.relaxation_time         # float: τ = 1/θ
ou.half_life               # float: t_{1/2} = ln(2)/θ
ou.stationary_mean         # float: μ
ou.stationary_variance     # float: σ² / (2θ)
ou.stationary_std          # float: σ / sqrt(2θ)
ou.stationary_skewness     # float: 0.0
ou.stationary_kurtosis     # float: 0.0 (excess)
ou.stationary_cumulants(4) # dict[int, float]
ou.stationary_density(x)   # Gaussian probability density
ou.stationary_cdf(x)       # Gaussian cumulative distribution function

Conditional Distribution & Moments: 

ou.conditional_mean(t)     # E[X_t | X_0] = μ + (x_0 - μ) e^{-θ t}
ou.conditional_variance(t) # Var(X_t | X_0) = (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ t})
ou.conditional_std(t)      # sqrt(Var(X_t | X_0))
ou.conditional_cumulants(t, order=4)  # exact Gaussian cumulants
ou.transition_density(x, t)# N(mean(t), var(t)) PDF
ou.transition_cdf(x, t)    # N(mean(t), var(t)) CDF
ou.char_func(u, t)         # E[exp(i u X_t)] exact characteristic function
ou.laplace_transform(s, t) # E[exp(-s X_t)] exact Laplace transform

Temporal Correlation & Power Spectrum: 

ou.autocovariance(h)       # (σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ h}
ou.autocorrelation(h)      # e^{-θ h}
ou.covariance(s, t)        # (σ² / (2θ)) (e^{-θ|t-s|} - e^{-θ(t+s)})
ou.spectral_density(omega) # σ² / (π (θ² + ω²)) Lorentzian PSD

Vasicek Term Structure & Bond Pricing: 

ou.bond_price(tau)         # P(0, τ) = A(τ) exp(-B(τ) r_0)
ou.bond_yield(tau)         # y(0, τ) = -ln(P(0, τ)) / τ
ou.asymptotic_yield        # lim_{τ→∞} y(0, τ) = μ - σ² / (2θ²)

Simulation: 

# Exact Gaussian increments without time discretization bias (default)
paths = ou.simulate(n_steps=100, n_paths=1000, T=1.0, method="exact")

# Euler–Maruyama scheme
paths_euler = ou.simulate(n_steps=100, n_paths=1000, T=1.0, method="euler")

References: - Uhlenbeck, G. E., & Ornstein, L. S. (1930). On the theory of the Brownian motion. Physical Review, 36(5), 823. - Vasicek, O. (1977). An equilibrium characterisation of the term structure. Journal of Financial Economics, 5(2), 177–188.

from spxa.zoo.beyond import OULevy

OULevy(lam: float, subordinator: Process | None = None, v0: float = 0.0)

Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process driven by a Lévy subordinator: dV_t = −λV_t dt + dL_{λt}. Default subordinator: GammaProcess(a=1, b=1).

Parameter Constraint Meaning lam > 0 Mean reversion rate λ subordinator must be a subordinator Driving Lévy process L v0 ℝ Initial value V₀

Extra properties (on the instance):

ou.stationary_variance    # float: κ₂(L₁)/(2λ)

ou.autocovariance(h: float) -> float
# e^{−λh}·Var(V∞)   [Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2001, eq. 17]

Simulation: Exact Euler discretisation.

Reference: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2001).

docs.title: MarkovModulatedPoissonProcess
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.beyond import MarkovModulatedPoissonProcess

MarkovModulatedPoissonProcess(
    Q: ArrayLike,
    rates: ArrayLike,
    *,
    initial_state: int = 0,
    initial_probabilities: ArrayLike | None = None,
)

An N-state Markov-modulated Poisson counting process (MMPP). The background continuous-time Markov chain has generator matrix Q, and the Poisson arrival intensity depends on its current state: rates[J(t)].

The counting paths are non-decreasing, but increments are generally dependent. Therefore, a general MMPP is not a Lévy process and does not have a global Lévy triplet.

Parameters

Parameter Meaning Q Generator matrix of the background Markov chain. rates Non-negative arrival intensity for each background state. initial_state Initial background state; defaults to 0. initial_probabilities Optional probability vector specifying the initial distribution over background states.

The * in the constructor signature means that initial_state and initial_probabilities must be passed as keyword arguments.

Methods and properties

mmpp.count_moments(t: float) -> tuple[float, float]
mmpp.stationary_distribution() -> np.ndarray
mmpp.mean_intensity  # property; returns float

mmpp.simulate_events(
    T: float = 1.0,
    *,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    max_arrivals: int = 1_000_000,
    max_transitions: int = 1_000_000,
) -> MMPPResult

mmpp.simulate(
    n_steps: int,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float = 1.0,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
  • count_moments(t) returns the expected event count and variance at time t.
  • stationary_distribution() returns the stationary distribution of the background Markov chain.
  • mean_intensity returns the long-run arrival rate under the stationary distribution.
  • simulate_events(T, ...) returns arrival timestamps and background-state transition history. The max_arrivals and max_transitions arguments limit simulation work.
  • simulate(n_steps, n_paths, T, rng) returns counting paths sampled on an evenly spaced time grid, with shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1).

Process properties

The MMPP has has_stationary_increments=False, has_independent_increments=False, and is_subordinator=False.

Although its counting paths are non-decreasing, a general MMPP is not a Lévy subordinator because its increments are generally dependent. It is therefore not eligible to act as a subordination clock through the @ operator.

Reference: Fischer and Meier-Hellstern (1993), “The Markov-modulated Poisson process (MMPP) cookbook,” Performance Evaluation, 18, 149–171.

docs.title: MultivariateBrownianMotion
docs.text:
from spxa.zoo.multivariate import MultivariateBrownianMotion

MultivariateBrownianMotion(
    mu: np.ndarray | None = None,
    sigma: np.ndarray | None = None,
    dim: int = 2,
)

d-dimensional BM with drift μ and covariance matrix Σ. Simulation via Cholesky decomposition: ΔX = μ·Δt + L·Z·√Δt where L=chol(Σ).

Extra methods: 

mbm.covariance(t: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray   # t·Σ
mbm.correlation() -> np.ndarray                 # correlation matrix of X₁
mbm.multivariate_triplet() -> MultivariateLevyTriplet

Simulation: returns shape (n_paths, n_steps+1, dim).

docs.title: Copulas & Multi-Asset Dependence (spxa.copula)
docs.text: The spxa.copula module provides comprehensive multi-asset dependence modeling rooted in Sklar's Theorem (1959). It includes Fréchet–Hoeffding bounds, elliptical copulas, Archimedean copulas, extreme value copulas, arbitrary marginal process coupling via CoupledProcess, ML/CML parameter estimation, and 3D visualization routines.

docs.title: Copula Base Class
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import Copula

Abstract base class for all \(d\)-dimensional copulas on \([0, 1]^d\).

Core Methods: - cdf(u) — Joint cumulative distribution function \(C(u_1, \dots, u_d) = \mathbb{P}(U_1 \le u_1, \dots, U_d \le u_d)\). - pdf(u) — Copula density \(c(\boldsymbol{u}) = \frac{\partial^d C}{\partial u_1 \cdots \partial u_d}\). - log_pdf(u) — Log-density with numerical stabilization. - sample(n, rng=None) — Generate \(n\) independent random vectors from \([0, 1]^d\). - conditional_cdf(u_d, u_given) — Conditional distribution \(\mathbb{P}(U_d \le u_d \mid U_1 = u_1, \dots)\). - inverse_conditional_cdf(p, u_given) — Inverse conditional CDF for sequential sampling. - rosenblatt_transform(u) — Rosenblatt probability integral transform to independent uniforms. - inverse_rosenblatt_transform(w) — Exact inversion of Rosenblatt transform. - kendall_tau() — Exact or numerical Kendall's rank correlation \(\tau\). - spearman_rho() — Exact or numerical Spearman's rank correlation \(\rho_S\). - tail_dependence() — Lower and upper tail dependence coefficients \((\lambda_L, \lambda_U)\). - frechet_hoeffding_bounds(u) — Lower \(W(\boldsymbol{u})\) and upper \(M(\boldsymbol{u})\) Fréchet–Hoeffding bounds.

docs.title: Fundamental Fréchet–Hoeffding Copulas
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import (
    IndependenceCopula,
    ComonotonicityCopula,
    CountermonotonicityCopula,
)
  • IndependenceCopula(dim=2): Product copula \(\Pi(\boldsymbol{u}) = \prod_{i=1}^d u_i\). Represents mutually independent variables (\(\tau = 0, \rho_S = 0, \lambda_L = \lambda_U = 0\)).
  • ComonotonicityCopula(dim=2): Upper Fréchet–Hoeffding bound \(M(\boldsymbol{u}) = \min(u_1, \dots, u_d)\). Represents perfect positive co-movement (\(\tau = 1, \rho_S = 1, \lambda_L = \lambda_U = 1\)).
  • CountermonotonicityCopula(): Lower Fréchet–Hoeffding bound for \(d=2\): \(W(u_1, u_2) = \max(u_1 + u_2 - 1, 0)\). Represents perfect negative dependence (\(\tau = -1, \rho_S = -1, \lambda_L = \lambda_U = 0\)).

docs.title: Elliptical Copulas
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import GaussianCopula, StudentTCopula
  • GaussianCopula(corr=0.5, dim=2): $\(C( oldsymbol{u}) = \Phi_{ oldsymbol{\Sigma}}(\Phi^{-1}(u_1), \dots, \Phi^{-1}(u_d))\)$ Zero tail dependence \(\lambda_L = \lambda_U = 0\). Kendall's tau satisfies \( au = rac{2}{\pi} \arcsin( ho)\).
  • StudentTCopula(df=4.0, corr=0.5, dim=2): $\(C( oldsymbol{u}) = t_{ u, oldsymbol{\Sigma}}(t_ u^{-1}(u_1), \dots, t_ u^{-1}(u_d))\)$ Exhibits symmetric positive tail dependence: $\(\lambda_L = \lambda_U = 2 t_{ u + 1}\left(-\sqrt{ rac{( u + 1)(1 - ho)}{1 + ho}} ight) > 0\)$

docs.title: Archimedean Copulas
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import (
    ArchimedeanCopula,
    ClaytonCopula,
    GumbelCopula,
    FrankCopula,
    JoeCopula,
    AliMikhailHaqCopula,
)

Generated by continuous, strictly decreasing convex generator \(\psi(t)\): $\(C(\boldsymbol{u}) = \psi^{[-1]}\left(\sum_{i=1}^d \psi(u_i)\right)\)$

Copula Generator \(\psi(t)\) Parameter Range Tail Dependence \((\lambda_L, \lambda_U)\) ClaytonCopula \(\frac{1}{\theta}(t^{-\theta} - 1)\) \(\theta \in (0, \infty)\) \(\lambda_L = 2^{-1/\theta}, \lambda_U = 0\) GumbelCopula \((-\ln t)^\theta\) \(\theta \in [1, \infty)\) \(\lambda_L = 0, \lambda_U = 2 - 2^{1/\theta}\) FrankCopula \(-\ln\frac{e^{-\theta t} - 1}{e^{-\theta} - 1}\) \(\theta \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}\) \(\lambda_L = 0, \lambda_U = 0\) (radial symmetry) JoeCopula \(-\ln(1 - (1 - t)^\theta)\) \(\theta \in [1, \infty)\) \(\lambda_L = 0, \lambda_U = 2 - 2^{1/\theta}\) AliMikhailHaqCopula \(\ln\frac{1 - \theta(1 - t)}{t}\) \(\theta \in [-1, 1)\) \(\lambda_L = 0, \lambda_U = 0\)

docs.title: Extreme Value Copulas
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import (
    ExtremeValueCopula,
    GalambosCopula,
    HuslerReissCopula,
)

Max-stable copulas satisfying \(C(u_1^t, \dots, u_d^t) = C(\boldsymbol{u})^t\) characterized by the Pickands dependence function \(A(w)\): $\(C(u_1, u_2) = \exp\left( (\ln u_1 + \ln u_2) A\left(\frac{\ln u_2}{\ln u_1 + \ln u_2}\right) \right)\)$

  • GalambosCopula(theta=1.5): $\(A(w) = 1 - (w^{-\theta} + (1 - w)^{-\theta})^{-1/\theta}, \quad \lambda_U = 2^{-1/\theta}\)$
  • HuslerReissCopula(theta=1.5): $\(A(w) = w \Phi\left(\frac{1}{\theta} + \frac{\theta}{2} \ln\frac{w}{1-w}\right) + (1 - w) \Phi\left(\frac{1}{\theta} - \frac{\theta}{2} \ln\frac{w}{1-w}\right), \quad \lambda_U = 2 - 2\Phi(1/\theta)\)$

docs.title: CoupledProcess
docs.text:
from spxa import CoupledProcess, GeometricBrownianMotion, ClaytonCopula

s1 = GeometricBrownianMotion(drift=0.05, sigma=0.20, s0=100.0)
s2 = GeometricBrownianMotion(drift=0.03, sigma=0.25, s0=100.0)
coupled = CoupledProcess(processes=[s1, s2], copula=ClaytonCopula(theta=2.0))

Couples arbitrary 1D marginal Process instances through a copula using quantile coupling / copula subordination.

Methods: - simulate(t_max, num_steps, num_paths, seed) — Generates correlated multi-asset paths strictly preserving 1D marginal distributions. - basket_call_price(strike, maturity, weights=None, r=0.0, num_paths=20000) — Monte Carlo pricing of European basket options \((\sum w_i S_i(T) - K)^+\). - spread_option_price(strike, maturity, r=0.0, num_paths=20000) — European spread options \((S_1(T) - S_2(T) - K)^+\). - best_of_call_price(strike, maturity, r=0.0, num_paths=20000) — Rainbow best-of call \((\max(S_1, \dots) - K)^+\). - worst_of_call_price(strike, maturity, r=0.0, num_paths=20000) — Rainbow worst-of call \((\min(S_1, \dots) - K)^+\).

docs.title: Fitting & Model Selection
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import fit_copula, select_best_copula, pseudo_observations
  • pseudo_observations(data): Transforms continuous empirical multivariate observations \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}\) into uniform pseudo-observations on \([0, 1]^d\) via normalized empirical rank: $\(U_{ij} = \frac{\operatorname{rank}(X_{ij})}{n + 1}\)$
  • fit_copula(data, copula_cls, method="cml") -> Copula: Fits copula parameters via Canonical Maximum Likelihood (CML) or rank inversion ("itau", "irho").
  • select_best_copula(data, candidate_families=None) -> tuple[Copula, dict]: Evaluates candidate copula models, ranking by AIC / BIC and Log-Likelihood to identify the best-fitting dependence structure.

docs.title: Copula Visualizations
docs.text:
from spxa.copula import (
    plot_copula_cdf,
    plot_copula_pdf,
    plot_copula_samples,
    plot_tail_dependence_curves,
)
  • plot_copula_cdf(copula, ...) — Interactive 3D wireframe and surface plot of the copula distribution \(C(u_1, u_2)\).
  • plot_copula_pdf(copula, ...) — 3D density surface \(c(u_1, u_2)\) illustrating corner blow-ups and joint tail concentrations.
  • plot_copula_samples(copula, n_samples=1500, ...) — Scatter plot of copula pseudo-samples alongside joint marginal distributions.
  • plot_tail_dependence_curves(copulas, ...) — Lower \(\lambda_L(u) = C(u, u) / u\) and upper \(\lambda_U(u) = (1 - 2u + C(u, u)) / (1 - u)\) empirical tail concentration curves.

docs.title: addition
docs.text:
from spxa.ops import add, sum_processes, triplet_add, exactness_for_addition


add(X: Process, Y: Process) -> Process
Equivalent to X + Y. Returns a new process representing the sum of two independent processes. Triplet: (b_X+b_Y, σ²_X+σ²_Y, ν_X+ν_Y) when both EXACT.

sum_processes(processes: Iterable[Process]) -> Process
Sum of an iterable of independent processes. Raises ValueError if empty.

triplet_add(t1: LevyTriplet, t2: LevyTriplet) -> LevyTriplet
Add two triplets component-wise. Useful when constructing custom processes.

exactness_for_addition(X: Process, Y: Process) -> tuple[ExactnessLevel, str]
Determine the ExactnessLevel of X+Y and the reason if it degrades. Returns (level, reason) where reason is "" if no degradation.

docs.title: scaling
docs.text:
from spxa.ops import scale, negate, subtract, triplet_scale

scale(X: Process, c: float) -> Process       # c·X (c ≠ 0)
negate(X: Process) -> Process                # −X
subtract(X: Process, Y: Process) -> Process  # X − Y
triplet_scale(triplet: LevyTriplet, c: float) -> LevyTriplet

triplet_scale implements the exact image-measure formula: b_Z = c·b + drift_correction, σ²_Z = c²σ², ν_Z(B) = ν_X(B/c).

docs.title: subordination
docs.text:
from spxa.ops import subordinate, char_exp_subordinated, bernstein_function, is_valid_subordination


subordinate(parent: Process, subordinator: Process) -> Process
Equivalent to parent @ subordinator. Returns Z_t = X_{T_t}.

char_exp_subordinated(
    parent: Process,
    subordinator: Process,
    u: float | np.ndarray,
    t: float = 1.0,
) -> np.ndarray
Characteristic function of Z = X @ T using the composition formula ψ_Z(u) = −φ(−ψ_X(u)) where φ is the Laplace exponent of T.

bernstein_function(
    subordinator: Process,
    lam: float | np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray
Evaluate the Laplace exponent φ(s) = −log E[e^{−sT₁}]. Dispatches to a closed-form bernstein_function method on the process when available (GammaProcess, InverseGaussianProcess, TemperedStable), falling back to numerical evaluation via the characteristic function.

is_valid_subordination(parent: Process, subordinator: Process) -> tuple[bool, str]
Check validity. Returns (True, "") or (False, reason).

docs.title: product
docs.text:
from spxa.ops import multiply, ProductProcess, cumulants_to_raw_moments, raw_moments_to_cumulants


multiply(X: Process, Y: Process, max_moment_order: int = 4) -> ProductProcess
Product process Z_t = X_t·Y_t. Always MOMENT_PROPAGATION. Emits SpxaDegradationWarning. Moments computed via E[X^n·Y^n] = E[X^n]·E[Y^n] (independence).

cumulants_to_raw_moments(kappas: dict[int, float]) -> dict[int, float]
raw_moments_to_cumulants(moments: dict[int, float]) -> dict[int, float]
Exact conversion between cumulants and raw moments via the cumulant-moment recurrence (Stuart & Ord 1994). Roundtrip error < 1e-12.

ProductProcess exposes .cumulants(order) and .simulate(...).

docs.title: integral
docs.text:
from spxa.ops import ito_isometry_variance, stochastic_convolution_char_func, StochasticIntegral


ito_isometry_variance(
    integrator: Process,
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    t: float = 1.0,
    n_quad: int = 1000,
) -> float
Exact variance of ∫₀ᵗ f(s) dX_s via the Itô isometry: Var = κ₂(X₁)·∫₀ᵗ f(s)² ds. Valid for square-integrable Lévy martingale X and deterministic f. (Applebaum 2009, Theorem 4.2.3.)

stochastic_convolution_char_func(
    integrator: Process,
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    u: float | np.ndarray,
    t: float = 1.0,
    n_quad: int = 500,
) -> np.ndarray
Characteristic function of ∫₀ᵗ f(s) dX_s for deterministic f. Formula: E[exp(iu∫₀ᵗ f(s)dX_s)] = exp(∫₀ᵗ ψ_X(u·f(s)) ds). Requires EXACT integrator.

StochasticIntegral(X: Process, Y: Process, f: Callable[[float], float])
Process Z_t = ∫₀ᵗ f(X_s) dY_s for random integrand f(X_s). Always MOMENT_PROPAGATION. Emits SpxaDegradationWarning. Simulation via Euler–Maruyama: Z_{t_{k+1}} ≈ Z_{t_k} + f(X_{t_k})·ΔY_k.

docs.title: divergence
docs.text:
from spxa.analytics import (
    l2_char_func_distance,
    hellinger_distance,
    wasserstein2_distance,
    kl_divergence_mc,
)

All divergences compare marginal distributions at time t. No Monte Carlo needed for L² and Hellinger — they use characteristic functions directly.

l2_char_func_distance(
    X: Process, Y: Process,
    t: float = 1.0,
    u_max: float = 50.0,
    n_points: int = 2000,
) -> float
L² distance between marginals: (1/2π)·∫|φ_X(u;t) − φ_Y(u;t)|² du. Equal to 0 iff X_t and Y_t have the same distribution (Plancherel theorem). Symmetric.

hellinger_distance(
    X: Process, Y: Process,
    t: float = 1.0,
    u_max: float = 50.0,
    n_points: int = 2000,
) -> float
Squared Hellinger distance H²(X_t, Y_t) ∈ [0, 1]. H²=0 iff distributions identical; H²=1 iff mutually singular.

wasserstein2_distance(
    X: Process, Y: Process,
    t: float = 1.0,
    u_max: float = 100.0,
    n_points: int = 4000,
) -> float
Wasserstein-2 distance W₂(X_t, Y_t). Computed via Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion followed by quantile function comparison. Returns W₂ (not squared).

kl_divergence_mc(
    X: Process, Y: Process,
    t: float = 1.0,
    n_samples: int = 10000,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> float
Monte Carlo estimate of KL(X_t ‖ Y_t) via importance sampling. Approximate — density recovered by Gil-Pelaez inversion. Always ≥ 0.

docs.title: euler
docs.text:
from spxa.sim import euler_maruyama, euler_maruyama_autonomous, geometric_levy, convergence_order_estimate


euler_maruyama(
    driver: Process,
    drift: Callable[[float, float], float],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, float], float],
    z0: float = 0.0,
    T: float = 1.0,
    n_steps: int = 1000,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Euler–Maruyama for dZ_t = a(Z_t, t) dt + b(Z_t, t) dX_t. drift(z, t) and diffusion(z, t) are Python callables. Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps+1).

euler_maruyama_autonomous(
    driver: Process,
    drift: float,
    diffusion: float,
    z0: float = 0.0,
    T: float = 1.0,
    n_steps: int = 1000,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Vectorised Euler for constant-coefficient SDEs: dZ = a dt + b dX. Exact for constant coefficients (no discretisation error). Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps+1).

geometric_levy(
    driver: Process,
    mu: float,
    sigma: float,
    s0: float = 1.0,
    T: float = 1.0,
    n_steps: int = 1000,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Simulate S_t = s₀·exp(drift_correction·t + σ·X_t) where the drift correction is chosen so E[S_t] = s₀·e^{μt} (risk-neutral). Drift correction computed from the MGF via the characteristic function. Exact — no discretisation. Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps+1).

convergence_order_estimate(
    driver: Process,
    drift: Callable[[float, float], float],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, float], float],
    z0: float = 0.0,
    T: float = 1.0,
    n_paths_ref: int = 5000,
    step_sizes: tuple[int, ...] = (50, 100, 200, 400),
    rng_seed: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, object]
Empirical strong-convergence order via log-log regression against a fine-grid reference solution. Returns dict with keys: errors, dt_values, estimated_order, log_log_slope, step_sizes.

docs.title: bridge
docs.text:
from spxa.sim import (
    brownian_bridge, gamma_bridge,
    brownian_bridge_interpolate,
    first_passage_time_bm, first_passage_time_exact_bm,
)


brownian_bridge(
    t_start: float = 0.0,
    t_end: float = 1.0,
    x_start: float = 0.0,
    x_end: float = 0.0,
    sigma: float = 1.0,
    n_points: int = 100,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
Exact conditional BM bridge X(t) | X(t_start)=x_start, X(t_end)=x_end. Returns (time_grid, paths) with time_grid.shape=(n_points+2,) and paths.shape=(n_paths, n_points+2). Endpoint constraint is exact. Conditional mean at t: x_start + (x_end−x_start)·(t−t_start)/(t_end−t_start).

gamma_bridge(
    a: float,
    b: float,
    T: float = 1.0,
    x_end: float | None = None,
    n_points: int = 100,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
Gamma process bridge via the Beta distribution identity: G(t)|G(T)=g_T ~ g_T·Beta(at, a(T−t)). Returns (time_grid, paths). If x_end=None, samples g_T from Gamma(aT, b).

brownian_bridge_interpolate(
    coarse_paths: np.ndarray,
    coarse_times: np.ndarray,
    fine_times: np.ndarray,
    sigma: float = 1.0,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Refine coarse BM paths to a finer time grid by inserting bridge-sampled interior points. Coarse path values at coarse_times are preserved exactly. Returns shape (n_paths, len(fine_times)).

first_passage_time_bm(
    level: float,
    mu: float = 0.0,
    sigma: float = 1.0,
    T_max: float = 10.0,
    n_steps: int = 10000,
    n_paths: int = 1000,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Estimate first passage times τ = inf{t: X_t ≥ level} by simulation. Returns shape (n_paths,). Paths not reaching level by T_max return np.inf.

first_passage_time_exact_bm(
    level: float,
    sigma: float = 1.0,
    n_samples: int = 10000,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Exact samples from the first passage time distribution of BM(0, σ) to a positive level. Uses the Lévy distribution (one-sided stable, α=1/2): P(τ ≤ t) = 2Φ(−level/(σ√t)). Returns shape (n_samples,). Requires level > 0.

docs.title: milstein
docs.text:
from spxa.sim import milstein, milstein_autonomous, milstein_multivariate


milstein(
    drift: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion_prime: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray] | None = None,
    x0: float | Sequence[float] | np.ndarray = 0.0,
    dt: float | None = None,
    n_steps: int | None = None,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    eps: float = 1e-5,
) -> np.ndarray
Order 1.0 strong convergence Milstein scheme: $\(X_{k+1} = X_k + a(t_k, X_k)\Delta t + b(t_k, X_k)\Delta W_k + \frac{1}{2} b(t_k, X_k) b'(t_k, X_k) (\Delta W_k^2 - \Delta t)\)$ If diffusion_prime is omitted, evaluated automatically via centered finite differences with step eps. Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1).

milstein_multivariate(
    drift: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion_jacobian: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    x0: Sequence[float],
    dt: float | None = None,
    n_steps: int | None = None,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Multivariate commutative Milstein scheme for \(d\)-dimensional coupled SDEs driven by \(m\)-dimensional Brownian motion. Returns shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1, d).

docs.title: stochastic runge-kutta
docs.text:
from spxa.sim import stochastic_runge_kutta, srk_weak2


stochastic_runge_kutta(
    drift: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    x0: float | Sequence[float] | np.ndarray = 0.0,
    dt: float | None = None,
    n_steps: int | None = None,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Derivative-free order 1.0 strong Stochastic Runge-Kutta (SRK) scheme: $\(\Upsilon_k = X_k + a(t_k, X_k)\Delta t + b(t_k, X_k)\sqrt{\Delta t}\)$ $\(X_{k+1} = X_k + a(t_k, X_k)\Delta t + b(t_k, X_k)\Delta W_k + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\Delta t}} [b(t_k, \Upsilon_k) - b(t_k, X_k)] (\Delta W_k^2 - \Delta t)\)$ Achieves strong order 1.0 convergence without requiring analytical or numerical derivatives of \(b(t, x)\).

srk_weak2(
    drift: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    diffusion: Callable[[float, np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    x0: float | Sequence[float] | np.ndarray = 0.0,
    dt: float | None = None,
    n_steps: int | None = None,
    n_paths: int = 1,
    T: float | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
Weak order 2.0 Runge-Kutta scheme for computing expectations \(\mathbb{E}[f(X_T)]\) with larger step sizes.

from spxa.sim import (
    sample_qmc_uniforms,

sample_qmc_brownian(

    T: float = 1.0,

docs.title: variance reduction
docs.text:
from spxa.sim import (
    control_variate_estimate,
    sample_antithetic_normals,
    sample_antithetic_brownian,
    importance_sampling_gaussian_shift,
    stratified_uniform_1d,
)


control_variate_estimate(
    y: np.ndarray,
    x: np.ndarray,
    mean_x: float | Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
) -> ControlVariateResult
Optimal single and multivariate control variate estimator: $\(\hat{Y}_{\mathrm{CV}} = Y - \boldsymbol{\beta}^{* T} (X - \mathbb{E}[X]), \quad \boldsymbol{\beta}^* = \Sigma_{XX}^{-1} \Sigma_{XY}\)$ Returns ControlVariateResult with mean, std_err, beta, r_squared, and variance_reduction_ratio.

sample_antithetic_brownian(n_pairs: int, n_steps: int, T: float = 1.0) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
Generates mirrored pairs \((W, -W)\) of Brownian paths.

importance_sampling_gaussian_shift(
    n_samples: int,
    mu_shift: float | Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
Samples under shifted Gaussian drift \(\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}\) and returns Radon-Nikodym likelihood ratio weights \(L(Z) = \exp(-\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}^T Z + \frac{1}{2} \|\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}\|^2)\).

docs.text:
from spxa.sim import mlmc_estimate, MLMCResult


mlmc_estimate(
    path_coupler: Callable[[int, int, np.random.Generator], tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray | None]],

inspect_levy_triplet(process: Union[Process, LevyTriplet]) -> LevyInspection
Performs diagnostic analysis on the characteristic triplet \((b, \sigma^2, u)\): - Drift \(b\) and Gaussian diffusion variance \(\sigma^2\) - Activity classification: Finite activity (\(\int u(dx) < \infty\)) with total jump rate \(\lambda\), or Infinite activity (\( u(\mathbb{R}) = \infty\)) - Variation classification: Finite variation (\(\sigma^2 = 0\) and \(\int_{|x|\le 1} |x| u(dx) < \infty\)) vs Infinite variation - Blumenthal-Getoor index \( eta \in [0, 2]\) and singularity order \(s \ge 0\) near zero

docs.title: Stochastic Optimal Control (spxa.control)
docs.text: Continuous-time stochastic optimal control module supporting exact dynamic programming, Riccati ODE integrations, closed-form Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) verification, and monotone finite-difference viscosity solvers.

docs.title: ControlProblem
docs.text:
class ControlProblem(abc.ABC):
    def __init__(t_terminal: float = 1.0, discount_rate: float = 0.0)
Abstract base class for continuous-time stochastic optimal control problems: $\(V(t, x) = \inf_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \mathbb{E}\left[ \int_t^T e^{-\rho (s - t)} f(s, x_s, u_s) ds + e^{-\rho (T - t)} g(x_T) \;\Big|\; x_t = x \right]\)$

Methods: - optimal_control(t: float, x: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: State-feedback optimal control policy \(u^*(t, x)\). - value_function(t: float, x: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: Value function \(V(t, x)\). - running_cost(t: float, x: np.ndarray | float, u: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: Instantaneous running cost \(f(t, x, u)\). - terminal_cost(x: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: Terminal bequest / liquidation cost \(g(x)\). - drift(t: float, x: np.ndarray | float, u: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: Controlled drift rate \(\mu(t, x, u)\). - diffusion(t: float, x: np.ndarray | float, u: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float: Controlled diffusion rate \(\sigma(t, x, u)\). - simulate(x0, num_steps=100, num_paths=1000, seed=None) -> ControlledTrajectory: Monte Carlo forward simulation under optimal control.

docs.title: ControlledTrajectory
docs.text:
@dataclass
class ControlledTrajectory:
    times: np.ndarray         # Shape (n_steps + 1,)
    states: np.ndarray        # Shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1, dim_state)
    controls: np.ndarray      # Shape (n_paths, n_steps, dim_control)
    realized_costs: np.ndarray # Shape (n_paths,)
Container for simulated state-control paths, pathwise realized costs, and summary statistics (mean_cost, std_cost).

docs.title: LinearQuadraticGaussian (aliases: LQG, LinearQuadraticRegulator)
docs.text:
LinearQuadraticGaussian(
    a_matrix: np.ndarray,      # Drift matrix A, shape (d, d)
    b_matrix: np.ndarray,      # Control matrix B, shape (d, m)
    c_matrix: np.ndarray,      # Diffusion matrix C, shape (d, p)
    q_matrix: np.ndarray,      # State running penalty Q, shape (d, d)
    r_matrix: np.ndarray,      # Control penalty R, shape (m, m)
    m_terminal: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, # Terminal state penalty M, shape (d, d)
    t_terminal: float = 1.0,
    n_riccati_grid: int = 500,
)
Continuous-time multi-dimensional Linear-Quadratic-Gaussian regulator: $\(dx_t = (A x_t + B u_t) dt + C dW_t\)$ $\(\min_{u_t} \mathbb{E}\left[ \int_0^T (x_t^T Q x_t + u_t^T R u_t) dt + x_T^T M x_T \right]\)$

Features: - Solves backward continuous matrix differential Riccati ODE: $\(\frac{dP}{dt} + A^T P + P A - P B R^{-1} B^T P + Q = 0, \quad P(T) = M\)$ - Constant scalar offset ODE \(\dot{s}(t) + \operatorname{Tr}(C^T P(t) C) = 0, s(T) = 0\). - steady_state_riccati(): Continuous Algebraic Riccati Equation (CARE) solver for infinite-horizon regulation. - Optimal state feedback control: \(u^*(t, x) = - R^{-1} B^T P(t) x\). - Analytical quadratic value function: \(V(t, x) = x^T P(t) x + s(t)\).

docs.title: MertonPortfolioControl (aliases: MertonControl, MertonPortfolio, OptimalConsumptionInvestment)
docs.text:
MertonPortfolioControl(
    mu: float = 0.08,             # Risky asset drift mu > r
    sigma: float = 0.20,          # Risky asset volatility sigma > 0
    r: float = 0.03,              # Risk-free rate
    gamma: float = 2.0,           # Relative risk aversion gamma > 0, != 1
    rho: float = 0.05,            # Subjective discount rate rho > 0
    epsilon_bequest: float = 1.0, # Terminal bequest weight epsilon >= 0
    t_terminal: float = 5.0,
)
Merton lifetime optimal portfolio asset allocation and consumption under CRRA utility: $\(dW_t = [r W_t + \pi_t (\mu - r) - c_t] dt + \pi_t \sigma dW_t\)$ $\(\max_{\pi, c} \mathbb{E}\left[ \int_0^T e^{-\rho t} \frac{c_t^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma} dt + \epsilon e^{-\rho T} \frac{W_T^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma} \right]\)$

Exact Analytics: - Merton ratio: \(\alpha^* = \frac{\pi_t^*}{W_t} = \frac{\mu - r}{\gamma \sigma^2}\) (constant over time and wealth). - Optimal consumption propensity \(\kappa(t) = c_t^* / W_t = \frac{\nu}{1 + (\epsilon^{1/\gamma} \nu - 1) e^{-\nu (T - t)}}\). - Effective discount rate: \(\nu = \frac{\rho - (1 - \gamma)\left(r + \frac{(\mu - r)^2}{2\gamma \sigma^2}\right)}{\gamma}\). - Closed-form HJB value function: \(V(t, W) = h(t)^\gamma \frac{W^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma}\), where \(h(t) = 1 / \kappa(t)\). - Positive-preserving log-Euler Monte Carlo path simulator.

docs.title: AlmgrenChrissExecution (aliases: AlmgrenChriss, AlmgrenChrissModel, OptimalExecution)
docs.text:
AlmgrenChrissExecution(
    total_shares: float = 10000.0, # Initial order size Q_0
    t_terminal: float = 1.0,       # Execution time window T
    sigma: float = 0.30,           # Asset volatility sigma
    eta: float = 2.5e-4,           # Temporary impact coefficient eta > 0
    gamma_impact: float = 2.5e-5,  # Permanent impact coefficient gamma >= 0
    risk_aversion: float = 1e-3,   # Risk aversion lambda >= 0 (0 recovers TWAP)
    s0: float = 100.0,             # Spot price S_0
)
Continuous-time optimal execution of large blocks under temporary and permanent price impact: $\(dq_t = v_t dt, \quad dS_t = \gamma v_t dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad \tilde{S}_t = S_t + \eta v_t\)$ $\(\min_{v_t} \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{S}] + \lambda \operatorname{Var}[\mathcal{S}]\)$

Exact Analytics: - Urgency parameter: \(\kappa = \sqrt{\frac{\lambda \sigma^2}{\eta}}\). - Optimal inventory trajectory: \(q^*(t) = Q_0 \frac{\sinh(\kappa (T - t))}{\sinh(\kappa T)}\). - Optimal trading velocity: \(v^*(t) = -Q_0 \kappa \frac{\cosh(\kappa (T - t))}{\sinh(\kappa T)}\). - Analytical expected shortfall \(\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{S}]\) and shortfall variance \(\operatorname{Var}[\mathcal{S}]\). - efficient_frontier(n_points=50): Generates Pareto-optimal \((\sigma_{\mathcal{S}}, \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{S}])\) execution frontier.

docs.title: AvellanedaStoikovMarketMaker (aliases: AvellanedaStoikov, OptimalMarketMaking, HighFrequencyMarketMaker)
docs.text:
AvellanedaStoikovMarketMaker(
    t_terminal: float = 1.0,      # Trading session length
    sigma: float = 0.20,          # Mid-price volatility sigma
    gamma_risk: float = 0.1,      # Inventory risk penalty gamma > 0
    intensity_a: float = 140.0,   # Fill intensity scale A > 0
    intensity_k: float = 1.5,     # Order book liquidity decay k > 0
    max_inventory: int = 10,      # Inventory boundary capacity |q| <= Q_max
    s0: float = 100.0,
)
High-frequency limit order book quoting with inventory risk control: $\(dS_t = \sigma dW_t, \quad dq_t = dN^b_t - dN^a_t, \quad \lambda(\delta) = A e^{-k \delta}\)$

Exact Analytics: - Reservation price: \(R(s, q, t) = s - q \gamma \sigma^2 (T - t)\). - Optimal half-spreads: $\(\delta^a(q, t) = \frac{1}{\gamma} \ln\left(1 + \frac{\gamma}{k}\right) - \frac{2q - 1}{2} \gamma \sigma^2 (T - t)\)$ $\(\delta^b(q, t) = \frac{1}{\gamma} \ln\left(1 + \frac{\gamma}{k}\right) + \frac{2q + 1}{2} \gamma \sigma^2 (T - t)\)$ - Total optimal bid-ask spread: \(s^*(t) = \frac{2}{\gamma} \ln\left(1 + \frac{\gamma}{k}\right) + \gamma \sigma^2 (T - t)\) (invariant to inventory \(q\)). - Inventory skew: automatically shades bid/ask quotes downward when long (\(q > 0\)) to dump inventory. - Coupled jump-diffusion simulation generating Brownian mid-prices alongside Poisson limit order fills.

docs.title: FiniteDifferenceHJB (aliases: HJBSolver, HamiltonJacobiBellman, ViscosityHJBSolver)
docs.text:
FiniteDifferenceHJB(
    x_min: float = -2.0,
    x_max: float = 2.0,
    n_space: int = 101,
    t_terminal: float = 1.0,
    n_time: int = 100,
    discount_rate: float = 0.0,
    control_candidates: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None,
    mode: str = "minimize",       # 'minimize' or 'maximize'
    boundary: str = "neumann",    # 'neumann' or 'dirichlet'
)
Monotone, upwind finite-difference viscosity solver for general 1D nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDEs: $\(\partial_t V - \rho V + \inf_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \left\{ \mu(t, x, u) \partial_x V + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2(t, x, u) \partial_{xx} V + f(t, x, u) \right\} = 0, \quad V(T, x) = g(x)\)$

Features: - Guaranteed Barles-Souganidis convergence to the unique viscosity solution. - Directional upwind spatial differencing ensuring monotonicity (M-matrix discrete maximum principle). - Vectorized policy optimization over control set \(\mathcal{U}\). - Linear Neumann / Dirichlet boundary extrapolation. - solve(drift, diffusion, running_cost, terminal_cost) & solve_problem(problem) backward PDE integration. - Bivariate cubic spline interpolator value(t, x) and optimal feedback lookup optimal_control(t, x).

docs.title: Model Calibration & Estimation Suite (spxa.calibration)
docs.text: The spxa.calibration package provides institutional-grade cross-sectional implied volatility surface fitting, time-series econometric estimation (MLE, GMM, ECF), nonlinear latent state filtering (UKF, SMC), and diagnostic validation.

docs.title: Data Containers & Representations
docs.text:
• MarketQuote(strike, maturity, value, quote_type): Single option contract market quote (implied volatility or price), with optional bid/ask, vega, forward, and discount factors.
  • MarketSlice(maturity, strikes, quotes): Single expiration smile with vectorized interpolation and moneyness transformations.
  • MarketSurface(slices, spot, rate, dividend_yield): Multi-tenor volatility surface with grid projection, coordinate flattening (to_arrays()), and classmethod MarketSurface.from_quotes().

docs.title: Calibrators
docs.text:
• SABRCalibrator: Calibrates Hagan et al. (2002) asymptotic Black-76 implied volatility smile \((\alpha, \beta, \rho, \nu)\) with bounded optimization.
  • HestonCalibrator: Calibrates Heston (1993) semi-analytical Fourier call pricing engine \((v_0, \kappa, \theta, \sigma, \rho)\) with Feller condition violation regularization.
  • BatesCalibrator: Joint calibration of Heston stochastic volatility and Merton compound Poisson jumps \((v_0, \kappa, \theta, \sigma, \rho, \lambda_J, \mu_J, \sigma_J)\).
  • DoubleHestonCalibrator: Two-factor stochastic volatility calibration \((v_{0,1}, \kappa_1, \theta_1, \sigma_1, \rho_1, v_{0,2}, \kappa_2, \theta_2, \sigma_2, \rho_2)\) capturing both short-term skew and long-term smile curvature.
  • CEVHestonCalibrator: Local-stochastic volatility model calibration combining CEV backbone elasticity \(\gamma\) with Heston stochastic variance.

docs.title: Losses & Optimizers
docs.text:
• Loss functions: RMSELoss, VegaWeightedLoss, RelativeErrorLoss, ArbitragePenalizedLoss (penalizing calendar and butterfly arbitrage violations).
  • Optimization engines: LeastSquaresOptimizer (Levenberg-Marquardt / Trust-Region Reflective), DifferentialEvolutionOptimizer (global stochastic search), HybridOptimizer (global differential evolution followed by local polish).

docs.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimators
docs.text:
• OrnsteinUhlenbeckMLE (VasicekMLE): Analytical Gaussian exact conditional MLE for mean-reverting diffusions.
  • BrownianMotionMLE & GeometricBrownianMotionMLE: Analytical exact closed-form Gaussian log-likelihood estimators.
  • CIRMaximumLikelihood (CIRMLE): Exact transition density MLE based on non-central chi-square distribution \(\chi^2(d, \lambda)\) with Bessel-scaled modified Bessel functions \(I_\nu\).
  • BESQMaximumLikelihood (BESQMLE): Exact dimension and scale recovery from squared Bessel diffusion paths.
  • StudentTInnovationsMLE: Heavy-tailed log-likelihood optimization over \((\mu, \sigma, \nu)\) with \(t\)-distributed innovations.
  • NormalInverseGaussianMLE (NIGMLE): Exact MLE for generalized hyperbolic NIG distributions using modified Bessel functions \(K_1\).

docs.title: GMM & Spectral HAC
docs.text:
• GeneralizedMethodOfMoments (GMMEstimator, GMM): Two-step optimal GMM with iterative weighting matrix update.
  • newey_west_hac: Robust Newey-West (1987) Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent (HAC) spectral density matrix estimator with Bartlett kernel.
  • hansen_j_test: Hansen (1982) omnibus test of overidentifying moment restrictions: \(J = N \cdot g_N(\hat{\theta})^T W_N^* g_N(\hat{\theta}) \sim \chi^2(m - k)\).
  • OrnsteinUhlenbeckGMM & CIRGMM: Multi-moment conditional expectation estimators.
  • ECFEstimator: Empirical Characteristic Function estimator minimizing integrated continuum weighted distance between sample ECF \(\phi_N(u)\) and model CF \(\phi(u; \theta)\).

docs.title: Unscented Kalman Filter & SMC
docs.text:
• MerweScaledSigmaPoints: Scaled unscented transformation with parameters \(\alpha, \beta, \kappa\) preserving higher-order Gaussian kurtosis without negative covariance spread.
  • UnscentedKalmanFilter (UKF): Nonlinear state filtering propagating sigma points through arbitrary non-linear transitions and measurement functions with online innovation log-likelihood tracking.
  • QuasiMaximumLikelihoodEstimator (QMLE): Maximum likelihood calibration of underlying state-space parameters using UKF Gaussian innovation decomposition \(\sum_t [\ln |F_t| + v_t^T F_t^{-1} v_t]\).
  • Resampling algorithms: effective_sample_size, systematic_resample, stratified_resample, multinomial_resample.
  • BootstrapParticleFilter (ParticleFilter, SequentialMonteCarlo): Sequential Monte Carlo SIR particle filtering for general non-Gaussian/non-linear latent state spaces.

docs.title: Specialized Domain Filters
docs.text:
• HestonVarianceFilter: Log-variance state-space tracker recovering latent variance \(v_t = \exp(x_t) > 0\) from realized asset returns.
  • SchwartzTwoFactorFilter: Convenience yield filter tracking unobserved commodity convenience yield \(\delta_t\) and spot price \(S_t\) from futures term structures.
  • DefaultIntensityFilter: Credit default hazard rate filter estimating unobservable hazard rate \(\lambda_t\) from observed CDS spread curves.

docs.title: Statistical Inference & Information Criteria
docs.text:
• compute_numerical_hessian: High-precision central finite difference Hessian matrix.
  • fisher_information_matrix: Observed Fisher information \(\mathcal{I}(\hat{\theta}) = -\nabla^2 \ln L(\hat{\theta})\).
  • sandwich_covariance_matrix: Huber-White / Godambe sandwich covariance estimator \(V = H^{-1} J H^{-1}\).
  • compute_parameter_inference: Standard errors, \(t\)-statistics, two-tailed \(p\)-values, Wald 95% confidence intervals, and parameter correlation matrix.
  • Information criteria: akaike_information_criterion (AIC), corrected_aic (AICc), bayesian_information_criterion (BIC), hannan_quinn_criterion (HQIC), and ModelComparisonTable with relative Akaike evidence weights.

docs.title: Residual & Arbitrage Diagnostics
docs.text:
• compute_residual_diagnostics: Standardized residual diagnostics, Ljung-Box autocorrelation test, and Jarque-Bera normality test.
  • analyze_surface_residuals: Volatility surface goodness-of-fit (RMSE, MAE, MRE) alongside butterfly and calendar spread arbitrage violation counts.
  • compute_profile_likelihood: Profile likelihood analysis evaluating parameter identifiability and non-linear profile confidence intervals.
  • evaluate_pit_diagnostics: Probability Integral Transform (PIT) uniformity test and Berkowitz (2001) joint likelihood ratio test.
  • CalibrationReport: Institutional summary report generator exporting formatted ASCII text tables and GitHub-flavored Markdown tables.
  • Visualization helpers: plot_smile_overlay, plot_surface_error_heatmap, plot_filtered_trajectory.

docs.title: Computational Graph Engine (spxa.graph)
docs.text: A unified Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) representation of stochastic models supporting analytical evaluation, numerical quadrature, vectorized batch acceleration, Monte Carlo simulation, and exact reverse-mode automatic differentiation.

docs.title: ComputationalGraph, Compiler & Backends
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    ComputationalGraph,
    GraphCompiler,
    AnalyticalBackend,
    NumericalBackend,
    SimulationBackend,
    AcceleratedBackend,
    get_backend,
    ExecutionRouter,
)
  • ComputationalGraph(name="StochasticGraph"): Container for stochastic nodes, parameters, constants, operators, and output ports.
  • add_node(node): Registers a node.
  • add_output(node, name): Declares a terminal output port.
  • topological_sort(): Computes linear execution order via Kahn's algorithm with cycle detection.
  • evaluate(feed_dict=None, backend=None): Executes DAG in topological order.
  • prune(targets): Removes dead code and nodes not in the dependency path of targets.
  • GraphCompiler(graph): Optimization passes for graph simplification:
  • constant_folding(): Evaluates subgraphs of purely constant nodes at compile time.
  • common_subexpression_elimination(): Merges identical operator nodes with identical inputs.
  • algebraic_simplification(): Simplifies identities (\(x + 0 = x\), \(x \times 1 = x\), \(x \times 0 = 0\)).
  • optimize(): Runs full pipeline and returns an optimized DAG.
  • Backends:
  • AnalyticalBackend: Closed-form formulas and moments.
  • NumericalBackend: Carr-Madan, Lewis, and Cosine Fourier quadrature solvers.
  • SimulationBackend: Vectorized pathwise Monte Carlo sampling.
  • AcceleratedBackend: Vectorized batch evaluation across strike and maturity grids.

docs.title: Reverse-Mode Autodiff Tape & Greeks
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    GradientTape,
    compute_graph_greeks,
    compute_graph_hessian,
    SmoothIndicatorNode,
    SoftplusNode,
)
  • GradientTape: Context manager recording DAG execution and computing reverse-mode vector-Jacobian products (VJPs):
  • tape.gradient(target_output, sources=None): Computes exact gradients \(\nabla_x y\) via reverse-mode accumulation.
  • tape.jacobian(targets, sources): Computes full Jacobian matrix \(J_{ij} = \partial y_i / \partial x_j\).
  • compute_graph_greeks(pricing_graph, spot_node, vol_node, rate_node=None, mat_node=None): Computes exact Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Vega, Rho, Theta) in a single tape pass without finite-difference truncation error.
  • compute_graph_hessian(graph, target_node, param_nodes): Evaluates full second-order Hessian matrix including cross-sensitivities (Vanna, Volga).
  • Smoothers:
  • SmoothIndicatorNode(input_node, threshold, beta=20.0): Differentiable sigmoid mollifier \(\sigma(\beta(x - K))\) for discontinuous payoffs (digitals, barriers).
  • SoftplusNode(input_node, k=10.0): Smooth approximation to \(\max(x, 0) = \frac{1}{k}\ln(1 + e^{kx})\).

docs.title: Universal Zoo & Submodule Adapters
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    GraphAdapterRegistry,
    to_graph,
    as_graph_node,
    UniversalProcessNode,
    DifferentiableSDEAdapter,
    RiskInstrumentAdapter,
    adapt_portfolio,
    CalculusGeneratorAdapter,
    CopulaAdapter,
)
  • to_graph(obj): Universally converts any spxa.zoo process (all 198+ processes and algebraic compositions), spxa.risk instrument, spxa.diff SDE, spxa.copula copula, or spxa.calculus generator into native computational graph nodes.
  • UniversalProcessNode: Reflects any process parameters, char-func methods, and simulation samplers into mutable ParameterNode handles synchronized with the underlying process.
  • adapt_portfolio(portfolio, paths_node): Adapts multi-asset portfolios into an aggregated net present value (NPV) and sensitivity aggregation DAG.

docs.title: Deep Stochastic Operators & Semimartingale Wires
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    ItoTransformNode,
    GirsanovTransformNode,
    EsscherTransformNode,
    BochnerSubordinationNode,
    AutomatedCumulantNode,
    InfinitesimalGeneratorNode,
    MartingaleVerificationNode,
    ScaleDensityNode,
    SpeedDensityNode,
    FellerBoundaryClassifierNode,
    MalliavinBismutDeltaNode,
    SemimartingaleWire,
    SemimartingaleComponents,
    QuadraticCovariationNode,
    StochasticProductNode,
    StochasticIntegralNode,
)
  • SemimartingaleWire(x0, drift_fn, diffusion_fn, jump_intensity): Typed graph edge carrying semimartingale decomposition \(X_t = X_0 + A_t + M_t^c + J_t\).
  • QuadraticCovariationNode(wire_X, wire_Y): Computes pathwise bracket \([X, Y]_t\) and predictable covariation rate \(\langle X^c, Y^c \rangle_t\).
  • StochasticProductNode(wire_X, wire_Y): Evaluates stochastic integration by parts \(d(XY) = X dY + Y dX + d[X, Y]\) with machine-precision balance (\(\sim 10^{-15}\)).
  • StochasticIntegralNode(integrand_fn, integrator_wire): Evaluates predictable Itô integrals \((H \cdot X)_t = \int_0^t H_s dX_s\) satisfying Itô isometry.
  • ItoTransformNode: Automatically derives SDE dynamics for \(Y_t = f(t, X_t)\) via graph autodiff.
  • GirsanovTransformNode & EsscherTransformNode: Algebraic risk-neutral measure shifts.
  • BochnerSubordinationNode & AutomatedCumulantNode: Laplace-exponent subordination and central-difference cumulant extraction.
  • InfinitesimalGeneratorNode & MartingaleVerificationNode: Dynkin generator evaluation \(\mathcal{A}f(x)\) and martingale defect proof (\(\mathcal{A}f \equiv 0\)).
  • ScaleDensityNode, SpeedDensityNode, FellerBoundaryClassifierNode: 1D ergodic diffusions and Feller boundary classification (Regular, Exit, Entrance, Natural).
  • MalliavinBismutDeltaNode: Bismut pathwise Greek weights for discontinuous payoffs without payoff differentiation.

docs.title: Four-Facet Representation Duality Engine
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    ProcessDualityCore,
    SDEFacet,
    GeneratorFacet,
    FourierFacet,
    DensityFacet,
    compile_levy_khintchine,
    triplet_to_fourier_facet,
)
  • ProcessDualityCore(sde=None, generator=None, fourier=None, density=None): Container uniting the 4 dual representations of a stochastic process with bi-directional cross-facet synthesis (SDE \(\leftrightarrow\) Generator \(\leftrightarrow\) Speed/Scale density).
  • compile_levy_khintchine(b, sigma_sq, jump_measure_fn): Compiles an arbitrary triplet \((b, \sigma^2, \nu)\) into an executable characteristic exponent \(\Psi(u)\).

docs.title: Algebraic Process Surgery Operators
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    DoleansExponentialNode,
    StochasticLogarithmNode,
    TanakaDecompositionNode,
    DoobHTransformNode,
    StratonovichToItoNode,
    ItoToStratonovichNode,
)
  • DoleansExponentialNode: Stochastic exponential martingale \(\mathcal{E}(X)_t = \exp(X_t - \frac{1}{2}\langle X^c \rangle_t) \prod(1+\Delta X_s)e^{-\Delta X_s}\).
  • StochasticLogarithmNode: Continuous-time stochastic logarithm \(\mathcal{L}(Z)_t = \int \frac{dZ_s}{Z_{s-}}\).
  • TanakaDecompositionNode: Decomposes \((X_t - a)^+ = (X_0 - a)^+ + \int \mathbf{1}_{X>a} dX + \frac{1}{2}L_t^a(X)\), isolating pathwise continuous local time \(L_t^a(X) \ge 0\).
  • DoobHTransformNode: Excessive harmonic function conditioning: \(\mu^h = \mu + \sigma^2 \frac{h'}{h}\) (derives 3D Bessel process drift \(1/x\)).
  • StratonovichToItoNode & ItoToStratonovichNode: Conversions with midpoint Itô correction \(\pm \frac{1}{2}\sigma \sigma'\).

docs.title: Statistical Information Geometry (spxa.geom, spxa.graph.geom)
docs.text:
Riemannian differential geometry of parameter manifolds equipped with the Fisher Information Metric.

from spxa.geom import (
    FisherInformationMetric,
    AffineConnection,
    GeodesicFlow,
)
from spxa.graph.geom import (
    FisherInformationMetricNode,
    NaturalGradientCalibratorNode,
)

docs.title: Fisher Information Metric (FIM)
docs.text:
• FisherInformationMetric.gaussian_fisher(mu, sigma): Exact \(2 \times 2\) FIM for univariate Gaussians \(g = \text{diag}(1/\sigma^2, 2/\sigma^2)\).
  • FisherInformationMetric.ou_transition_fisher(x0, dt, theta, mu, sigma): Exact 3D transition FIM for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusions.
  • FisherInformationMetric.empirical_fisher(scores): Empirical score outer product covariance matrix \(\frac{1}{N}\sum s_k s_k^\top\).
  • FisherInformationMetric.numerical_hessian_fisher(neg_log_lik_fn, theta): Negative log-likelihood Hessian estimator.

docs.title: Connections & Christoffel Symbols
docs.text:
• AffineConnection(metric_fn, dim):
  • christoffel_symbols(theta): Levi-Civita Riemannian connection \(\Gamma^k_{ij}(\theta) = \frac{1}{2} g^{kl} (\partial_i g_{jl} + \partial_j g_{il} - \partial_l g_{ij})\).
  • amari_alpha_connection(theta, alpha, skewness_tensor): Amari \(\alpha\)-connection \(\Gamma^{(\alpha), k}_{ij} = \Gamma^k_{ij} - \frac{\alpha}{2} g^{kl} T_{ijl}\).
  • riemann_curvature_tensor(theta): Riemann curvature tensor \(R^l_{ijk}\).
  • ricci_scalar(theta): Ricci scalar curvature \(R = g^{ik} R_{ik}\).

docs.title: Riemannian Geodesic Shooting & Rao Distance
docs.text:
• GeodesicFlow(connection):
  • exponential_map(theta_0, v_0): Integrates geodesic ODE \(\ddot{\theta}^k + \Gamma^k_{ij} \dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j = 0\).
  • geodesic_shooting(theta_0, theta_1): Solves two-point boundary value problem.
  • rao_distance(theta_0, theta_1): Riemannian distance \(d_R = \int_0^1 \sqrt{g_{ij}\dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j} dt\).
  • gaussian_exact_rao_distance(p1, p2): Closed-form hyperbolic distance \(2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{arctanh}(\delta)\).

docs.title: Natural Gradient Manifold Calibration
docs.text: • NaturalGradientCalibratorNode(parameters, loss_fn, metric_fn, learning_rate): Riemannian natural gradient optimizer: $\(\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \eta g^{-1}(\theta_t) \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}(\theta_t)\)$ eliminating ill-conditioned parameter ravines.

docs.title: Rough Paths & Tensor Signatures (spxa.signature, spxa.graph.signature)
docs.text:
Pathwise, non-parametric representation of continuous and jump paths using Chen's iterated integrals and hyperbolic PDE kernels.

from spxa.signature import (
    PathSignature,
    SignatureAlgebra,
    SignatureKernel,
)
from spxa.graph.signature import (
    PathSignatureNode,
    SignatureKernelNode,
    ExpectedSignatureNode,
    SignatureLinearPricerNode,
)

docs.title: Truncated Path Signature & Chen Identity
docs.text:
• PathSignature(depth=3):
  • signature(path): Computes truncated signature \(S(X)_{0,T}^{(M)} = \bigoplus_{k=0}^M \int dX^{\otimes k}\) via piecewise-linear step integration.
  • flatten_signature(sig): Concatenates signature levels into a 1D feature vector of dimension \(\frac{d^{M+1}-1}{d-1}\).
  • verify_chen_identity(path, split_idx): Verifies Chen's multiplicative identity \(S(X)_{0,T} = S(X)_{0,t} \otimes S(X)_{t,T}\).

docs.title: Shuffle Algebra & Log-Signature Compression
docs.text:
• SignatureAlgebra.shuffles(u, v): Generates shuffle permutations \(u \sqcup v\) satisfying \(S^u \cdot S^v = \sum_{w \in u \sqcup v} S^w\).
  • SignatureAlgebra.log_signature_2d(sig, depth): Projects signatures onto the free Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{g}^{(M)}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) extracting the antisymmetric Lévy area \(A^{12} = \frac{1}{2}(S^{12} - S^{21})\) and Hall commutators.
  • SignatureAlgebra.log_signature_dimension(d, depth): Computes minimal Lie algebra dimension via Witt's formula \(L_d(k) = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{m|k}\mu(m) d^{k/m}\) (e.g. 66.7% dimension compression for 2D paths at depth 3).

docs.title: Signature Kernel via 2D Hyperbolic Goursat PDE
docs.text:
• SignatureKernel.solve_goursat_pde(path_x, path_y): Solves the 2D hyperbolic Goursat PDE \(\frac{\partial^2 K}{\partial s \partial t} = K(s, t) \langle \dot{X}_s, \dot{Y}_t \rangle\) with boundary conditions \(K(s, 0) = 1, K(0, t) = 1\).
  • SignatureKernel.evaluate(path_x, path_y): Computes infinite-order inner product \(\langle S(X), S(Y) \rangle\) in \(O(N_X \cdot N_Y)\) time without tensor truncation.
  • SignatureKernel.compute_gram_matrix(paths): Computes symmetric Gram matrix for path collections.
  • SignatureKernel.normalized_distance(path_x, path_y): Evaluates Hilbert space distance \(\|S(X) - S(Y)\|\).

docs.title: Universal Linear Pricing on Signatures
docs.text: • SignatureLinearPricerNode(depth=3): Prices arbitrary path-dependent payoffs by linear regression on expected signatures: $\(\text{Price} \approx \langle \mathbf{w}, \mathbb{E}[S(X)_{0,T}] \rangle\)$

docs.title: Rough Volatility & Volterra Calculus (spxa.rough, spxa.graph.rough)
docs.text:
Non-Markovian, sub-diffusive stochastic volatility models driven by fractional Brownian motion with Hurst exponent \(H < 1/2\).

from spxa.rough import (
    FractionalKernel,
    RoughBergomi,
    FractionalRiccatiSolver,
)
from spxa.graph.rough import (
    RoughKernelNode,
    RoughBergomiNode,
    FractionalRiccatiNode,
)

docs.title: Fractional Kernels & Hybrid Convolution
docs.text:
• FractionalKernel(hurst=0.1):
  • kernel_value(t): Riemann-Liouville power kernel \(K_H(t) = \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} t^{H - 1/2}\).
  • sample_fbm_cholesky(t_mat, n_steps, n_paths): Exact fractional Brownian motion simulation via Cholesky decomposition of covariance \(R_H(t, s) = \frac{1}{2}(t^{2H} + s^{2H} - |t - s|^{2H})\).
  • hybrid_convolution(dw, dt, b_cutoff=3): Bennedsen-Lunde-Pakkanen (2017) hybrid convolution scheme combining local analytical integration for \(s \approx t\) with FFT-accelerated regular tail convolution.

docs.title: Rough Bergomi (rBergomi) Model & Short-Time Skew
docs.text:
• RoughBergomi(hurst=0.1, eta=1.9, rho=-0.7, xi0=0.04, s0=100.0):
  • simulate_paths(t_mat, n_steps, n_paths): Simulates joint paths of spot \(S_t\) and instantaneous variance \(v_t = \xi_0 \exp(\eta\sqrt{2H} \tilde{W}_t^H - \frac{1}{2}\eta^2 t^{2H})\).
  • theoretical_short_time_skew(tau): Evaluates leading-order ATM implied volatility skew blow-up: $\(\left| \frac{\partial \sigma_{BS}}{\partial k} \right|_{k=0} \approx \frac{|\rho|\eta}{2} \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{H + 1/2} \tau^{H - 1/2}\)$

docs.title: Fractional Adams-Bashforth-Moulton Riccati Solver
docs.text:
• FractionalRiccatiSolver(hurst=0.1, lambda_param=1.0, rho=-0.7, nu=0.3):
  • solve(u, t_mat, n_steps): Fractional Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector solver for the non-local Volterra integral Riccati equation: $\(h(t) = \int_0^t \frac{(t-s)^{H-1/2}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} F(u, h(s)) ds\)$
  • rough_heston_char_func(u, t_mat, v0, theta): Evaluates Rough Heston characteristic function \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_T}]\) using fractional and standard integration of \(h(t)\).

docs.title: Model Morphing Framework (spxa.morph)
docs.text: The spxa.morph package provides a rigorous, first-class mathematical framework for continuous homotopies, information-geometric geodesics, optimal transport displacement interpolations, and dynamic transitions between stochastic processes.

docs.title: Core Morphing Abstractions (spxa.morph.base, spxa.morph.morphed_process)
docs.text:
• morph(p0, p1, alpha=0.5, method="triplet", coupling="independent", **kwargs): Functional operator morphing process \(P_0\) into \(P_1\) at homotopy parameter \(\alpha \in [0, 1]\). Also accessible via p0.morph(p1, alpha=alpha, method=method).
  • MorphMethod: Canonical enum of supported morphing schemes:
  • TRIPLET ("triplet", "characteristic"): Linear convex combination on the cone of conditionally positive-definite characteristic exponents \(\psi_\alpha(u) = (1 - \alpha)\psi_0(u) + \alpha\psi_1(u)\).
  • GENERATOR ("generator", "sde"): Infinitesimal generator homotopy \(\mathcal{A}_\alpha = (1 - \alpha)\mathcal{A}_0 + \alpha\mathcal{A}_1\).
  • GEODESIC ("geodesic", "fisher_rao"): Riemannian Fisher-Rao geodesic flow or Amari dual connections on statistical manifolds.
  • WASSERSTEIN ("wasserstein", "displacement"): McCann displacement interpolation along geodesics in \(\mathcal{W}_2\).
  • CONVEX_COMBINATION ("convex_combination", "pathwise"): Direct coupled pathwise simulation \(X_\alpha(t) = (1 - \alpha)X_0(t) + \alpha X_1(t)\).
  • SURFACE ("surface", "volatility_surface"): Total implied variance surface homotopy \(w_\alpha(k, T) = (1 - \alpha)w_0(k, T) + \alpha w_1(k, T)\).
  • MorphedProcess: First-class Process subclass representing the continuous homotopy \(P_\alpha\), carrying full property lattice tracking, exactness preservation, moment derivations, and path simulation.

docs.title: Characteristic Triplet Morphing (spxa.morph.triplet_morph)
docs.text:
• morph_triplets(triplet0, triplet1, alpha): Computes exact morphed Lévy triplet \((b_\alpha, \sigma_\alpha^2, u_\alpha)\) where \(b_\alpha = (1-\alpha)b_0 + \alpha b_1\), \(\sigma_\alpha^2 = (1-\alpha)\sigma_0^2 + \alpha\sigma_1^2\), and \( u_\alpha = (1-\alpha) u_0 + \alpha u_1\).
  • MorphedLevyMeasure(nu0, nu1, alpha): Exact mixture Lévy measure evaluating density, total mass, tails, and moments in closed form.
  • char_exp_morphed(p0, p1, alpha, u, t): Evaluates morphed characteristic function \(\mathbb{E}[e^{iu X_\alpha(t)}] = (\mathbb{E}[e^{iu X_0(t)}])^{1-\alpha} (\mathbb{E}[e^{iu X_1(t)}])^\alpha\).

docs.title: SDE & Infinitesimal Generator Homotopy (spxa.morph.generator_morph)
docs.text:
• GeneratorMorphEngine: Constructs morphed Markov diffusions governed by \(\mathcal{A}_\alpha = (1 - \alpha)\mathcal{A}_0 + \alpha\mathcal{A}_1\).
  • MorphedSDEDiffusion(p0, p1, alpha, x0=1.0, drift_mode="linear", diffusion_mode="quadratic"):
  • drift(t, x): \(\mu_\alpha(t, x) = (1 - \alpha)\mu_0(t, x) + \alpha \mu_1(t, x)\).
  • diffusion(t, x): Quadratic variance mode \(\sigma_\alpha(t, x) = \sqrt{(1-\alpha)\sigma_0^2(t, x) + \alpha\sigma_1^2(t, x)}\) or linear mode.
  • generator_action(f, df, d2f, t, x): Evaluates \((\mathcal{A}_\alpha f)(x) = \mu_\alpha f'(x) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma_\alpha^2 f''(x)\).
  • simulate(n_steps, n_paths, T, rng, scheme="euler"|"milstein"): High-order vector Euler-Maruyama and Milstein numerical discretization.

docs.title: Information-Geometric & Geodesic Morphing (spxa.morph.geodesic_morph)
docs.text:
• GeodesicMorphEngine: Morphing engine along Riemannian geodesics in statistical parameter manifolds.
  • gaussian_rao_distance(mu0, sigma0, mu1, sigma1): Exact Fisher-Rao hyperbolic distance \(d_R(\theta_0, \theta_1) = \sqrt{2}\ln((1+\delta)/(1-\delta))\) with \(\delta = \sqrt{ [(\Delta\mu)^2 + 2(\Delta\sigma)^2] / [(\Delta\mu)^2 + 2(\Sigma\sigma)^2] }\).
  • gaussian_geodesic_path(mu0, sigma0, mu1, sigma1, alpha): Exact circular arc Riemannian geodesic coordinates \((\mu(\alpha), \sigma(\alpha))\) on \(\mathbb{H}^2\).
  • GeodesicMorphedProcess(p0, p1, alpha, connection="riemannian"): Process whose parameters follow the Levi-Civita geodesic, Amari \(e\)-geodesic (natural coordinates), or \(m\)-geodesic (expectation coordinates).

docs.title: Optimal Transport & Wasserstein-2 Morphing (spxa.morph.wasserstein_morph)
docs.text:
• WassersteinMorphEngine: Optimal transport morphing engine using McCann displacement interpolation in \(\mathcal{W}_2\).
  • bures_wasserstein_distance(m0, cov0, m1, cov1): Exact 2-Wasserstein distance \(W_2^2 = \|m_0 - m_1\|^2 + \text{Tr}(\Sigma_0 + \Sigma_1 - 2(\Sigma_0^{1/2} \Sigma_1 \Sigma_0^{1/2})^{1/2})\).
  • gaussian_displacement_interpolation(m0, cov0, m1, cov1, alpha): McCann displacement interpolation \((m_\alpha, \Sigma_\alpha)\) using Brenier's optimal transport matrix \(A\).
  • WassersteinMorphedProcess(p0, p1, alpha): Process with exact linear quantile displacement \(F_\alpha^{-1}(p) = (1 - \alpha) F_0^{-1}(p) + \alpha F_1^{-1}(p)\).

docs.title: Dynamic Schedules & Stochastic Morphing (spxa.morph.dynamic_morph)
docs.text:
• LinearSchedule(t0=0.0, t1=1.0): Linear ramp \(\alpha(t) = \text{clip}((t - t_0)/(t_1 - t_0), 0, 1)\).
  • CosineSchedule(t0=0.0, t1=1.0): Cosine ramp \(\alpha(t) = \frac{1}{2}(1 - \cos(\pi \tau))\) with zero endpoint acceleration.
  • SmoothstepSchedule(t0=0.0, t1=1.0, order=1|2): Cubic Hermite (\(3\tau^2 - 2\tau^3\)) and quintic smootherstep (\(6\tau^5 - 15\tau^4 + 10\tau^3\)).
  • SigmoidalSchedule(t_mid=0.5, rate=10.0): Logistic transition schedule centered at \(t_{\text{mid}}\).
  • StateThresholdSchedule(x_crit, delta=0.1, direction=1): Endogenous barrier schedule \(\alpha(x)\) triggered when state penetrates critical threshold.
  • DynamicMorphedProcess(p0, p1, schedule, x0=1.0, stochastic_alpha=False, kappa_alpha=2.0, alpha_bar=0.5, sigma_alpha=0.2): Continuous process supporting deterministic schedules and stochastic Jacobi/Wright-Fisher diffusion morph trajectories: $\(d\alpha_t = \kappa(\bar{\alpha} - \alpha_t) dt + \sigma_\alpha \sqrt{\alpha_t (1 - \alpha_t)} dW_t^\alpha\)$

docs.title: Multi-Model Barycenters & Ensembles (spxa.morph.barycenter, spxa.morph.ensemble)
docs.text:
• ModelBarycenter(processes, weights=None, geometry="triplet"|"wasserstein"): Fréchet mean of a portfolio of models on probability simplex \(\mathbf{w} \in \Delta^K\).
  • bures_wasserstein_barycentric_cov(covariances, weights, max_iter=50, tol=1e-8): Iterative fixed-point solver for Bures-Wasserstein barycentric covariance \(\Sigma^* = \sum w_k (\Sigma^{*1/2} \Sigma_k \Sigma^{*1/2})^{1/2}\).
  • ModelEnsemble(models, weights=None, learning_rate=1.0): Adaptive ensemble supporting exponential Bayesian loss updates \(w_k \leftarrow w_k \exp(-\eta L_k)\) and mixture or barycentric path generation.

docs.title: Implied Volatility Surface Morphing (spxa.morph.surface_morph)
docs.text:
• SurfaceMorphEngine: Morphing engine for total implied variance surfaces \(w_\alpha(k, T) = (1 - \alpha)w_0(k, T) + \alpha w_1(k, T)\).
  • MorphedVolatilitySurface(vol_fn0, vol_fn1, alpha=0.5, spot=100.0, rate=0.0):
  • implied_vol(k, T): Evaluates morphed Black-Scholes implied volatility \(\sigma_\alpha(k, T) = \sqrt{w_\alpha(k, T)/T}\).
  • check_calendar_arbitrage(k, t_grid): Verifies monotonicity \(\partial_T w_\alpha(k, T) \ge 0\).
  • check_butterfly_arbitrage(k_grid, T): Verifies Durrleman-Gatheral condition \(g_\alpha(k, T) \ge 0\).
  • risk_neutral_density(strikes, T): Extracts Breeden-Litzenberger state price density \(q_\alpha(K) = e^{rT} \partial^2 C_\alpha / \partial K^2\).

docs.title: Computational Graph & Visualization (spxa.graph.morph, spxa.vis.morph)
docs.text:
• MorphNode(x, y, alpha): Computational graph node implementing homotopy \((1 - \alpha)x + \alpha y\) with reverse-mode VJP rule \(\partial L/\partial \alpha = (y - x) \cdot \partial L/\partial z\).
  • QuadraticVarianceMorphNode(sig0, sig1, alpha): Volatility diffusion node with gradient \(\partial \sigma / \partial \alpha = (\sigma_1^2 - \sigma_0^2)/(2\sigma)\).
  • plot_morph_density_evolution(p0, p1, alphas, x_range, t): Waterfall density evolution plot.
  • plot_morph_paths(morphed, n_paths, n_steps, T): Multi-path trajectory visualization.
  • plot_morph_surface(morphed_surface, k_grid, t_grid): 3D interactive implied volatility surface rendering.
  • plot_geodesic_phase_portrait(mu0, sig0, mu1, sig1): Phase-space hyperbolic Riemannian geodesic trajectory.

docs.title: PDE & PIDE Solvers (spxa.pde, spxa.graph.pde)
docs.text: Finite-difference solvers for pricing equations, transition densities and exponential Lévy PIDEs. Every scheme is covered by a convergence test against a closed form or a published reference. The theory is in PDE and PIDE methods. All objects below can be imported from spxa.pde, which is also available lazily as spxa.pde.

docs.title: Grids, Operators & Time Stepping
docs.text:
• Grid1D.uniform(lo, hi, n_nodes) and Grid1D.sinh(lo, hi, n_nodes, center, alpha=None, align_center=True, align=()): uniform grid, or sinh-stretched grid clustered at center. Points in align are placed exactly on nodes. Methods include refine(), locate(x) and interpolate(values, x).
  • TimeGrid.uniform(maturity, n_steps, event_taus=()) and TimeGrid.from_calendar_events(...): time grids in \(\tau = T - t\) that include event times.
  • Boundary conditions:
  • Dirichlet(value): \(u = g\).
  • Neumann(value): \(u_x = g\).
  • Linear(): \(u_{xx} = 0\).
  • Natural(): the equation itself, with one-sided derivatives.

Values can be scalars or functions of \(\tau\). - LinearPDE1D(...) and DiscreteOperator1D(pde, grid, left, right, convection_scheme="auto") (or "central", "upwind"): the equation \(u_\tau = a u_{xx} + b u_x + c u + f\) and its second-order discretisation. - ThetaSolver1D(operator, theta=0.5, rannacher_steps=2, rannacher_after_events=True): θ-scheme with Rannacher start-up. .solve(...) returns a ThetaResult. - Payoff(fn, kinks, name) with vanilla(K, option), digital(...) and asset_or_nothing(...). project_payoff(payoff, grid, method="average"|"kink"|"none") returns cell averages around kinks. - PDESolution1D stores nodal values and provides .value(s), .greeks(s) (value, delta, gamma, theta) and .__story__(). PDEPricingResult(price, delta, gamma, theta, spot, solution, vega, rho, exercise_boundary, method).

docs.title: Early Exercise
docs.text:
• Step-wise solvers for the linear complementarity problem:
  • PenaltyLCP(penalty=1e8, tol=1e-10, max_iter=100)
  • PSORLCP(omega=1.5, tol=1e-10, max_iter=20000)
  • BrennanSchwartzLCP(side="left")
  • IkonenToivanenLCP()

make_lcp(method, side="left") builds one by name. complementarity_residual(...) measures how well a solution satisfies the LCP. - ExerciseBoundary(taus, locations, side): the early-exercise boundary recorded during the solve.

docs.title: One-Factor Pricers
docs.text:
• BlackScholesPDE(r, sigma, q=0.0): sigma can be a constant or a local volatility sigma(S, t). Methods:
  • european(K, T, spot, option="call", bump_greeks=False, **kw)
  • american(K, T, spot, option="put", method="penalty", bump_greeks=False, **kw)
  • bermudan(K, T, spot, exercise_times, option="put", **kw)
  • digital(K, T, spot, option="call", cash=1.0, **kw)
  • barrier(K, T, spot, barrier, barrier_type="down-and-out", option="call", rebate=0.0, rebate_timing="hit", american=False, method="penalty", **kw)
  • double_barrier(K, T, spot, lower, upper, option="call", rebate=0.0, **kw)
  • discrete_barrier(K, T, spot, barrier, monitoring_times, barrier_type="down-and-out", option="call", rebate=0.0, **kw)

Keyword arguments (n_space, n_time, s_max, dividends=[DiscreteDividend(time, amount, proportional)], ...) are passed on to solve. - AsianPDE(r, sigma, q=0.0).price(K, T, spot, option="call", fixings=None, past_average=0.0, n_space=401, n_time=200, ...): Večeř's PDE for continuous or discrete arithmetic averages. .call(...) and .put(...) are shortcuts. - ShortRatePDE(kappa, theta, sigma, model="vasicek"|"cir"): methods zero_coupon_bond(T, r0, ...), coupon_bond(cashflows, r0, ...) and bond_option(K, T, S, r0, option="call", american=False, method="penalty", ...). - DupirePDE(r, sigma, q=0.0).solve(spot, T, maturities=None, n_space=401, n_time=200, k_max=None, ...): returns a DupireSurface of call prices over strike and maturity. Also local_vol_from_prices(strikes, maturities, prices, r, q=0.0) and implied_volatility(price, S, K, T, r, q=0.0, option="call", tol=1e-12).

docs.title: Generators, Densities & Lévy PIDEs
docs.text:
• to_pde(process, **kwargs) (also Process.to_pde()):
  • For a registered diffusion, returns a DiffusionPDE.
  • For an exponential Lévy model, returns LevyPIDE.from_process(process, r=..., q=...). This raises ValueError without r.
  • Raises NotImplementedError for unregistered processes.
  • FokkerPlanck1D(drift, volatility, grid, convection_scheme="auto", time_homogeneous=None).solve(initial, T, n_time=200, ...): returns a DensitySolution with .mass(), .mean(), .variance(), .expectation(g), .pdf(x) and .cdf(x). The discrete adjoint \(V^{-1}A^\top V\) conserves mass exactly.
  • LevyJumpOperator(density, h, max_jump): discretised jump integral with moment-matched small jumps. It exposes weights, intensity, compensator and apply(u, x, tau, far_left, far_right).
  • LevyPIDE(r, q, sigma, density, name="Levy"): constructors and methods from_process(process, r, q=0.0), european(K, T, spot, option="call", n_space=801, n_time=200, half_width=None, **kw) and american(K, T, spot, option="put", method="penalty", ...).

docs.title: Two-Factor ADI
docs.text:
• Grid2D(x, y): tensor grid with C-ordered unknowns, index i * ny + j.
  • Edge conditions Dirichlet2D(value), Neumann2D(value), Natural2D() and Linear2D(). A value can be a scalar or a function (coordinate along the edge, tau).
  • LinearPDE2D(axx, axy, ayy, bx, by, c, f, time_homogeneous=None): checks that \(a_{xx}, a_{yy} \ge 0\) and \(a_{xy}^2 \le 4a_{xx}a_{yy}\).
  • DiscreteOperator2D(pde, grid, edges, upwind="auto"|"none"): edges are given as {"x_lo", "x_hi", "y_lo", "y_hi"}. .split(tau) returns the matrices [A0, A1, A2] and sources [b0, b1, b2]. .apply(u, tau) applies the operator.
  • ADISolver(operator, scheme="hundsdorfer_verwer", theta=None, damping_steps=1): the scheme can be douglas, craig_sneyd, modified_craig_sneyd or hundsdorfer_verwer (aliases do, cs, mcs, hv). .solve(initial, T, n_time=100, obstacle=None, store_history=False, callback=None) returns an ADIResult. Passing an obstacle switches on the Ikonen–Toivanen splitting.
  • PDESolution2D: .value(x, y), .derivative(x, y, dx, dy) and .theta(x, y), using bicubic splines.
  • HestonPDE(r, kappa, theta, sigma, rho, q=0.0): methods european(K, T, spot, v0, option="call", n_s=101, n_v=51, n_time=100, scheme=..., s_max=None, v_max=None, damping_steps=1) and american(..., option="put"). Both return a HestonPDEResult with price, delta, gamma, theta, dv (\(u_v\)) and vega (\(2\sqrt{v_0}\,u_v\)), plus exercise_boundary for American options. Also from_process(heston_process, r, q=0.0) and the feller property.
  • TwoAssetBlackScholesPDE(r, sigma1, sigma2, rho, q1=0.0, q2=0.0): methods price(payoff, T, s1, s2, n1=101, n2=101, n_time=100, american=False, ...), exchange(T, s1, s2), spread(K, T, s1, s2, option), best_of(K, T, s1, s2) and worst_of(K, T, s1, s2). Each returns a TwoAssetPDEResult with delta and gamma tuples and cross_gamma.

docs.title: Monte Carlo, Risk & Graph Bridges
docs.text:
• longstaff_schwartz(paths, times, payoff, r, degree=3, basis="laguerre"|"monomial", regression_paths=None, scale=1.0, itm_only=True, side=None): returns an LSMResult with price, std_error, confidence_interval(), exercise_probability and boundary. Pass regression_paths for the two-pass, low-biased estimator.
  • gbm_paths(S0, r, sigma, T, n_steps, n_paths, q=0.0, seed=None, antithetic=True) generates exact GBM paths. lsm_american(K, T, spot, r, sigma, q=0.0, option="put", n_dates=50, n_paths=100_000, degree=3, basis="laguerre", seed=0, two_pass=True) prices an American vanilla with LSM.
  • pde_price(instrument, market, vega=False, vol_bump=1e-3, **solver_options): prices spxa.risk instruments: EuropeanOption, BarrierOption, AsianOption and two-asset BasketOption. The market dictionary holds spot, <id>_VOL, <id>_DIV and r. It returns a notional-scaled PDEQuote. pde_pricing_fn(book, **kw) returns a market -> value callable for StressTestingEngine. supported_instruments() lists the accepted types.
  • spxa.graph.pde.bs_pde_price_node(spot, volatility, rate, *, strike, maturity, option="call", style="european"|"american", dividend=0.0, **solver_options) and heston_pde_price_node(spot, v0, kappa, theta, sigma, rho, rate, *, strike, maturity, ...): OperatorNodes whose vector–Jacobian products use the grid Greeks (spot, \(v_0\)) and bumps for the other inputs.

docs.title: Verification & References
docs.text:
• convergence_study(solver, levels, reference=None, ratio=2.0, order=2.0) returns a ConvergenceStudy (errors, observed orders, Richardson value). Also available: observed_order(errors, ratio=2.0), observed_order_from_values(...) and richardson_extrapolate(coarse, fine, ratio=2.0, order=2.0).
  • spxa.pde.reference: closed forms used by the tests:
  • Black–Scholes: bs_price, bs_greeks, bs_digital_price, bs_asset_or_nothing_price.
  • Barriers: barrier_price (Reiner–Rubinstein), double_barrier_price.
  • Trees and American bounds: binomial_price (CRR/Leisen–Reimer), perpetual_american_put, perpetual_put_boundary.
  • Fourier: lewis_call_price with bs_cf, heston_cf and levy_cf.
  • Jumps: merton_price.
  • Short rate: vasicek_bond, vasicek_bond_option, cir_bond, cir_bond_option.
