  • Two assets: margrabe_price, spread_option_price.

docs.title: Market Conventions (spxa.market)
docs.text: Dates, accrual conventions, calendars, schedules, curves, option formulas, implied volatility and quote handling shared by spxa.rates and spxa.vol. The theory is in Market conventions. Dates may be datetime.date, datetime.datetime, ISO strings or numpy.datetime64.

docs.title: Dates, Day Counts & Calendars
docs.text:
• to_date(value), add_months(d, months, end_of_month_rule=False), add_tenor(d, tenor, end_of_month_rule=False), end_of_month(d), is_end_of_month(d), days_between(start, end), is_leap_year(year), days_in_month(year, month), days_in_year(year).
  • Tenor(spec): parses "3M", "1Y6M", "2W", "10D"; supports negation, integer multiples, equality and .months (month-based tenors) / .days (day- and week-based tenors).
  • DayCount(name) with .year_fraction(start, end, **kw) and .day_count(start, end). Conventions: ACT/360, ACT/365F, ACT/ACT ISDA, ACT/ACT ICMA (keywords ref_start, ref_end, frequency), 30/360 (Bond Basis), 30/360 US, 30E/360, 30E/360 ISDA (keyword termination), BUS/252 (keyword calendar). Functional forms year_fraction(start, end, convention, **kw) and day_count(...); available_day_counts().
  • Calendar(name="WEEKENDS", extra_holidays=(), extra_business_days=()) for TARGET, US-FED, US-SIFMA (SOFR), UK and WEEKENDS. Methods: is_business_day, is_holiday, holidays(start, end), business_days_between(start, end), next_business_day, previous_business_day, add_business_days(d, n), with_holidays(...), with_business_days(...). JointCalendar(calendars, rule="holiday_if_any"|"holiday_if_all"), get_calendar(spec) (a name, a calendar or a list for a joint calendar), available_calendars() and easter_sunday(year).

docs.title: Schedules
docs.text:
• adjust(d, calendar="WEEKENDS", convention="MF"): conventions F, MF, P, MP, U (long names accepted); available_business_day_conventions().
  • Schedule(effective, termination, tenor="6M", calendar="WEEKENDS", convention="MF", termination_convention=None, stub="short_front", end_of_month=False, first_date=None, next_to_last_date=None): stubs short_front, long_front, short_back, long_back. It is a sequence of adjusted dates with .periods() (a list of AccrualPeriod holding adjusted, unadjusted and reference dates), .year_fractions(day_count), .is_regular() and .frequency.

docs.title: Curves & Equity Forwards
docs.text:
• discount_from_rate(rate, t, compounding="continuous") and rate_from_discount(df, t, compounding): compounding "continuous", "simple" or a frequency per year.
  • YieldCurve (abstract): discount(t), zero_rate(t, compounding), forward_rate(t1, t2, compounding="simple"), instantaneous_forward(t) and shifted(spread). Times are year fractions or dates (with reference_date).
  • FlatCurve(rate, compounding="continuous", reference_date=None, day_count="ACT/365F") and InterpolatedDiscountCurve(times, discounts, ...) (log-linear).
  • Dividend(time, amount, kind="cash"|"proportional") and EquityForward(spot, discount, dividend_yield=None, repo=None, dividends=()) with forward(t), discount(t) and dividend_pv(t).

docs.title: Option Formulas & Implied Volatility
docs.text:
• black_price(F, K, T, sigma, df=1.0, option="call") and black_greeks(...): a dictionary with price, delta (forward), gamma, vega, theta, vanna, volga, dual_delta and dual_gamma. All arguments broadcast; option may be "call"/"put", booleans or ±1.
  • bachelier_price(F, K, T, sigma_n, df=1.0, option="call") and bachelier_greeks(...).
  • shifted_black_price(F, K, T, sigma, shift, df=1.0, option="call") and shifted_black_greeks(...).
  • black_scholes_price(S, K, T, r, sigma, q=0.0, option="call") and black_scholes_greeks(...) (spot delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho, epsilon).
  • implied_black_volatility(price, F, K, T, df=1.0, option="call", errors="nan"|"raise") and implied_normal_volatility(...): machine-precision inversion, vectorised; prices outside the arbitrage bounds give NaN or raise. normalised_black_call(x, s) is the normalised price \(b(x, s)\).

docs.title: Quotes, Arbitrage, Parity & Carry
docs.text:
• OptionQuote(strike, option, bid=None, ask=None, last=None, volume=None, open_interest=None) with mid, spread, relative_spread and two_sided.
  • OptionChain(expiry, quotes, forward=None, discount=None, spot=None, valuation_date=None, day_count="ACT/365F"): expiry is a year fraction or a date. Also OptionChain.from_arrays(expiry, strikes, call_bid, call_ask, put_bid, put_ask, **kw). Methods: T, strikes, calls(), puts(), mids(option), pairs(), filter(min_bid, max_relative_spread, two_sided, strike_range, min_open_interest), otm(forward), implied_vols(forward, discount, model="black"|"normal", which="mid"|"bid"|"ask", otm_only=True) and to_market_slice() (a spxa.calibration.surface.data.MarketSlice).
  • OptionSurfaceQuotes(chains, spot=None): sorted by expiry; expiries, filter(**criteria) and from_records(records, spot, **chain_kwargs).
  • check_call_prices(strikes, calls, forward, discount=1.0, expiry=nan, tol=0.0), check_calendar_arbitrage(slices, tol=0.0) and check_surface_quotes(surface, forwards=None, discounts=None, tol=0.0, use="otm") return an ArbitrageReport (truthy when arbitrage-free) of ArbitrageViolation(kind, expiry, strikes, amount). Kinds: lower_bound, upper_bound, call_spread, put_spread, butterfly, calendar. call_prices_from_chain(chain, forward, discount, use="otm"|"calls").
  • implied_forward(chain, discount=None, n_strikes=None, weights="spread"|"equal", outlier_threshold=4.0, max_iter=10) returns a ParityFit(forward, discount, strikes, residuals, rejected, discount_fitted) with n and rmse. implied_forwards(surface, discounts=None, **kw).
  • implied_carry(spot, forward, T), implied_dividend_yield(spot, forward, T, repo_discount) and implied_repo_rate(spot, forward, T, dividend_yield=0.0).
  • ImpliedForwardCurve(spot, times, forwards, discounts=None): forward(t), carry(t), discount_curve(), dividend_curve(), dividend_yield(t) and to_equity_forward(); constructors from_parity_fits(spot, times, fits) and from_surface(surface, spot=None, **kw).

docs.title: Interest Rates (spxa.rates, spxa.graph.rates)
docs.text: This section covers interest-rate instruments on real calendar dates, priced on separate discount and projection curves (any spxa.market.YieldCurve). It also covers volatility products and SABR, short-rate, HJM, Cheyette and market models, Bermudan swaptions and inflation. The theory is in Interest rates.

docs.title: Indices & Overnight Compounding
docs.text:
• OvernightIndex(name, currency, day_count="ACT/360", calendar="WEEKENDS", publication_lag=1) with fixing_dates(start, end), next_fixing_date(d) and accrual(d); IborIndex(name, currency, tenor, day_count="ACT/360", calendar="TARGET", fixing_days=2, convention="MF", end_of_month=True) with value_date, fixing_date, maturity_date and accrual. Presets SOFR, ESTR, SONIA, EURIBOR1M, EURIBOR3M, EURIBOR6M, EURIBOR12M; get_index(name) and available_indices().
  • FixingHistory(index, fixings) keyed by fixing date: from_pairs, add, get, last_date, as_mapping.
  • compounded_overnight_rate(index, start, end, fixings=None, projection=None, lookback=0, lockout=0, observation_shift=False, spread=0.0, spread_compounding="exclusive", method="compounded"|"averaged") returns a CompoundedRate (rate, accrual, dates, rates, weights, n_fixed, growth_factor). observation_schedule(...) exposes the dates and weights.
  • forward_overnight_rate(index, curve, d), curve_projection(index, curve) and projected_overnight_rate(index, start, end, curve, fixings=None, ...) (telescoping shortcut when no lookback, shift or lockout applies).

docs.title: Cashflows, Legs & Pricing
docs.text:
• Coupons: FixedCoupon, IborCoupon (use_index_dates=True projects over the index's value and maturity dates), OvernightCoupon (ISDA conventions as above) and SimpleCashflow; each has payment_date and amount(projection, fixings).
  • fixed_leg(schedule, notional, rate, day_count="30/360", payment_lag=0, payment_calendar=None), ibor_leg(schedule, notional, index, spread=0.0, gearing=1.0, day_count=None, payment_lag=0, use_index_dates=True) and overnight_leg(schedule, notional, index, spread=0.0, payment_lag=0, ...); notional is a number or one value per period.
  • leg_pv(leg, discount, projection=None, fixings=None, valuation_date=None), leg_annuity(leg, discount, valuation_date=None) and cashflow_table(...) (rows with dates, accrual, rate, amount, discount factor and PV). Coupons paid on or before the valuation date are excluded.

docs.title: Money Market & Futures
docs.text:
• Deposit(start, end, rate, day_count="ACT/360", notional=1.0) and Deposit.from_tenor(trade_date, tenor, rate, calendar="TARGET", spot_lag=2, ...): implied_rate(curve), pv(curve).
  • FRA(start, end, strike, index=None, day_count="ACT/360", notional=1.0, payer=True) and FRA.from_index(index, trade_date, start_tenor, strike, notional=1.0, payer=True) (e.g. start_tenor="3M" for a 3×6 on a 3M index): forward_rate, settlement_amount(fixing), implied_rate, pv(discount, projection, fixings).
  • IMM helpers imm_date(year, month), is_imm_date, next_imm_date, imm_code, imm_from_code.
  • RateFuture(start, end, price, index=None, day_count="ACT/360", convexity=None) and RateFuture.from_imm(index, imm, price): forward_rate, convexity_adjustment(projection, a, sigma), implied_rate, implied_price, convexity_adjusted_forward(a, sigma, t1, t2). Convexity functions hull_white_futures_convexity(t1, t2, a, sigma) and hull_white_rate_convexity(...).
  • OvernightFuture(start, end, price, index=SOFR, method="compounded"|"averaged", convexity=None), OvernightFuture.from_imm(imm, price) (3M) and OvernightFuture.monthly(year, month, price) (1M): forward_rate(projection, fixings), convexity_adjustment(projection, a, sigma, fixings), implied_rate, implied_price. Exact Hull–White pieces: hull_white_compounding_covariance(t, T, a, sigma), hull_white_discrete_compounded_convexity(times, a, sigma) and hull_white_compounded_convexity(ts, te, a, sigma).

docs.title: Swaps & Bonds
docs.text:
• Swap(fixed, floating, payer=True): fixed_leg_pv, floating_leg_pv, annuity, pv(discount, projection, fixings, valuation_date), par_rate, par_spread, with_fixed_rate(rate), pv01, dv01(discount, projection, fixings, valuation_date, bump=1e-4), start, maturity.
  • ois_swap(trade_date, tenor, fixed_rate, index=SOFR, notional=1.0, payer=True, frequency="1Y", payment_lag=2, spot_lag=2, fixed_day_count=None, forward_start=None, spread=0.0) and vanilla_swap(trade_date, tenor, fixed_rate, index=EURIBOR6M, notional=1.0, payer=True, fixed_tenor="1Y", fixed_day_count="30/360", float_tenor=None, spot_lag=None, forward_start=None, spread=0.0, use_index_dates=True). notional may be a number, one value per period, or a function of the accrual start such as step_notional(dates, values) or linear_notional(start, end, initial, final=0.0).
  • BasisSwap(first, second) with leg_pvs, pv and par_spread; basis_swap(trade_date, tenor, first, second, spread=0.0, notional=1.0, first_tenor=None, second_tenor=None, spot_lag=2, payment_lag=0, forward_start=None, use_index_dates=True) (spread on the first leg).

  • FixedRateBond(effective, maturity, coupon, frequency="6M", day_count="ACT/ACT ICMA", calendar="US-SIFMA", settlement_days=1, face=100.0, first_coupon=None): cashflows() (BondCashflow rows), settlement_date(trade_date), accrued_interest(settle), dirty_price(y, settle), clean_price(y, settle), yield_from_clean(clean, settle), macaulay_duration, modified_duration, convexity, dirty_price_from_curve(curve, settle, z_spread=0.0) and z_spread(clean, curve, settle).

  • Front-end stubs: Deposit.overnight(trade_date, rate, calendar="TARGET", day_count="ACT/360", notional=1.0), Deposit.tom_next(...) and Deposit.spot_next(...).

docs.title: Curve Construction
docs.text:
• PiecewiseCurve(times, discounts, scheme=LogLinearDiscount(), reference_date=None, day_count="ACT/365F") and PiecewiseCurve.from_zero_rates(times, rates, scheme, ...): discount, zero_rate, forward_rate, instantaneous_forward (analytic), node_times, node_discounts, node_zero_rates, with_discounts, shifted. Schemes: LogLinearDiscount(), LinearZero(), CubicZero(bc="natural") (bc is a SciPy CubicSpline boundary condition), CubicSplineRT(), MonotoneCubicRT() and MonotoneConvex(positivity=False) (Hagan–West).
  • Helpers, each with quote, pillar, curves, implied_quote(curves) and residual(curves): DepositHelper(deposit, quote, curve="discount"), FRAHelper(fra, quote, curve), FutureHelper(future, quote, curve, a=0.0, sigma=0.0) (Hull–White convexity; quarterly_futures(reference_date, prices, index=SOFR, ...) builds a strip), SwapHelper(swap, quote, discount="discount", forward=None), BasisSwapHelper(swap, quote, first, second, discount="discount") and BondHelper(bond, quote, settle, curve="discount", quote_type="clean"|"yield").
  • bootstrap_curve(helpers, reference_date, scheme=None, name="discount", known=None, day_count="ACT/365F", max_passes=None, tol=1e-13, spreads=()) returns a BootstrapResult (curve, base, curves, max_residual, node_values, jacobian(bump=1e-7), node_sensitivities(bump=1e-7)).
  • fit_curves([CurveSpec(name, helpers, scheme, spreads), ...], reference_date, known=None, tol=1e-14, max_iter=30, bump=1e-7) solves several curves simultaneously by Newton's method and returns a GlobalFitResult (curves, helpers, residuals, max_residual, iterations, jacobian, nodes).
  • Diagnostics: compare_schemes(times, rates, schemes) returns one SchemeDiagnostics (scheme, min_forward, roughness, locality, sensitivity) per scheme; bump_locality(times, rates, scheme, bump=1e-4) and forward_roughness(curve, t_max, points=20001, t_min=0.0).

docs.title: Turns, Meetings, Parametric Curves & Curve Sets
docs.text:
• ForwardSpread(start, end, spread), turn_of_year(year, spread, calendar="TARGET") and SpreadAdjustedCurve(base, spreads); pass spreads= to bootstrap_curve or CurveSpec to fit the base curve under known turns.
  • flat_forward_curve(reference_date, dates, rates) (piecewise-flat forwards stepping on dates) and meeting_date_curve(helpers, reference_date, step_dates, known=None, weights=None) returning a MeetingCurveResult (exact or Gauss–Newton least squares).
  • NelsonSiegelSvensson(beta0, beta1, beta2, beta3=0.0, tau1=1.0, tau2=None, reference_date=None) (zero, instantaneous_forward, params, is_svensson) and nelson_siegel(beta0, beta1, beta2, tau); fit_nss_zero_rates(times, zero_rates, weights=None, svensson=True, tau_bounds=(0.05, 30.0)) (variable projection) and fit_nss(helpers, reference_date, svensson=True, known=None, weights=None), both returning an NSSFit.
  • CurveSet(curves, discount, projections=None, fixings=None): discount_curve, projection(index), projection_name, get, with_curve, bumped(shift, names=None), pv(instrument, valuation_date=None) and CurveSet.from_fit(result, discount, projections).

docs.title: Curve Risk, Hedging & PCA
docs.text:
• A price function maps a dict of named curves to a value, e.g. lambda c: swap.pv(c["discount"], c["EUR-6M"]).
  • node_deltas(pv, curves, names=None, bump=1e-7) returns a NodeRisk(nodes, deltas) with for_curve(name). curve_nodes(curve) and with_node_values(curve, x) read and replace the node values \(x = -\log P\) of a piecewise curve, with turn spreads kept.
  • quote_jacobian(helpers, curves, names=None, bump=1e-7) and quote_deltas(pv, result=None, *, helpers=None, curves=None, names=None, bump=1e-7, jacobian=None). The latter takes a BootstrapResult or GlobalFitResult and returns a QuoteRisk(helpers, deltas) with per_bp, total and table().
  • key_rate_hats(keys, t), KeyRateShiftedCurve(base, keys, shifts) and key_rate_deltas(pv, curves, keys, names=None, bump=1e-4), which returns a KeyRateRisk(keys, deltas) with per_bp and total.
  • hedge_notionals(target, hedges, weights=None) and par_hedge(pv, result, hedges) return a HedgeResult(notionals, residual) with residual_norm.
  • node_gamma(pv, curves, names=None, bump=1e-5) and pnl_explain(pv, before, after, names=None), which returns a PnLExplain(full, first_order, second_order) with explained and unexplained.
  • curve_pca(rates, tenors, n_components=3, differences=True) returns a CurvePCA(tenors, components, variances, total_variance, mean) with explained_ratio, volatilities, scores, reconstruct, scenario(component, n_sd=1.0), factor_deltas(key_deltas) and factor_variance(key_deltas).

docs.title: Caps, Floors, Swaptions & SABR
docs.text:
• Caplet(coupon, strike, kind="cap"|"floor") on one IborCoupon: expiry(discount), forward(projection), weight(discount) (\(N\tau P(t_p)\)) and price(discount, projection, vol, model="black"|"normal"|"shifted_black", shift=0.0). CapFloor(caplets, strike, kind="cap") with maturity, price(...), caplet_prices(...), annuity(discount), atm_strike(discount, projection=None), with_strike(strike, kind=None) and implied_flat_vol(price, discount, ...). cap_floor(trade_date, tenor, strike, index=EURIBOR6M, notional=1.0, kind="cap", skip_first=True, forward_start=None, use_index_dates=True) builds the strip.
  • Swaption(swap, expiry, settlement="physical"|"cash") with strike, is_payer, notional, time_to_expiry(discount), forward_rate(discount, projection=None), frequency(), annuity(discount, projection=None), price(discount, projection=None, vol=0.2, model="black"|"normal"|"shifted_black", shift=0.0) and implied_vol(price, ...). swaption(trade_date, expiry, tenor, strike, index=EURIBOR6M, payer=True, notional=1.0, settlement="physical", fixed_tenor="1Y", ...) builds one; cash_annuity(S, n, m, notional=1.0) is the par-yield annuity.
  • SABR(alpha, beta, rho, nu, shift=0.0) with lognormal_vol(F, K, T, method="hagan"|"obloj"), normal_vol(F, K, T) and price(F, K, T, df=1.0, option="call", vol="lognormal"|"normal"). Functional forms sabr_lognormal_vol(F, K, T, alpha, beta, rho, nu, shift=0.0, method="hagan"), sabr_normal_vol(...) and z_over_chi(z, rho). alpha_from_atm(atm_vol, F, T, beta, rho, nu, shift=0.0); calibrate_sabr(F, strikes, vols, T, beta, shift=0.0, vol_type="lognormal", method="hagan", weights=None, atm_vol=None) returns a SABRFit(model, errors, rmse).
  • ArbitrageFreeSABR(model, F, T, n=400, n_steps=100, n_sd=4.0): the Hagan et al. (2014) density PDE. .solve() returns a SABRDensity with mass(), mean(), call(K), put(K), implied_vol(K, vol="lognormal") and the absorbed masses P_L, P_R. sabr_paths(model, F0, T, n_steps, n_paths, seed=0, bridge=True) returns SABRPaths with call(K) and put(K) (absorption at \(-\)shift).
  • strip_caplet_vols(caps, flat_vols, discount, projection=None, model="black", shift=0.0, bounds=(1e-6, 5.0)) bootstraps a piecewise-constant CapletVolCurve(expiries, vols).
  • SwaptionCube(expiries, tenors, models) with sabr(expiry, tenor) (interpolated parameters), vol(expiry, tenor, K, F, vol_type="lognormal") and SwaptionCube.calibrate(expiries, tenors, forwards, strikes, vols, beta, shift=0.0, vol_type="lognormal").
  • CMSReplication(S0, T, annuity, discount_pay, price, n, m=1, delta=0.0, mapping="standard"|"linear", slope=None, lower=0.0, upper=None): static replication on swaption prices, with alpha(S), expectation(f), coupon(), convexity_adjustment(), caplet(K) and floorlet(K).

docs.title: Short-Rate Models
docs.text:
• ShortRateModel is the protocol shared by the models below: zcb_option(T, S, K, option="call"), caplet(caplet, projection=None), cap(cap, projection=None) and swaption(swaption, projection=None). The projection basis is a deterministic spread.
  • HullWhite(curve, a, sigma, sigma_times=None) (piecewise-constant sigma on sigma_times): B(t, T), y(t), phi(t), mean_x(t), forward_mean(t, T), integrated_variance(t), discount_bond(t, T, x), short_rate(t, x), bond_option_vol(T, S), with_sigma(...) and swaption(..., method="jamshidian"|"integral").
  • Hull–White engines:
  • hull_white_paths(model, times, n_paths, seed=0, antithetic=True) returns exact HullWhitePaths with at(t), short_rate(t), zero_bond(t, T) and price(payoff, t). hull_white_transition(model, t0, t1, x, rng) is one exact step.
  • HullWhiteTree(model, horizon, n_steps): a trinomial tree fitted to the curve, with node_rates(alpha, x).
  • HullWhitePDE(model, n_space=201, n_time=200, n_sd=7.0): solve(payoff, T, exercise=None, american=None, lcp="brennan_schwartz"), value(...), zero_bond(T), zcb_option(T, S, K, option="call", american=False) and swaption(swaption).
  • Calibration:
  • calibrate_hull_white(curve, instruments, targets, projection=None, a=0.03, mode="bootstrap"|"global", sigma_times=None, sigma_bounds=(1e-6, 0.2)) returns a HullWhiteCalibration(model, prices, targets) with errors and max_relative_error.
  • market_prices(instruments, vols, discount, projection=None, model="black", shift=0.0) and model_price(model, inst, projection=None) price the inputs.
  • model_implied_vols(model, instruments, projection=None, quote="black", shift=0.0) inverts model prices back to vols.
  • G2PP(curve, a, sigma, b, eta, rho): V(t, T), covariance(t), forward_mean(t, T), phi(t), discount_bond(t, T, x, y), bond_option_vol(T, S), option_on_cashflows(T, times, amounts, const=0.0, n_quad=None) and swaptions by one-dimensional quadrature. g2pp_paths(model, times, n_paths, seed=0, antithetic=True) returns G2PPPaths with zero_bond and price. calibrate_g2pp(curve, instruments, targets, projection=None, initial=(0.5, 0.01, 0.05, 0.008, -0.5), n_quad=24) returns a G2PPCalibration. HullWhite2F(a_bar, sigma1, b_bar, sigma2, rho_bar) converts with to_g2pp(curve) and from_g2pp(model).
  • BlackKarasinski(curve, a, sigma) with tree(horizon, n_steps), which returns a BlackKarasinskiTree fitted to the curve. black_karasinski_paths(tree, n_paths, seed=0, antithetic=True) samples the tree and returns BlackKarasinskiPaths with short_rate(m), zero_bond(m, maturity) and price(payoff, m).
  • CIRPlusPlus(curve, kappa, theta, sigma, x0): provides feller, cir_forward(t), phi(t), Phi(t, T), discount_bond(t, T, x) and forward_measure_law(T) (scaled noncentral \(\chi^2\)). Options are noncentral chi-square closed forms, and swaptions use Jamshidian's decomposition.

docs.title: HJM & Cheyette
docs.text:
• GaussianHJM(curve, vols, n_quad=48, breakpoints=()) with factor volatilities vols[i](t, T) such as exponential_vol(sigma, a) and hump_vol(alpha, beta, gamma). Methods: sigma(t, T), Sigma(t, T), drift(t, T), forward_bond_variance(T, s, e), closed-form zcb_option, caplet and cap, and GaussianHJM.from_hull_white(model, n_quad=48).
  • hjm_paths(model, maturities, n_paths, record=None, keep=None, seed=0, antithetic=True) returns HJMPaths with deflated(t, T), deflator(t), zero_bond(t, T) and price(payoff, t).
  • Cheyette(curve, kappa, sigma, beta=0.0, sigma_times=None): the local volatility is \(\max(\sigma(t) + \beta x, 0)\). Methods: sigma_at(t), local_vol(t, x), G(t, T), discount_bond(t, T, x, y), short_rate(t, x), ybar(t) and to_hull_white() (when beta = 0).
  • Cheyette engines:
  • cheyette_paths(model, horizon, n_steps, n_paths, record=None, seed=0, antithetic=True) returns CheyettePaths with zero_bond and price.
  • CheyettePDE(model, n_x=161, n_y=41, n_time=200, n_sd=6.0) provides solve(payoff, T, exercise=None), zero_bond(T) and swaption(swaption).
  • swap_rate_dynamics(model, swaption, projection=None, n_time=128) returns a DisplacedSwapRate(S0, annuity, expiry, lam, skew) with price(K, payer=True); cheyette_swaption(...) is the resulting approximate price.
  • calibrate_cheyette(curve, swaptions, targets, projection=None, kappa=0.03, initial=(0.01, 0.0), beta_bounds=(-2.0, 5.0)) returns a CheyetteCalibration with max_relative_error.

docs.title: LIBOR & Forward Market Models
docs.text:
• AbcdVol(a, b, c, d) gives \((a + b\tau)e^{-c\tau} + d\), with the closed-form covariance(Ti, Tj, t0, t1). Correlations: exponential_correlation(times, beta), rebonato_correlation(times, beta, rho_inf) and reduce_rank(rho, n_factors).
  • LiborMarketModel(curve, times, vol, k=None, correlation=None, shift=0.0): displaced lognormal forwards. Methods: sigma(t), covariance(t0, t1), caplet_variance(i), caplet_vol(i), caplet(i, K, notional=1.0, option="call"), swap_weights(alpha, beta), and swaption_vol(alpha, beta) and swaption(alpha, beta, K, payer=True, notional=1.0) by Rebonato's formula.
  • lmm_paths(model, n_paths, steps_per_period=4, seed=None, antithetic=True, predictor_corrector=True) simulates under the spot measure. It returns LMMPaths with fixings, deflator(k), bond(k, e) and price(values, k).
  • fit_abcd(times, caplet_vols, initial=(0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 0.1)). calibrate_lmm(curve, times, caplet_vols, swaptions, swaption_vols, shift=0.0, initial_correlation=(0.1, 0.5)) reprices caplets exactly and fits the correlation to swaptions. It returns an LMMCalibration with max_swaption_error.
  • ForwardMarketModel(curve, times, vol, k=None, correlation=None, shift=0.0): backward-looking compounded rates (Lyashenko–Mercurio) whose volatility decays over the accrual period. It has decay(t), sigma(t), covariance(t0, t1), caplet_variance(i), caplet_vol(i) and caplet(...). fmm_paths(model, n_paths, steps_per_period=4, seed=None, antithetic=True) returns FMMPaths with fixings, deflator(k) and price(values, k).
  • SABRLMM(curve, times, alphas, beta, rho, nu, correlation=None, shift=0.0) with sabr(i) and caplet(...). sabr_lmm_paths(model, n_paths, steps_per_period=8, seed=None, antithetic=True) returns LMMPaths.

docs.title: Bermudan Swaptions & Least Squares
docs.text:
• BermudanSwaption(exercise_times, underlyings): payer-signed ModelCashflows(times, amounts) (pv(discount), value(model, t, x)) for each exercise. It has n_exercise, maturity, underlying_value(k, model, x), exercise_value(k, model, x), restrict(ks) and underlying_pv(k, discount).
  • Built by bermudan_swaption(swap, discount, projection=None, lockout=1) (co-terminal) or bermudan_from_times(exercise_times, end, fixed_rate, notional=1.0, payer=True, frequency=1).
  • coterminal_swaptions(swap, discount, lockout=1) lists the European components.
  • swap_cashflows(swap, discount, projection=None) and coupon_cashflows(fixed, floating, sign, discount, projection=None) convert legs into model cashflows.
  • Lattice engines: bermudan_pde(engine, bermudan) (a HullWhitePDE or CheyettePDE) and bermudan_tree(tree, bermudan) (a HullWhiteTree).
  • Least squares:
  • ExerciseProblem(times, x0, step, exercise_value, basis), built by hull_white_exercise_problem(model, bermudan) or cheyette_exercise_problem(model, bermudan, steps_per_year=50).
  • lsm(problem, n_paths, seed=0, n_train=None) fits an LSMPolicy (continuation, exercise, value_from) on training paths and values it on independent paths, which gives a lower bound.
  • andersen_broadie(result, n_outer=1000, n_inner=500, seed=0) returns a DualBound(upper, stderr, lower, lower_stderr) with gap and midpoint.

docs.title: Inflation
docs.text:
• CPIFixings(name, levels) keyed by reference month: from_pairs(name, pairs), from_series(name, first_month, values), add, get and last_month. month_start(d).
  • InflationIndex(name, fixings, lag=3, interpolated=True, digits=None) with reference_months(d), reference_cpi(d) (TIPS daily interpolation, optional rounding), index_ratio(d, base_date) and is_fixed(d).
  • Seasonality(factors): twelve multiplicative log factors. It has adjustment(month, base_month) and Seasonality.estimate(fixings, years=None), which estimates them from the history (demeaned average log change by calendar month).
  • bootstrap_inflation_curve(index, start, quotes, seasonality=None) fits the zero-coupon swap rates {years: rate} exactly. It returns an InflationCurve(index, base_month, pillar_months, pillar_levels, seasonality=None) with fixing(month), reference_cpi(d), zero_coupon_rate(start, maturity, years=None) and real_curve(nominal, today, years=30).
  • ZeroCouponInflationSwap(start, years, fixed_rate, notional=1.0) has maturity, inflation_leg(nominal, curve), fixed_leg(nominal), present_value(nominal, curve) and fair_rate(curve). YearOnYearInflationSwap(start, years, fixed_rate, notional=1.0, months=12, day_count="30/360") has schedule(), inflation_leg(nominal, curve, model=None), annuity(nominal), present_value(...) and fair_rate(...); passing a Jarrow–Yildirim model adds the convexity.
  • InflationLinkedBond(coupon, maturity, dated_date, index, frequency=2, face=100.0, deflation_floor=True, base_cpi=None), with Treasury's TIPS formulas:
  • base, coupon_dates() and accrued(settlement);
  • real_price(settlement, real_yield) and real_yield(settlement, real_price);
  • settlement_amount(settlement, real_yield, digits=6);
  • present_value(nominal, inflation, today, model=None), a dict of coupons, principal, floor and total, with the deflation floor valued under model;
  • breakeven_inflation(nominal_yield, real_yield).
  • JarrowYildirim(nominal, real, cpi0, a_n, sigma_n, a_r, sigma_r, sigma_i, rho_nr=0.0, rho_ni=0.0, rho_ri=0.0): nominal and real Hull–White rates with a lognormal index. Methods: forward_index(T), zero_coupon_swap_rate(T), yoy_convexity(T1, T2), yoy_forward(T1, T2), yoy_swaplet(T1, T2), yoy_swap_rate(times), log_ratio_variance(T1, T2), zero_coupon_caplet(T, strike, option="call") and yoy_caplet(T1, T2, strike, option="call").
  • jy_paths(model, T, n_steps, n_paths, record=(), seed=None) returns JYPaths(times, discount, index, nominal_rate, real_rate) with column(t). The curve parts are integrated exactly, so seasonal real curves are repriced.
  • calibrate_jarrow_yildirim(model, quotes, parameters=("sigma_i", "sigma_r"), starts=(1/3, 1.0, 3.0)) fits InflationOptionQuote(start, end, strike, price, option="call", kind="yoy"|"zc") prices with a multi-start search. It returns a JYFit(model, parameters, rmse, success).

docs.title: Risk Adapter, Graph Nodes & Extension Points
docs.text:
• curve_price(instrument, market, base=None) values an spxa.risk.instruments.InterestRateSwap on market["<rate id>_CURVE"], or on a flat curve at market["r"]. Against base, the change in r is a parallel zero-rate shift. It returns a CurveQuote(instrument_id, price, dv01, par_rate, annuity) with the exact parallel DV01. curve_pricing_fn(book, base_market=None) returns a market -> value callable for StressTestingEngine.
  • spxa.graph.rates:
  • discounted_cashflows_node(zero_rates, pillars, times, amounts) and par_swap_rate_node(zero_rates, pillars, maturity, frequency=0.5) take zero-rate input nodes, interpolated linearly in zero rate.
  • Their analytic vector–Jacobian products give all key-rate sensitivities in one GradientTape pass.
  • zero_curve_weights(pillars, times) returns the interpolation weights.
  • Extension points:
  • InterpolationScheme (fit(times, logp) returns a FittedInterpolation with evaluate(t)), with hyman_slopes(x, y) and discrete_forwards(times, logp).
  • CurveHelper (pillar, curves, implied_quote, residual) and last_curve_date(leg).
  • nss_loadings(t, tau1, tau2=None, forward=False).
  • Typing aliases: Cashflow, Leg and NotionalLike; CashflowRow is a row of cashflow_table.

docs.title: Volatility Modelling (spxa.vol, spxa.graph.vol)
docs.text: This section covers arbitrage-free implied-volatility slices and surfaces in log-forward moneyness \(k = \log(K/F)\) and total variance \(w = \sigma^2 T\). It also covers the models calibrated to them: local, stochastic local and rough volatility, VIX, martingale optimal transport bounds, variance swaps and model risk. The theory is in Volatility.

docs.title: Coordinates & SVI Slices
docs.text:
• log_moneyness(K, F), strike_from_log_moneyness(k, F), total_variance(sigma, T), implied_vol_from_total_variance(w, T), normalised_call_from_total_variance(k, w) and total_variance_from_price(price, F, K, T, df=1.0, option="call").
  • SVIRaw(a, b, rho, m, sigma): callable as w(k), with total_variance, dw, d2w, implied_vol(k, T), min_variance, argmin, left_slope, right_slope, satisfies_lee_bound(), to_natural(), to_jump_wings(t), to_array()/from_array(p).
  • SVINatural(delta, mu, rho, omega, zeta) with to_raw(); SVIJumpWings(v, psi, p, c, v_min, t) with to_raw(), butterfly_free_projection(), satisfies_ssvi_bounds() and to_ssvi_natural().

docs.title: SSVI & eSSVI
docs.text:
• SSVI(rho, phi, theta) with total_variance(k, T), total_variance_theta(k, theta), implied_vol, slice(T) (raw SVI), butterfly_conditions(thetas), calendar_conditions(thetas) and is_arbitrage_free(thetas). Curvatures HestonLikePhi(lam) and PowerLawPhi(eta, gamma); ATMVarianceCurve(times, thetas).
  • ESSVISlice(theta, psi, rho) with phi, total_variance, to_raw() and butterfly_free(); essvi_calendar_free(first, second, tol=0.0); ESSVI(times, slices, long_theta_slope=None) with params(T), slice(T), total_variance(k, T), implied_vol, violations() and is_arbitrage_free(); anchored_theta(rho, psi, k_star, theta_star).

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
• calibrate_svi(k, w, weights=None, max_slope=2.0, sigma_bounds=(1e-4, 5.0), m_bounds=None, n_starts=4) (quasi-explicit) and svi_inner_fit(k, w, m, sigma, weights=None, max_slope=2.0) return an SVIFit(params, rmse, sse, nfev, success) or a (slice, sse) pair.
  • calibrate_svi_butterfly_free(k, w, weights=None, max_slope=2.0, grid=None, initial=None, min_g=1e-8, lower=None, min_gap=0.0): Durrleman's condition (and, with lower, no calendar arbitrage against the previous slice) imposed with cutting planes.
  • calibrate_svi_surface(expiries, ks, ws, weights=None, max_slope=2.0, min_g=1e-8, min_gap=0.0, grid=None) returns an SVISurfaceFit(expiries, slices, fits) with rmse and success.
  • calibrate_ssvi(expiries, ks, ws, phi="power_law"|"heston", no_arbitrage=True) returns an SSVIFit(surface, thetas, rmse, success); isotonic_increasing(y, weights=None) is the pool-adjacent-violators fit used for \(\theta_t\).
  • calibrate_essvi(expiries, ks, ws, n_rho=41, margin=1e-9) returns an ESSVI.

docs.title: Diagnostics, Interpolation & Distributions
docs.text:
• durrleman_g(k, w, dw, d2w), risk_neutral_density(slice, k), check_butterfly(slice, k=None, tol=0.0) (a ButterflyCheck with min_g, argmin and negative_intervals) and check_calendar(slices, k=None, tol=0.0) (a CalendarCheck with worst, at_k and between). Both checks are truthy when arbitrage-free.
  • wing_asymptotics(slice, k_far=1e4) returns WingAsymptotics(left_slope, right_slope) with left_moment, right_moment, left_decay, right_decay and satisfies_lee_bound. Also lee_moment_from_slope(beta), lee_slope_from_moment(x) and rogers_tehranchi_slope(slice, k=None).
  • PriceInterpolatedSurface(expiries, slices) with theta(t), bucket(t), otm_price(k, t), call_price(k, t), total_variance(k, t), implied_vol(k, t) and density(k, t).
  • ImpliedDistribution(slice, k_min=None, k_max=None) with pdf, cdf, survival, digital_call, digital_put, expectation(f, points=None), total_mass, forward_ratio, moment(n), call(k), quantile(u) and sample(n, rng=None, grid=4001).
  • VarianceInterpolatedSurface(expiries, slices, mode="fixed_k"|"normalised") with theta(t), total_variance(k, t) and implied_vol(k, t); both modes extrapolate beyond the last expiry.

docs.title: Surfaces from Quotes
docs.text:
• build_vol_surface(quotes, method="svi"|"essvi"|"ssvi", weights="uniform"|"vega"|"spread", spot=None, min_quotes=5, **fit_kwargs) takes an OptionSurfaceQuotes and returns a SurfaceBuild(surface, method, expiries, forwards, discounts, ks, ws, weights, fit, parity) with vol_rmse, model_total_variance and quality(tol=1e-8, points=401). The quality report is a SurfaceQuality(expiries, calendar_free, worst_calendar) of ExpiryQuality rows (n_quotes, vol_rmse, max_vol_error, atm_vol, atm_skew, min_g, butterfly_free), with arbitrage_free, worst_vol_error and table().
  • ForwardTermStructure(expiries, forwards, discounts, spot=None) with forward(t) and discount(t); chain_total_variance(chain, forward, discount, weights="uniform") returns (k, w, weights).
  • repair_call_prices(strikes, prices, forwards, discounts, weights=None, bid=None, ask=None) returns a RepairResult(prices, perturbation, l1, violations_before, violations_after); call_arbitrage_constraints(strikes, forwards) exposes the linear constraints as an ArbitrageConstraints.
  • fengler_smooth(strikes, calls, forward, discount=1.0, expiry=None, smoothing=1e-6, weights=None, upper=None) returns a FenglerSmile with price, normalised, implied_vol, density and roughness. fengler_surface(expiries, strikes, calls, forwards, discounts, smoothing=1e-6) returns a FenglerSurface with slice(T) and calendar_violation(points=401); spline_matrices and spline_eval_matrix are the underlying natural-spline algebra.

docs.title: The Surface Object, Deltas & Risk
docs.text:
• VolSurface(model, forward) and the constructors VolSurface.from_slices(expiries, slices, forward, time_interpolation="price"|"fixed_k"|"normalised"), VolSurface.flat(sigma, forward) and VolSurface.from_spot(model, spot, rate, dividend_yield=None).
  • Pricing: price(K, T, option="call"), implied_vol(K, T), implied_vol_k, total_variance, smile(T, strikes), atm_vol(T) and atm_skew(T).
  • Forward variance: forward_variance(T1, T2, k=0.0), forward_vol and forward_variance_grid(expiries, k).
  • Greeks: greeks(K, T, option="call", dynamics="sticky_strike"|"sticky_moneyness", bump=1e-4), delta(K, T, option, kind="forward"|"spot", premium_adjusted=False) and strike_from_delta(delta, T, ...).
  • Simulation: terminal_distribution(T) and sample_terminal(T, n, rng=None).
  • Bumps: bumped(bump).
  • black_delta(F, K, T, sigma, option="call", kind="forward", premium_adjusted=False, carry=1.0), strike_from_delta(delta, F, T, sigma, ...) (sigma may be a smile \(k \mapsto \sigma(k)\)) and atm_dns_strike(F, T, sigma, premium_adjusted=False).
  • Bumps: parallel_bump(size), skew_bump(size), expiry_buckets(pillars, size) and BumpedModel(base, bump). bucketed_vega(value, surface, bumps, size) returns the central-difference vega for each bump.
  • Persistence: to_dict(obj), from_dict(d), dumps(obj, **json_kwargs) and loads(s) for surfaces, total-variance models, forwards and yield curves (bit-exact JSON round trips).
  • Protocols: TotalVarianceModel (anything with total_variance(k, T)) and ForwardLike (anything with forward(t) and discount(t)).

docs.title: Local Volatility
docs.text:
• LocalVolSurface(surface, dk=1e-3, dt_rel=1e-3, y_range=(-4.0, 4.0), t_min=1e-4) applies Dupire's formula in implied total variance to a VolSurface.
  • Values: terms(y, T), local_variance_k(y, T), local_vol_k(y, T), local_vol(K, T) and density(T, spot, r, q=0.0, n=801, n_time=400, width=8.0).
  • Links to spxa.pde: dupire_pde(r, q=0.0) and black_scholes_pde(r, q=0.0), plus american(K, T, spot, r, q=0.0, option="put", **kw) and barrier(K, T, spot, barrier, r, q=0.0, barrier_type="down-and-out", option="call", **kw).
  • VolSurface.local_vol_surface(**kw) and VolSurface.local_vol(K, T) call it.
  • dupire_local_variance(y, w, w_y, w_yy, w_T) (nan where undefined) and bbf_implied_vol(local_vol_k, k, n=401), the short-expiry Berestycki–Busca–Florent inverse. LocalVolGrid(ys, ts, variance, forward, floor=0.01, cap=3.0) and LocalVolGrid.from_surface(lv, ys, ts) tabulate it for fast lookups.
  • Andreasen–Huge interpolation:
  • calibrate_andreasen_huge(expiries, strikes, vols, grid=None, max_nodes=None, weights=None) fits piecewise-constant local-vol levels expiry by expiry.
  • It returns an AndreasenHugeFit(surface, errors, nfev) with max_error and rmse.
  • AndreasenHugeSurface(expiries, nodes, levels, grid=None) provides grid_calls(t), normalised_call(y, t) and total_variance(k, T), so it can back a VolSurface.
  • Helpers: andreasen_huge_grid(y_max=4.0, n=401, concentration=0.5) and piecewise_constant_vol(nodes_y, levels, y).
  • local_vol_paths(sigma, spot, r, q, T, n_steps, n_paths, seed=0, antithetic=True, record=None) returns LocalVolPaths with at(t), price(payoff, T) and forward_start(T1, T2, k, option="call").
  • local_vol_diagnostics(lv, spot, r, q, strikes, expiries, n_space=801, n_time=400, y_grid=None, n_t=40, reprice=True) returns LocalVolDiagnostics with errors, max_error, worst(), undefined_fraction and first_undefined_time().

docs.title: Stochastic Local Volatility
docs.text:
• Heston(v0, kappa, theta, xi, rho) has feller, scaled(eta), mean_variance(t), expected_total_variance(T), cf(T), price(K, T, F=1.0, df=1.0, option="call"), implied_vol(K, T, F=1.0) and atm_short_vol(). variance_std(model, t) and variance_quantile(model, t, q) give the exact variance law.
  • slv_grid(model, T, n_y=121, n_v=61, n_sd=5.0, vol=None, v_tail=1e-6) returns an SLVGrid(y, v) with shape, weights and node(y, v).
  • slv_forward(model, grid, T, n_time=100, leverage=None, record=(), damping_steps=2) solves the two-dimensional Fokker–Planck equation with ADI. It returns an SLVForward holding an SLVDensity for each recorded time. Each density has mass, marginal(), expectation(g), forward(), conditional_variance(), call(k) and implied_vol(k).
  • Leverage calibration:
  • calibrate_leverage(local_vol, model, T, grid=None, n_time=100, record=(), ...) calibrates by forward induction, \(L^2 = \sigma_{LV}^2/E[v \mid y]\). It returns a LeverageCalibration(model, leverage, forward) with smile(k, t).
  • calibrate_leverage_particles(local_vol, model, T, n_steps=100, n_particles=50000, nodes=None, bandwidth=1.5, seed=None) is the particle method, built on kernel_conditional_mean(x, v, nodes, h). It returns a ParticleCalibration.
  • LeverageSurface(ts, ys, values) has row(t) and LeverageSurface.constant(value=1.0).
  • calibrate_slv(local_vol, heston, eta, T, n_y=121, n_v=61, n_time=100, record=(), grid=None, vol=0.2) scales vol-of-variance by the mixing fraction eta and calibrates the leverage. It returns an SLVModel with paths(T, n_steps, n_paths, **kw), pde(r=0.0, q=0.0, **kw) and smile(k, t). as_local_vol(local_vol, T, ...) tabulates a surface's local vol.
  • slv_paths(model, leverage, T, n_steps, n_paths, record=(), seed=None, antithetic=True, lower=None, upper=None, bridge=True) returns SLVPaths with at(t) and price(payoff, t, knock_out=False). Barriers use Brownian-bridge survival weights.
  • SLVPDE(model, leverage=None, r=0.0, q=0.0, n_x=161, n_v=61, n_time=100, n_sd=5.0, vol=None) provides european(K, T, option="call", spot=1.0), barrier(K, T, option="call", spot=1.0, lower=None, upper=None) and price(payoff, T, spot=1.0, lower=None, upper=None).

docs.title: Rough Volatility & VIX
docs.text:
• RoughHeston(v0, theta, lam, nu, rho, hurst) has log_cf(u, T, n_steps=200), cf(u, T, n_steps=200), expected_variance(t) and heston_limit(). fractional_riccati(u, T, alpha, lam, nu, rho, n_steps=200) is the Adams scheme behind it.
  • LiftedHeston(v0, theta, lam, nu, rho, hurst, n=20, weights=None, speeds=None) has g0(t), expected_variance(t), log_cf and cf. lifted_weights(n, hurst, r=None) gives the geometric partition.
  • Both models inherit FourierPricing: price(K, T, F=1.0, df=1.0, option="call", n_steps=200, n_quad=256, u_max=20.0) and implied_vol(K, T, F=1.0, n_steps=200).
  • calibrate_rough_heston(maturities, strikes, vols, initial, free=("v0", "theta", "nu", "rho", "hurst"), forwards=None, weights=None, n_steps=400) returns a RoughHestonFit(model, vols, targets, nfev) with rmse. n_steps must keep the Adams scheme stable over the whole Fourier range; too few steps make the objective non-smooth (see the theory chapter, §10.3).
  • rbergomi_paths(hurst, eta, rho, xi, T, n_steps, n_paths, s0=1.0, seed=None, keep_variance=False) uses the hybrid scheme, with weights from hybrid_weights(hurst, dt, n). It returns RBergomiPaths with price(K, option="call", conditional=True) and implied_vol(K).
  • calibrate_rbergomi(T, strikes, vols, initial, free=("hurst", "eta", "rho"), n_steps=50, n_paths=10000, seed=0) returns an RBergomiFit with rmse.
  • HestonVIX(model, delta=VIX_WINDOW) (VIX_WINDOW = 30/365) gives VIX futures and options in closed form up to one quadrature: variance_law(T), expected_vix_squared(T), futures(T), options(T, K, option="call") and implied_vols(T, K).
  • RBergomiVIX(hurst, eta, xi, delta=VIX_WINDOW, n_nodes=24) provides:
  • exact Gaussian sampling: vix_squared(T, n_paths, seed=None), futures(T, n_paths=200000, seed=None), options(...) and implied_vols(...);
  • lognormal approximations: lognormal_moments(T), futures_lognormal(T) and options_lognormal(T, K, option="call");
  • quadrature details: xi(t), nodes(T), covariance(T) and expected_vix_squared(T).
  • calibrate_heston_joint(spx, vix, initial, weights=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)) fits all five Heston parameters to SmileQuote(T, strikes, vols) SPX smiles and VIXQuote(T, futures, strikes, vols) VIX quotes. It returns a JointFit with rmse(part).

docs.title: Martingale Optimal Transport
docs.text:
• DiscreteMarginal(points, weights) has mean, call(k), expect(f) and precedes(other, tol=1e-12) (convex order). Built by marginal_from_calls(strikes, calls, floor=None) or surface_marginals(surface, expiries, strikes) (laws of \(S_T/F_T\)).
  • mot_solve(mu, nu, payoff, sense="max"|"min") solves the linear program with HiGHS. It returns an MOTResult(value, plan, phi, psi, h, sense, mu, nu) with dual_value and hedge(x, y). mot_bounds(mu, nu, payoff) returns (lower, upper), and ot_solve(...) drops the martingale constraint for comparison.
  • mot_sinkhorn(mu, nu, payoff, sense="max", eps=1e-3, eps_start=None, tol=1e-9, max_iter=5000) is entropic MOT. It returns a SinkhornResult with the potentials and the marginal and martingale errors reached.
  • robust_bounds(surface, T1, T2, payoff, strikes, scale=1.0) returns (lower, upper, lower_result, upper_result). Ready-made payoffs are forward_start_call(k, ratio=1.0) and forward_start_straddle(k=1.0, ratio=1.0).
  • Hedges as trades:
  • static_replication(points, values) returns a StaticReplication(cash, forward, strikes, calls) with price(marginal).
  • superhedge_pnl(result, payoff, x, y) is the pathwise hedge P&L.
  • mot_multi(marginals, payoff, sense="max") handles several dates and returns (value, plan).

docs.title: Variance & Volatility Swaps
docs.text:
• fair_variance(otm, T, sd=None) computes the fair variance from normalised OTM prices. variance_swap_strike(surface, T) and gamma_swap_strike(surface, T) apply the Carr–Madan replication to a surface; variance_swap_curve(surface, expiries) returns the term structure.
  • ForwardVarianceCurve(expiries, strikes) is piecewise-flat \(\xi_0(t)\), with integral(t), variance_swap(T) and forward_variance_swap(T1, T2). vix_index(surface, delta=30/365) is the model-free VIX.
  • realised_variance(log_prices, times, demean=False), variance_swap_payoff(realised, strike, cap=None) and variance_swap_mtm(realised_variance, t, T, strike, fair_remaining, df, notional=1.0).
  • heston_integrated_variance_laplace(model, T, s) and heston_volatility_swap(model, T), which gives \(E\sqrt{V_T/T}\) by the Laplace transform.

docs.title: Model Risk
docs.text:
• ModelRisk(names, prices, errors, std_errors) holds the prices of one claim, or a vector of claims, under named models. Build it with ModelRisk.from_prices(prices, errors=None, std_errors=None) or ModelRisk.from_samples(samples, payoff, errors=None, discount=1.0).
  • Admissible set and Cont's coherent measure: admissible(tolerance), upper, lower, width and relative_width.
  • Penalised measure: penalised(lam) and penalised_width(lam).
  • Statistics and comparison: significant(n_se=3.0), within(lower, upper, n_se=3.0), share(lower, upper) (against a model-free interval) and combine(weights).
  • smile_rmse(model_vols, market_vols, weights=None).

docs.title: Risk Adapter, Processes & Graph Nodes
docs.text:
• surface_price(instrument, market, base=None, dynamics="sticky_strike"|"sticky_moneyness", spot_bump=1e-4) values an spxa.risk.instruments.EuropeanOption on market["<id>_SURFACE"].
  • Spot moves scale the forwards.
  • Against base, changes in <id>_VOL and r are parallel vol and rate shifts.
  • It returns a SurfaceQuote(instrument_id, price, vol, forward, delta, vega).
  • surface_pricing_fn(book, base_market=None, dynamics=...) feeds StressTestingEngine.
  • process_vol_surface(process, spot, rate, expiries, dividend_yield=0.0, width=2.5, n_strikes=21), also available as Process.to_vol_surface(spot, rate, expiries, **kw), works on exponential-Lévy models from the zoo.
  • It prices OTM options with Lewis's formula, inverts Black and fits SVI per expiry.
  • It returns a ProcessSurface(surface, expiries, log_moneyness, model_vols, max_vol_error).
  • spxa.graph.vol nodes:
  • svi_total_variance_node(a, b, rho, m, sigma, *, k) has an analytic gradient.
  • surface_price_node(spot, vol_shift=0.0, *, surface, strike, maturity, option="call", dynamics="sticky_strike") uses the adapter's delta and vega as its vector–Jacobian product.

docs.title: Stochastic Calculus Engine (spxa.calculus)
docs.text:
The spxa.calculus module provides a first-class, institutionally rigorous analytical and computational stochastic calculus suite in Python. It bridges exact symbolic computer algebra with high-precision pathwise numerical semimartingale statistics, variational Wiener space calculus, and stochastic measure transformations.

Engine Architecture & Core Author

Julian Vance (Quantitative Research & Stochastic Analysis) Engineered the complete spxa.calculus suite: symbolic Itô/Stratonovich differential algebra, Doléans-Dade semimartingale exponentials, Girsanov measure shifts, Feller boundary classifications, and Malliavin variational operators.

docs.title: 1. Symbolic Itô Calculus & PDE Derivations (spxa.calculus.symbolic)
docs.text:
The symbolic engine models stochastic differentials algebraically over the Itô multiplication table:

\[\begin{aligned} dt \cdot dt &= 0, \quad dt \cdot dW_i = 0, \quad dW_i \cdot dt = 0 \\ dW_i \cdot dW_j &= \rho_{ij} \, dt \\ dN_i \cdot dN_j &= \delta_{ij} \, dN_i, \quad dN_i \cdot dt = 0, \quad dN_i \cdot dW_j = 0 \end{aligned}\]

Given any \(C^{1,2}\) scalar function \(f(t, X_1, \dots, X_d)\), apply_ito_symbolic performs multidimensional Taylor series expansion, applies Itô product rules, and extracts the drift and diffusion terms.

import sympy as sp
from spxa.calculus.symbolic import SymbolicSDE, apply_ito_symbolic, derive_kolmogorov_pde

# Define driving symbols
t, S, mu, sigma, dW = sp.symbols("t S mu sigma dW")

# Geometric Brownian Motion: dS = mu * S * dt + sigma * S * dW
gbm = SymbolicSDE(
    state_vars=(S,),
    time_var=t,
    drift=(mu * S,),
    diffusion=((sigma * S,),),
    wiener_vars=(dW,),
)

# Apply Itô's formula symbolically to log(S)
result = apply_ito_symbolic(sp.log(S), gbm)
print(result.drift_term)        # mu - sigma**2 / 2
print(result.diffusion_terms)   # (sigma,)

# Derive the Kolmogorov Backward / Feynman-Kac pricing PDE
pde = derive_kolmogorov_pde(gbm, discount_rate=mu)
print(pde)

docs.title: 2. Itô & Stratonovich Calculus Engine (spxa.calculus.ito)
docs.text:
Calculates multivariate Itô differentials, converts between Itô and Stratonovich drift formulations, and verifies the discrete semimartingale integration by parts identity:

\[X_t Y_t - X_0 Y_0 = \int_0^t X_{s-} dY_s + \int_0^t Y_{s-} dX_s + [X, Y]_t\]

docs.title: Stratonovich Drift Conversions
docs.text:
For an Itô SDE \(dX_t = b(t, X_t) dt + \sigma(t, X_t) dW_t\), the Stratonovich drift is:

\[\underline{b}_i(t, x) = b_i(t, x) - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^d \sigma_{jk}(t, x) \frac{\partial \sigma_{ik}}{\partial x_j}(t, x)\] 
from spxa.calculus.ito import ito_to_stratonovich, stratonovich_to_ito

# CEV Diffusion: sigma(x) = sigma * x^gamma
drift_fn = lambda t, x: 0.05 * x
diff_fn = lambda t, x: 0.3 * (x ** 0.6)

strat_drift = ito_to_stratonovich(drift_fn, diff_fn, d=1, m=1)
recovered_ito = stratonovich_to_ito(strat_drift, diff_fn, d=1, m=1)

docs.title: 3. Doléans-Dade Exponentials & Martingales (spxa.calculus.doleans)
docs.text:
Evaluates the unique solution to \(dZ_t = Z_{t-} dX_t\) with \(Z_0 = 1\):

\[\mathcal{E}(X)_t = \exp\left( X_t - X_0 - \frac{1}{2} [X^c]_t \right) \prod_{0 < s \le t} (1 + \Delta X_s) e^{-\Delta X_s}\]

It also provides the inverse stochastic logarithm:

\[\mathcal{L}(Z)_t = \int_0^t \frac{1}{Z_{s-}} dZ_s\]

and evaluates Novikov's criteria and the martingale defect \(D(t) = Z_0 - \mathbb{E}[Z_t]\) to detect strict local martingales.

from spxa.calculus.doleans import doleans_exponential, stochastic_logarithm, martingale_defect

# Pathwise Doléans exponential and exact logarithm recovery
z_path = doleans_exponential(x_path)
recovered_x = stochastic_logarithm(z_path)

# Verify whether simulated paths form a true martingale
defect_res = martingale_defect(all_paths, times)
print(f"Is true martingale: {defect_res.is_true_martingale}")

docs.title: 4. Girsanov Measure Transformations (spxa.calculus.girsanov)
docs.text:
Implements the Cameron-Martin-Girsanov theorem:

\[Z_t = \left. \frac{d\mathbb{Q}}{d\mathbb{P}} \right|_{\mathcal{F}_t} = \exp\left( -\int_0^t \theta_s dW_s^\mathbb{P} - \frac{1}{2} \int_0^t |\theta_s|^2 ds \right)\]

Shifts Brownian drift under risk-neutral (\(\mathbb{Q}\)), \(T\)-forward (\(\mathbb{Q}^T\)), and annuity measures, and reweights pathwise expectations via importance sampling:

\[\mathbb{E}^\mathbb{Q}[\Phi(S_T)] = \mathbb{E}^\mathbb{P}[\Phi(S_T) Z_T]\] 
from spxa.calculus.girsanov import risk_neutral_measure_change

rn_change = risk_neutral_measure_change(
    physical_drift=0.12,
    volatility=0.20,
    risk_free_rate=0.05
)

# Transform expectations under Physical measure into Risk-Neutral prices
rn_price = rn_change.expectation_change(call_payoffs, radon_nikodym_densities)

docs.title: 5. Infinitesimal Generators & Dynkin Solvers (spxa.calculus.generator)
docs.text:
Evaluates the differential operator \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = b(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2(x) f''(x)\) and solves boundary value problems via scale and speed measures:

\[s'(x) = \exp\left(-\int_a^x \frac{2 b(y)}{\sigma^2(y)} dy\right), \quad m(x) = \frac{2}{\sigma^2(x) s'(x)}\]
  • Dynkin Mean First Exit Time: Solves \(\mathcal{A} u(x) = -1\) on \((a, b)\) with \(u(a) = u(b) = 0\): $\(u(x) = \frac{s(x) - s(a)}{s(b) - s(a)} \int_a^b (s(b) - s(y)) m(y) dy - \int_a^x (s(x) - s(y)) m(y) dy\)$
  • Feller Boundary Classification: Classifies boundaries into Regular, Exit, Entrance, or Natural.
from spxa.calculus.generator import (
    classify_feller_boundary,
    dynkin_mean_exit_time,
    dynkin_exit_probability
)

# Mean first exit time for standard Brownian motion on [-1, 1]
x_grid, u_vals = dynkin_mean_exit_time(lambda x: 0.0, lambda x: 1.0, a=-1.0, b=1.0)
# u(0) = 1.0 (exact theoretical value)

# Feller classification for CIR at boundary 0
feller_res = classify_feller_boundary(
    drift_fn=lambda x: 2.0 * (0.04 - x),
    diffusion_fn=lambda x: 0.1 * (x ** 0.5),
    boundary_point=0.0,
    interior_point=0.04
)
print(feller_res.classification)  # BoundaryType.ENTRANCE

docs.title: 6. Realized Quadratic Variation & Jump Tests (spxa.calculus.variation)
docs.text:
Computes realized quadratic variation, covariation, and Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard realized bipower variation (BV) to separate continuous diffusive volatility from jumps:

\[\text{BV}_t = \frac{\pi}{2} \sum_{k=2}^n |\Delta X_k| \cdot |\Delta X_{k-1}| \xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}} \int_0^t \sigma_s^2 ds\]

Provides statistical hypothesis tests: - BNS \(Z\)-Test: Tests \(H_0: \text{No jumps}\) against \(H_1: \text{Jumps present}\). - Lee-Mykland Test: Intraday identification of jump arrival times and magnitudes using local bipower volatility and Gumbel thresholds.

from spxa.calculus.variation import bns_jump_test, lee_mykland_jump_test

bns_res = bns_jump_test(price_series, alpha=0.01)
print(f"Jumps detected: {bns_res.has_jumps}, p-value: {bns_res.p_value}")

lm_res = lee_mykland_jump_test(price_series, times, alpha=0.01)
print(f"Detected jump timestamps: {lm_res.jump_times}")

docs.title: 7. Local Times & Tanaka's Formula (spxa.calculus.local_time)
docs.text:
Estimates semimartingale local time \(L_t^a(X)\) via Meyer's mollified Gaussian kernel estimator:

\[L_t^a(X) = \lim_{\epsilon \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{2\epsilon} \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_s - a| < \epsilon\}} d[X, X]_s\]

Verifies Tanaka's formula decomposition for call and absolute value payoffs:

\[(X_t - a)^+ = (X_0 - a)^+ + \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{X_s > a\}} dX_s + \frac{1}{2} L_t^a(X)\]

and validates the occupation times identity:

\[\int_0^T \mathbf{1}_{\{a \le X_s \le b\}} d[X, X]_s = \int_a^b L_T^u(X) du\] 
from spxa.calculus.local_time import tanaka_decomposition, verify_occupation_times_formula

tanaka = tanaka_decomposition(path, level=0.0)
print(f"Accumulated local time at zero: {tanaka.tanaka_local_time[-1]}")

lhs, rhs, rel_err = verify_occupation_times_formula(path, lower_bound=-0.5, upper_bound=0.5)

docs.title: 8. Malliavin Variational Calculus (spxa.calculus.malliavin)
docs.text:
Provides variational calculus on Wiener space \(\mathbb{D}^{1,2}\): - First Variation Process \(Y_t = \frac{\partial X_t}{\partial x_0}\): Linearized tangent SDE. - Malliavin Derivative \(D_s X_t = Y_t Y_s^{-1} \sigma(X_s) \mathbf{1}_{\{s \le t\}}\). - Bismut-Elworthy-Li Formula: Computes exact Greeks for non-differentiable / digital payoffs without differentiation: $\(\nabla_x \mathbb{E}[\Phi(X_T)] = \frac{e^{-rT}}{T} \mathbb{E}\left[ \Phi(X_T) \int_0^T \sigma^{-1}(X_t) Y_t dW_t \right]\)$ - Clark-Ocone Formula: Explicit replicating portfolio delta representation: $\(\Delta_0 = \frac{e^{-rT}}{\sigma S_0 T} \mathbb{E}[\Phi(S_T) W_T]\)$

from spxa.calculus.malliavin import bismut_elworthy_li_delta, clark_ocone_hedging_delta

# Calculate Delta for a discontinuous Digital Call Option (1_{S_T >= K})
bismut_res = bismut_elworthy_li_delta(
    paths=s_paths,
    terminal_payoff=(s_paths[:, -1] >= K).astype(float),
    times=times,
    bm_increments=dw,
    diffusion_func=lambda t, s: sigma * s,
    discount_factor=np.exp(-r * T)
)
print(f"Exact Digital Delta: {bismut_res.greek_value} +/- {bismut_res.standard_error}")

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to spxa are documented here. Follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• pde/ — finite-difference PDE and PIDE solvers (spxa.pde, spxa.graph.pde). Every scheme is covered by a convergence test against a closed form or a published reference. Contents:
  • Infrastructure.
    • Grids: uniform and sinh-stretched Grid1D with strikes, barriers and spots placed on nodes; TimeGrid with calendar events.
    • Boundary conditions: Dirichlet, Neumann, linear and natural.
    • Operators and time stepping: second-order DiscreteOperator1D with automatic upwinding; ThetaSolver1D (Crank–Nicolson with Rannacher start-up); payoff projection.
    • Results: grid Greeks and __story__() summaries.
  • Early exercise. PenaltyLCP, PSORLCP, BrennanSchwartzLCP and IkonenToivanenLCP, plus complementarity_residual and recorded exercise boundaries.
  • One-factor pricers.
    • BlackScholesPDE: European, digital, American, Bermudan, single, double and discretely monitored barriers, discrete dividends, local volatility, and bumped vega/rho.
    • DupirePDE and local_vol_from_prices.
    • AsianPDE (Večeř; continuous and discrete averages).
    • ShortRatePDE (Vasicek/CIR bonds and European/American bond options).
  • Generators and densities.
    • to_pde and Process.to_pde(): diffusion generators and exponential-Lévy PIDEs.
    • FokkerPlanck1D: a discrete-adjoint density solver that conserves mass to machine precision.
  • Lévy PIDEs. LevyJumpOperator (cell-integrated large jumps, moment-matched small jumps, FFT convolution) and LevyPIDE for European and American options under Merton, Kou, VG, CGMY and NIG.
  • Two-factor ADI.
    • Building blocks: Grid2D, Dirichlet2D/Neumann2D/Natural2D/Linear2D, LinearPDE2D, DiscreteOperator2D.
    • ADISolver: Douglas, Craig–Sneyd, modified Craig–Sneyd and Hundsdorfer–Verwer, with damping steps and Ikonen–Toivanen early exercise.
    • HestonPDE: European and American, with Greeks and vega.
    • TwoAssetBlackScholesPDE: exchange, spread, best-of and worst-of options, European or American.
  • Cross-checks and bridges.
    • longstaff_schwartz and lsm_american: two-pass least-squares Monte Carlo.
    • pde_price and pde_pricing_fn: price spxa.risk instruments and feed StressTestingEngine.
    • spxa.graph.pde.bs_pde_price_node and heston_pde_price_node: graph nodes whose vector–Jacobian products use the grid Greeks.
  • Verification.
    • Convergence tools: convergence_study, observed_order and richardson_extrapolate.
    • Closed-form references in spxa.pde.reference: Black–Scholes, Reiner–Rubinstein, binomial trees, perpetual put, Lewis with Heston/Lévy characteristic functions, Merton series, Vasicek/CIR bonds and options, Margrabe, spread options.
  • Documentation. See docs/theory/pde.md and section 19 of the API reference.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• zoo.levy.CGMY: the Lévy density, total mass, tail and drift now temper upward jumps with \(M\) and downward jumps with \(G\), as the characteristic exponent does; previously they described the mirror-image process. For \(1 \le Y < 2\) the drift now includes the \(-\int_{|x|>1} x\,\nu(dx)\) correction. The first cumulant is no longer rejected as nonexistent when \(\Gamma(1-Y)\) is finite.
  • zoo.levy.NIG: the triplet drift and tail integrated the NIG probability density instead of the Lévy density. The drift now follows from \(\mathbb{E}[X_1] = \mu + \delta\beta/\gamma\), and the tail integrates the Lévy density.
  • zoo.levy.KouJumpDiffusion: char_func now uses the closed-form exponent. The inherited numerical Lévy–Khintchine integral returned nan at complex arguments such as \(u = -i\).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• morph/ — Model Morphing (spxa.morph, spxa.graph.morph): continuous interpolation between processes. The triplet homotopy \(\psi_\alpha = (1-\alpha)\psi_0 + \alpha\psi_1\) is EXACT for Lévy processes. Also includes generator, Fisher–Rao geodesic, Wasserstein and convex-combination morphs; time- and state-dependent schedules (DynamicMorphedProcess); ModelBarycenter, ModelEnsemble and SurfaceMorphEngine; and the Process.morph / spxa.morph API. See docs/theory/model_morphing.md.
  • zoo/beyond/multivariate_hawkes.py — Multivariate Hawkes mutually exciting point process (MultivariateHawkesProcess, MultivariateHawkes, MHawkes): \(M\)-dimensional Hawkes intensity \(\lambda_m(t)\), branching infectivity matrix \(\mathbf{\Gamma}\), spectral radius stationarity condition \( ho(\mathbf{\Gamma}) < 1\), exact expected arrival intensity \(\mathbf{\lambda}_\infty = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{\Gamma})^{-1} \mathbf{\mu}\), and Ogata thinning event simulation.
  • zoo/levy/nts.py — Normal Tempered Stable (NTS) Lévy process (NormalTemperedStableProcess, NormalTemperedStable, NTSProcess): Subordinated Brownian motion \(X_t = heta T_t + \sigma W(T_t)\) with Tempered Stable subordinator, exact closed-form characteristic function, exact cumulant generating function, and subordination simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/kou_sv.py — Kou Stochastic Volatility Jump-Diffusion model (KouSVProcess, KouSV, KouStochasticVolatility): Coupled Heston mean-reverting stochastic volatility with Kou asymmetric double-exponential jumps, affine characteristic function, Lewis Fourier inversion European call/put options, and full-truncation Euler simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/diffusion_bridge.py — General Diffusion Bridge via Doob's \(h\)-transform (GeneralDiffusionBridge, DiffusionBridge, DoobBridge): Drift correction \(\mu^*(x, t) = \mu(x) + \sigma^2(x) \partial_x \ln p(b, T \mid x, t)\) for Brownian, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, and Geometric Brownian Motion bridges, exact moments, and pinned path simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/rough_heston.py — Rough Heston stochastic volatility model (RoughHestonProcess, RoughHeston, RoughVolatility): Fractional Volterra stochastic volatility of order \(\alpha = H + 1/2 \in (1/2, 1)\), singular kernel \(K(t) = t^{\alpha - 1} / \Gamma(\alpha)\), Mittag-Leffler expected variance, power-law implied volatility skew \(|\partial \sigma_{IV} / \partial k| \sim T^{H - 0.5}\), and fractional convolution simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/g2pp.py — Two-Factor Hull–White (G2++) short-rate diffusion model (G2PlusPlusProcess, G2PlusPlus, TwoFactorHullWhite): Two coupled OU factors driving short rate \(r(t) = x(t) + y(t) + \phi(t)\), closed-form zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T)\), Brigo–Mercurio European bond option formulas, and exact bivariate Gaussian factor simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/three_halves.py — 3/2 Stochastic Volatility diffusion model (ThreeHalvesProcess, ThreeHalves, ThreeHalvesModel): Super-linear volatility-of-variance \(dv_t = \kappa v_t ( heta - v_t) dt + \epsilon v_t^{3/2} dW_t\), exact reciprocal CIR transformation \(y_t = 1/v_t\) with automatic Feller satisfaction, Inverse-Gamma stationary law, and exact non-central chi-square path simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/schwartz_one_factor.py — Schwartz One-Factor (1997) commodity diffusion model (SchwartzOneFactor, ExponentialOU, Schwartz1F): Mean-reverting log-spot Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics, exact lognormal transition law and moments, closed-form commodity futures price term structure \(F(t, T)\), and Black-76 European options on futures.
  • zoo/beyond/garch_diffusion.py — Nelson (1990) continuous-time GARCH(1,1) diffusion limit (GARCHDiffusion, ContinuousGARCH, GARCHDiffusionProcess): Linear diffusion coefficient \(g(v) = \sigma v\), exact Inverse-Gamma stationary distribution, conditional moments from linear moment ODE system, and guaranteed-positive log-Euler simulation.
  • zoo/beyond/bilinear.py — Bilinear Diffusion process (BilinearDiffusion, BilinearDiffusionProcess, AffineDiffusion): Affine drift and affine volatility \(dX_t = (a + b X_t) dt + (c + d X_t) dW_t\), Pearson diffusion family moments, exact second-moment ODE solution, and high-order Milstein boundary simulation.
  • vis/levy_inspector.py — Lévy triplet diagnostic inspector and dual-panel density visualizer: Decomposes \((b, \sigma^2, u)\), classifies finite activity (\(\int u(dx) < \infty\)) vs infinite activity (\( u(\mathbb{R}) = \infty\)), finite vs infinite path variation, estimates Blumenthal-Getoor index \( eta \in [0, 2]\) and singularity order \(s\), and plots near-zero singularity zoom vs tail decay on semi-log scale.
  • vis/surface.py — 3D implied volatility surface and cross-model smile visualizer: Computes and renders 3D \((K, T, \sigma_{\mathrm{IV}})\) surfaces with isoline contours, cross-model smile comparison curves across diffusions, jumps, and stochastic volatility models, and volatility term structure plots.
  • vis/story_dag.py — Process composition DAG visualizer and multi-format exporter: Walks CompositionNode trees and exports to ASCII / Unicode tree structures, Mermaid flowcharts for Markdown previews, Graphviz DOT files, and publication-quality hierarchical NetworkX + Matplotlib diagrams.
  • vis/__init__.py — Unified visualization namespace exposing all diagnostic, surface, and DAG tools.
  • examples/visualization_example.py — End-to-end demonstration script generating sample plots and diagrams.
  • tests/unit/test_vis.py — Comprehensive unit test suite for all visualization submodules.
  • sim/milstein.py — High-order 1D and multivariate commutative Milstein simulation schemes: Order 1.0 strong convergence with analytical or automatic centered finite-difference diffusion derivatives.
  • sim/runge_kutta.py — Derivative-free Stochastic Runge-Kutta schemes: Strong order 1.0 Kloeden-Platen scheme (matching Milstein accuracy without diffusion derivatives) and weak order 2.0 scheme for expectation evaluation.
  • sim/qmc.py — Quasi-Monte Carlo simulation engine: Sobol and Halton low-discrepancy sequences, Owen scrambling, and hierarchical Brownian bridge path construction.
  • sim/variance_reduction.py — Comprehensive variance reduction toolkit: Optimal single/multivariate control variate regression estimator, antithetic Gaussian and Brownian paths, Girsanov importance sampling with Radon-Nikodym likelihood weights, and 1D stratified uniform sampling.
  • sim/predictor_corrector.py — Drift-implicit predictor-corrector schemes for stiff SDEs: Unconditionally stable trapezoidal integration for stiff mean-reverting processes.
  • sim/mlmc.py — Giles (2008) Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) framework: Optimal \(O(\epsilon^{-2})\) estimation complexity, adaptive level selection, and optimal variance allocation.
  • examples/simulation_backends_example.py — Comprehensive demonstration of all advanced simulation backends.
  • zoo/beyond/cbi.py — CBISubordinator (CBIProcess, DawsonWatanabeProcess, ContinuousStateBranching): Dawson-Watanabe continuous-state branching process with continuous and jump immigration (Kawazu & Watanabe 1971; Dawson & Li 2012): \(dX_t = (a - b X_t) dt + \sqrt{c X_t} dW_t + dJ_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form Riccati solution \(v(t, \lambda)\), affine Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t}]\), exact conditional mean and variance with compound Poisson immigration, analytical extinction probability for pure CSBP, and high-order Milstein simulation with non-negative reflection. References: Kawazu & Watanabe (1971); Dawson & Li (2012); Li (2011); Grey (1974).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cbi Dawson-Watanabe Milstein sampler with jump immigration.
  • zoo/beyond/chen.py — ChenModel (ChenThreeFactor, ChenShortRate, ChenProcess): Chen (1996) three-factor interest rate model with stochastic central tendency (mean) and stochastic variance: \(dr_t = k ( heta_t - r_t) dt + \sqrt{\zeta_t r_t} dW_{1,t}\), \(d heta_t = \kappa ( ar{ heta} - heta_t) dt + \alpha \sqrt{ heta_t} dW_{2,t}\), \(d\zeta_t = \lambda ( ar{\zeta} - \zeta_t) dt + eta \sqrt{\zeta_t} dW_{3,t}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form expectations, Feller condition analytics, exact 10-dimensional matrix exponential moment system for second moments and conditional variance, term structure zero-coupon bond pricing and yield curve, and coupled 3-factor simulation. References: Chen (1996).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_chen coupled 3-factor path sampler.
  • zoo/beyond/regime_switching_gbm.py — RegimeSwitchingGBM (RSGBM, RegimeSwitchingBlackScholes, MarkovSwitchingGBM): Continuous-time Markov-modulated Black-Scholes diffusion of Hamilton (1989), Naik (1993), and Guo (2001): \(dS_t = \mu(Y_t) S_t dt + \sigma(Y_t) S_t dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact CTMC transition probabilities \(P(t) = \exp(Q t)\), stationary probability distribution \( oldsymbol{\pi}\), arbitrary order exact matrix exponential moments \(\mathbb{E}[S_t^n \mid S_0, Y_0]\), continuous characteristic function via matrix exponentials, closed-form Gil-Pelaez European call and put option pricing with machine-precision put-call parity, and coupled Markov-jump and diffusion path simulation. References: Hamilton (1989); Naik (1993); Guo (2001); Elliott, Aggoun, & Moore (1994).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_regime_switching_gbm coupled Markov chain and diffusion path sampler.
  • zoo/beyond/jacobi.py — JacobiProcess (JacobiDiffusion, WrightFisherDiffusion, Jacobi): Jacobi bounded diffusion model on \([y_{\min}, y_{\max}]\) (canonical \([0, 1]\)) of Ackerer, Filipović, & Turnes (2018): \(dY_t = \kappa ( heta - Y_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{ rac{(Y_t - y_{\min})(y_{\max} - Y_t)}{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}} dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact Beta stationary law \(\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha, eta)\), exact polynomial moment propagation (mean, second moment, and conditional variance), Feller boundary classifications at both lower and upper endpoints (entrance vs regular reflecting), and high-order Milstein path simulation with strict boundary preservation. References: Ackerer, Filipović, & Turnes (2018); Karlin & Taylor (1981); Filipović & Larsson (2016).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_jacobi Milstein path simulator for bounded intervals.
  • zoo/beyond/bns.py — BNSModel (BNSProcess, BarndorffNielsenShephard, BNS): Non-Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic volatility model of Ole E. Barndorff-Nielsen & Neil Shephard (2001): \(dX_t = (\mu + eta \sigma_t^2) dt + \sigma_t dW_t + ho dZ_{\lambda t}, \quad d\sigma_t^2 = -\lambda \sigma_t^2 dt + dZ_{\lambda t}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Gamma-OU variance driven by a compound Poisson BDLP \(Z_t\) with rate \(\alpha\) and exponential jump size \( eta_{bdlp}\), exact stationary variance distribution \(\Gamma(\alpha, eta_{bdlp})\), exact conditional and integrated variance moments, continuous Fourier characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), European call/put option pricing via Gil-Pelaez inversion with exact Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile computation, and coupled vectorized simulation. References: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2001); Nicolato & Venardos (2003); Schoutens (2003).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_bns coupled asset price and stochastic variance simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/schwartz_two_factor.py — SchwartzTwoFactor (Schwartz97, Schwartz2F, SchwartzTwoFactorModel): Canonical two-factor commodity pricing model of Eduardo Schwartz (1997) with mean-reverting convenience yield: \(dS_t = (r - \delta_t) S_t dt + \sigma_1 S_t dW_1^Q(t), \quad d\delta_t = \kappa (\hat{\alpha} - \delta_t) dt + \sigma_2 dW_2^Q(t)\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact closed-form futures pricing \(F(S_t, \delta_t, au)\) via Schwartz (1997) Proposition 1 eq. (12), exact conditional Gaussian moments for convenience yield \(\delta_t\) and log-spot \(X_t = \ln S_t\), exact characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), analytical Black-76 European call and put options with exact Put-Call parity, and joint vectorized path simulation of spot prices and convenience yields. References: Schwartz (1997); Bjerksund (1991).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_schwartz_two_factor joint spot and convenience yield simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/jcir.py — JCIRProcess (JCIR, JumpCIRProcess, JCIRModel): Jump-Extended Cox-Ingersoll-Ross short-rate model of Duffie & Garleanu (2001) and Maghsoodi (1996): \(dr_t = \kappa ( heta - r_t) dt + \sigma \sqrt{r_t} dW_t + dJ_t, \quad r_0 \ge 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features non-negative interest rates with compound Poisson exponential jump shocks (\(Y_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\mu_J)\)), exact stationary mean \( heta_\infty = heta + (\lambda_J \mu_J)/\kappa\) and stationary variance, exact conditional moments at any horizon, closed-form exponential-affine zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T) = \exp(A( au) - B( au) r_t)\) with exact analytical Riccati integration, term structure yields, analytical instantaneous forward rates, exact conditional characteristic function, and exact simulation combining non-central \(\chi^2\) CIR transitions with compound Poisson jump increments. References: Duffie & Garleanu (2001); Maghsoodi (1996); Brigo & Mercurio (2006).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_jcir exact non-central chi-squared + compound Poisson jump simulator.
  • zoo/beyond/bessel.py — SquaredBesselProcess (BESQ, SquaredBessel) and BesselProcess (BES, Bessel): Canonical squared Bessel and Bessel diffusion processes of Feller (1951), Pitman & Yor (1982), and Revuz & Yor (1999): \(dX_t = \delta dt + 2\sqrt{X_t} dW_t, \quad R_t = \sqrt{X_t}, \quad dR_t = rac{\delta - 1}{2 R_t} dt + dW_t\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact transition density and CDF via non-central \(\chi^2\) distribution \( rac{X_t}{t} \sim \chi^2(\delta, rac{x_0}{t})\), exact closed-form cumulants \(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4\) to arbitrary order, exact Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda X_t}] = (1 + 2\lambda t)^{-\delta/2} \exp\left(- rac{\lambda x_0}{1 + 2\lambda t} ight)\), exact continuous characteristic function \(\phi(u; t)\), Feller boundary classification at 0 (entrance for \(\delta \ge 2\), reflecting for \(0 < \delta < 2\), absorbing for \(\delta = 0\)), exact Bessel process confluent hypergeometric moments \(\mathbb{E}[R_t]\), and exact path simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Feller (1951); Pitman & Yor (1982); Revuz & Yor (1999).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_besq and sample_bessel exact path simulators using scaled non-central chi-squared increments.
  • zoo/beyond/schobel_zhu.py — SchobelZhuProcess (SchobelZhu, SchobelZhuModel, SZModel): Schöbel-Zhu (1999) stochastic volatility model: \(dS_t = (r - q) S_t dt + \sigma_t S_t dW_t^S, \quad d\sigma_t = \kappa ( heta - \sigma_t) dt + au dW_t^\sigma\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Gaussian volatility dynamics with non-negative instantaneous variance \(v_t = \sigma_t^2\), exact continuous characteristic function, Gil-Pelaez European Call and Put pricing satisfying exact Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile inversion, and coupled vectorized path simulation. References: Schöbel & Zhu (1999); Lord & Kahl (2007).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_schobel_zhu simulator supporting coupled asset and volatility paths.
  • zoo/beyond/black_karasinski.py — BlackKarasinskiProcess (BlackKarasinski, BKProcess, BKModel): Black-Karasinski (1991) lognormal short-rate model: \(d(\ln r_t) = a(b - \ln r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t, \quad r_t = \exp(x_t) > 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Guarantees strictly positive interest rates across all horizons. Features exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Gaussian conditional moments for log-rate \(x_t = \ln(r_t)\), exact short-rate lognormal conditional and stationary moments, Monte Carlo zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(0, T)\) and yield curve \(y(0, T)\), and exact path simulation without discretization error for \(x_t\). References: Black & Karasinski (1991); Brigo & Mercurio (2006).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_black_karasinski simulator supporting exact log-rate transitions.
  • zoo/levy/gh.py — GeneralizedHyperbolicProcess (GH, GHProcess, GeneralizedHyperbolic): Generalized Hyperbolic (GH) Lévy process of Barndorff-Nielsen (1977) and Eberlein & Prause (2002): infinite-activity pure-jump Lévy process generated by the 5-parameter Generalized Hyperbolic distribution \(GH(\lambda, \alpha, eta, \delta, \mu)\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact characteristic exponent \(\psi(u)\) with modified Bessel \(K_\lambda\) functions, exact cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\) derived from underlying GIG subordinator moments, Lévy triplet \((b, 0, u)\), Gil-Pelaez European Call and Put pricing with exact Put-Call parity, implied volatility smile inversion, subfamily classification (NIG, Hyperbolic, Hyperbolic Cosine), and vectorized simulation via exact Inverse Gaussian subordination and Gil-Pelaez CDF inversion. References: Barndorff-Nielsen (1977); Barndorff-Nielsen & Halgreen (1977); Eberlein & Prause (2002).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_gh simulator supporting exact NIG subordination and Gil-Pelaez inversion.
  • zoo/beyond/sabr.py — SABRProcess (SABRModel, SABR): SABR (Stochastic Alpha, Beta, Rho) stochastic volatility model of Hagan et al. (2002): \(dF_t = \alpha_t F_t^ eta dW_t^F, \quad d\alpha_t = u \alpha_t dW_t^\alpha\) with \(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^F dW_t^\alpha] = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Hagan et al. (2002) asymptotic Black-76 implied volatility closed form with Obłój (2008) corrections, at-the-money (ATM) volatility formula, Black-76 European Call and Put pricing satisfying Put-Call parity, exact forward and log-normal volatility moments, smile backbone classification, and coupled vectorized simulation via log-Euler and Euler schemes. References: Hagan, Kumar, Lesniewski, & Woodward (2002); Obłój (2008).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_sabr simulator supporting coupled forward price and stochastic volatility paths.
