  • zoo/beyond/hull_white.py — HullWhiteProcess (HullWhite, HW1F, ExtendedVasicek): Hull-White (1990) one-factor Gaussian short-rate model (extended Vasicek): \(dr_t = a(b - r_t) dt + \sigma dW_t\) with mean-reversion speed \(a > 0\), volatility \(\sigma > 0\), and long-term target rate \(b \in \mathbb{R}\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact zero-coupon bond pricing \(P(t, T) = A(t, T) \exp(-B(t, T) r_t)\), spot yield curve, instantaneous forward rates, conditional short rate and integrated rate moments, autocovariance, Jamshidian (1989) closed-form European bond Call and Put options with exact Put-Call parity, caplets and floorlets, and exact path simulation without time discretization error. References: Hull & White (1990, 1993); Jamshidian (1989); Vasicek (1977).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_hull_white simulator with exact Gaussian transitions and Euler fallback.
  • zoo/beyond/bates.py — BatesProcess (BatesModel, Bates96, SVJ): Bates (1996) stochastic volatility with jumps model coupling the Heston (1993) CIR variance diffusion with Merton (1976) log-normal price jumps: \(dS_t = (\mu - q - \lambda ar{k}) S_t dt + \sqrt{V_t} S_t dW_t^S + S_{t-} (e^Y - 1) dN_t\), \(dV_t = \kappa ( heta - V_t) dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V\) with \(\mathbb{E}[dW^S dW^V] = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features continuous Albrecher et al. (2007) characteristic function factored with compound Poisson jumps, drift compensator \(-\lambda ar{k}\), high-precision cumulants \(\kappa_1, \dots, \kappa_4\), European Call and Put pricing via Gil–Pelaez Fourier inversion, exact Put-Call parity, Black–Scholes implied volatility smile inversion, and vectorized path simulation via Lord et al. (2010) full-truncation CIR scheme and Poisson jump shocks. References: Bates (1996); Heston (1993); Albrecher et al. (2007); Lord et al. (2010).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_bates path simulator supporting both log-return \(X_t\) and instantaneous variance \(V_t\).
  • zoo/levy/kou.py — KouJumpDiffusion (KouProcess, Kou72, Kou02): Kou (2002) double exponential jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with asymmetric double exponential jump shocks: \(X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\), \(f_Y(y) = p \eta_1 e^{-\eta_1 y}\mathbb{I}_{y \ge 0} + (1-p) \eta_2 e^{\eta_2 y}\mathbb{I}_{y < 0}\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact closed-form Lévy triplet \((b, \sigma^2, u)\) with analytical truncated drift integral, characteristic exponent \(\psi(u)\), analytical cumulants of all orders \(n\), European Call and Put option pricing via Gil–Pelaez / Carr–Madan Fourier inversion, Put-Call parity, Black–Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion, and exact simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Kou (2002); Cont & Tankov (2004).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_kou exact path simulator with zero discretization error.
  • zoo/beyond/cev.py — CEVProcess (CEV, ConstantElasticityOfVariance): Constant Elasticity of Variance (CEV) local volatility diffusion process \(dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma S_t^\gamma dW_t, S_0 = s_0 > 0\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness. Features state-dependent local return volatility \(\sigma_{ ext{loc}}(S) = \sigma S^{\gamma - 1}\), constant return variance elasticity \(2(\gamma - 1)\), boundary classification with absorbing zero (default / bankruptcy risk) for \(\gamma < 1\), exact European option pricing via Schroder's (1989) non-central chi-squared representation across equity leverage (\(\gamma < 1\)), geometric Brownian motion (\(\gamma = 1\)), and commodity inverse leverage (\(\gamma > 1\)) regimes, exact Put-Call parity, analytical absorption probability \(P(S_T = 0) = 1 - F_{\chi^2}(x; 1/(1-\gamma))\), transition CDF, analytical Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Vega), conditional moments (closed-form for \(\gamma \in \{0.5, 1.0\}\) and quadrature propagation for general \(\gamma\)), and vectorized path simulation. References: Cox (1975); Schroder (1989); Emanuel & MacBeth (1982); Choi & Wu (2021).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cev simulation routine supporting second-order Milstein and Euler–Maruyama schemes with absorbing boundary conditions at zero and exact geometric Brownian motion for \(\gamma = 1\).
  • zoo/levy/merton.py — MertonJumpDiffusion (MertonProcess, Merton76): Merton (1976) jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with normally distributed compound Poisson jump shocks: \(X_t = \mu t + \sigma W_t + \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} Y_i\), \(Y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_J, \sigma_J^2)\) under EXACT exactness level. Features exact Lévy triplet \((b, \sigma^2, u)\) with analytical truncated Gaussian drift integral, closed-form characteristic exponent, analytical cumulants of all orders \(n\), Merton (1976) analytical option pricing formula via Poisson mixture of Black–Scholes values, Put-Call parity, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion, and exact vectorized simulation with zero time discretization error. References: Merton (1976); Cont & Tankov (2004).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_merton exact path simulator with zero discretization error.
  • zoo/beyond/heston.py — HestonProcess (Heston): Continuous-time affine stochastic volatility diffusion model \(dX_t = (\mu - rac{1}{2}V_t)dt + \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^S\), \(dV_t = \kappa( heta - V_t)dt + \sigma_v \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V\) with \(d\langle W^S, W^V angle_t = ho dt\) under MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness. Features exact characteristic functions via Albrecher et al. (2007) continuous formulation, CIR instantaneous and integrated variance moments, Feller condition verification, analytical cumulants, European Call and Put option pricing via Gil-Pelaez Fourier inversion, Black-Scholes implied volatility smile/skew inversion via root-finding, and Full Truncation simulation (Lord et al. 2010). References: Heston (1993); Albrecher et al. (2007); Lord et al. (2010).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_heston simulation routine supporting Lord et al. (2010) Full Truncation scheme and truncated Euler scheme.
  • zoo/beyond/ornstein_uhlenbeck.py — OrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess (OrnsteinUhlenbeck, Vasicek): Continuous-time Gaussian mean-reverting diffusion \(dX_t = heta(\mu - X_t)dt + \sigma dW_t\) with MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features exact Gaussian transition density, exact conditional moments and cumulants, stationary distribution \(N(\mu, \sigma^2/(2 heta))\), relaxation time \( au = 1/ heta\), half-life \(t_{1/2} = \ln(2)/ heta\), exponential autocovariance and autocorrelation, two-time covariance, Lorentzian power spectral density \(S(\omega) = \sigma^2/(\pi( heta^2+\omega^2))\), exact Laplace transform and characteristic function, Vasicek zero-coupon bond pricing \(P( au) = A( au)e^{-B( au)r_0}\), yield curves, and asymptotic long-term yield. References: Uhlenbeck & Ornstein (1930); Vasicek (1977).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_ou supporting exact Gaussian increments without discretization bias (method="exact") and Euler–Maruyama discretisation (method="euler").
  • zoo/beyond/cir.py — CIRProcess (CoxIngersollRoss): Cox–Ingersoll–Ross square-root diffusion process \(dr_t = \kappa( heta - r_t)dt + \sigma\sqrt{r_t}dW_t\) with MOMENT_PROPAGATION exactness level. Features Feller condition evaluation (\(2\kappa heta \ge \sigma^2\)), exact non-central chi-squared transition density and exact simulation via sample_cir, exact conditional moments and cumulants of all orders, stationary Gamma distribution properties, exponential autocovariance, exact Laplace transform and characteristic function, zero-coupon bond pricing \(P( au) = A( au)e^{-B( au)r_0}\) via the Riccati system, yield curves, and asymptotic long-term yield. References: Cox, Ingersoll & Ross (1985); Feller (1951).
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_cir supporting exact non-central chi-squared transition sampling (method="exact"), full-truncation Euler–Maruyama (method="truncated_euler"), and reflected Euler–Maruyama (method="reflected_euler").
  • zoo/levy/compound_poisson.py — CompoundPoisson: general compound Poisson process with homogeneous Poisson arrival counter and parameterised jump distributions (NormalJump, ExponentialJump, DoubleExponentialJump, UniformJump, DiscreteJump). EXACT exactness level with closed-form Lévy triplet (b=λ·E[Y·𝟙_{|Y|≤1}], σ²=0, ν=λ·F_Y), exact characteristic function φ(u;t) = exp(λt(φ_Y(u)-1)), exact cumulants of all orders κ_n = λ·t·E[Yⁿ], and vectorized exact Poisson thinning simulation. References: Kingman (1993); Cont & Tankov (2004) Sec. 3.4; Sato (1999) Ex. 8.4.
  • sim/exact.py — Vectorized sample_compound_poisson using np.repeat and np.bincount with fallback for non-vectorized custom samplers.
  • zoo/beyond/mmpp.py — MarkovModulatedPoissonProcess: N-state MMPP (CTMC-modulated Poisson counts). MOMENT_PROPAGATION; no Levy triplet (dependent increments). Exact event-driven simulation, finite-horizon mean/variance and cumulants of any order via block matrix exponentials (with a conditioning guard), stationary distribution and mean intensity. Reference: Fischer & Meier-Hellstern (1993), Performance Evaluation 18, 149-171.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Minimum NumPy raised to numpy>=2.0. The library uses np.trapezoid, which does not exist in NumPy 1.x, so the old numpy>=1.24 lower bound allowed broken installs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• rough/riccati.py — FractionalRiccatiSolver: corrected the sign of the linear Riccati coefficient to \((i\rho\nu u - \lambda)\), and the characteristic function now uses \(V_0 I^{1-\alpha}h(T) = V_0\int_0^T F(u, h(s))\,ds\) (El Euch & Rosenbaum 2019). It reduces to the classical Heston closed form at \(H = 1/2\).
  • rough/rbergomi.py — RoughBergomi simulates the Riemann–Liouville driver and its Brownian motion jointly and exactly (Cholesky), so \(\rho\) now correlates returns with variance and \(\mathbb E[v_t] = \xi_0\). theoretical_short_time_skew gains the missing \(1/(H + 3/2)\) factor (Fukasawa). Added FractionalKernel.volterra_joint_covariance and sample_volterra_cholesky.
  • signature/kernel.py — the Goursat solver weighted the increment term by 5/4. It is now the second-order trapezoidal scheme, converging to \(I_0(2)\) for \(X = Y = t\).
  • signature/algebra.py — level-3 log-signature Hall coordinates were twice their true value. log_signature_dimension computes the Möbius function exactly; the old lookup table stopped at \(n = 6\), which gave wrong Witt dimensions from depth 10.
  • calibration/surface/{heston,bates,double_heston}.py — the share-measure probability \(P_1\) normalised \(\varphi(u - i)\) by \(S_0\) instead of \(\varphi(-i) = S_0e^{rT}\), so every call price was wrong when \(r \ne 0\). Regression tests now check against the Black–Scholes and Merton limits.
  • calibration/filter/particle_filter.py — BootstrapParticleFilter discarded the previous weights on steps without resampling. Weights are now carried forward, and the incremental likelihood is \(\log\sum_i w_{k-1}^i p(y_k \mid x_k^i)\). Checked against the exact Kalman log-likelihood.
  • calibration/mle/hac.py — newey_west_hac(kernel="quadratic_spectral") silently used Bartlett weights. It now implements the Andrews (1991) kernel and rejects unknown kernels.
  • scripts/extract_changelog.py — the release workflow's note extractor did not match bracketed Keep a Changelog headings (## [X.Y.Z] — date), so GitHub releases got the placeholder body Release X.Y.Z.

docs.title: [1.0.0] — 2026-09-19
docs.text: Initial public release. Establishes the algebraic core, the 13-process Lévy zoo, the beyond-Lévy category, the ops/sim/analytics layers, multivariate support, and the story renderer.

docs.title: Added — Core engine
docs.text:
• core/exactness.py — ExactnessLevel enum (EXACT / MOMENT_PROPAGATION / SIMULATION_ONLY) with total ordering and combine() rule: operations degrade to the minimum level of their operands
  • core/exceptions.py — SpxaError, ExactnessError, SpxaDegradationWarning
  • core/levy_measure.py — LevyMeasure hierarchy: CompoundLevyMeasure, DensityLevyMeasure, ScaledLevyMeasure
  • core/triplet.py — immutable LevyTriplet(b, σ², ν) with arithmetic (__add__, .scale()), numerical char_exp() via the Lévy–Khintchine formula, and cumulant(n) (Sato 1999, Thm 25.3)
  • core/properties.py — ProcessProperties lattice tracking stationarity, independence, martingale, finite mean/variance, tail index, self-similarity, subordinator flag, Hurst index; propagation rules for +, scaling, and @ derived from Sato (1999) Ch. 11 & 30
  • core/process.py — abstract Process base class; operator overloads +, *, @, -, unary -; each returns a new immutable _ComposedProcess or _ScaledProcess instance; .triplet, .cumulants(), .char_func(), .__story__(), .__story_latex__()
  • story/narrator.py — CompositionNode tree, narrate() plain-text derivation engine, narrate_latex() / story_latex() MathJax-ready LaTeX renderer

docs.title: Added — Process zoo (spxa.zoo.levy)
docs.text:
• BrownianMotion — triplet (μ, σ², 0), exact Gaussian simulation, closed-form char_func_exact()
  • PoissonProcess — discrete Lévy measure, exact inter-arrival simulation, char_func_exact()
  • GammaProcess — subordinator, exact bernstein_function() a·log(1+u/b) (Schilling et al. 2012, Ex. 3.9), exact cumulants, Gamma simulation
  • VarianceGamma — Lévy density C/|x|·exp(Ax−B|x|), closed-form cumulants to order 4 and series above, exact char_func_exact() (Madan, Carr & Chang 1998, eq. 4), exact simulation via Gamma subordination
  • NIG — Bessel Lévy density, exact char_func_exact(), closed-form cumulants, simulation via InvGaussian subordination (Barndorff-Nielsen 1997)
  • AlphaStable — exact char_func, self-similarity index 1/α, Chambers–Mallows–Stuck simulation (Samorodnitsky & Taqqu 1994)
  • CGMY — exact char_func, closed-form cumulants finite for α < 2, series-representation simulation (Carr, Geman, Madan, Yor 2002; Rosiński 2001)
  • InverseGaussianProcess — exact Bernstein function, cumulants (2n−1)!!·μ^{2n-1}/λ^{n-1}, exact char_func, Wald simulation (Tweedie 1957)
  • MeixnerProcess — stable log-cosh characteristic function, exact cumulants to order 4, Gil-Pelaez CDF-inversion simulation (Schoutens & Teugels 1998)
  • TemperedStable — Lévy density C·x^{-1−α}·exp(−λx), exact Bernstein function, cumulants C·Γ(n−α)/λ^{n−α}, CDF-inversion simulation (Rosiński 2007)
  • NegativeBinomialProcess — finite-activity discrete subordinator, exact characteristic function, closed-form cumulants to order 4, exact NegBin sampler (Quenouille 1949)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• core/triplet.char_exp: split-integral SciPy compatibility (no points kwarg with infinite limits)
  • zoo/vg: triplet drift singularity — switched to tail integrals on [1, ∞) anchored to the exact mean; cumulants() and char_func() overridden with exact closed-form formulas
  • zoo/gamma: triplet drift replaced from quadrature to exact exponential integral E₁(b)
  • zoo/nig: char_func() overridden to route through char_func_exact, eliminating Lévy–Khintchine numerical overflow at large |u|
  • zoo/beyond/fbm: Davies–Harte circulant embedding off-by-one and broadcast error
  • sim/euler.geometric_levy: switched to MGF-based drift correction for non-Gaussian drivers
  • ops/bernstein_function: stabilised elementwise computation, avoiding log(0)
  • core/_ComposedProcess.simulate: subordination (@) implemented via path interpolation
  • analytics/fourier: replaced deprecated np.trapz with np.trapezoid (NumPy 2.x)
  • pyproject.toml: corrected build backend to setuptools.build_meta

docs.title: 1. Overview and Core Philosophy
docs.text:
In quantitative finance, models have historically been siloed across distinct libraries: - One implementation for closed-form analytics (e.g. characteristic function quadrature). - Another implementation for Monte Carlo simulation paths. - Finite difference routines for Greek sensitivities. - Specialized optimization loops for model calibration.

spxa.graph solves this fragmentation by treating stochastic processes, analytical transforms, payoff functions, and risk metrics as nodes in a shared Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). A stochastic model is defined once; the execution engine then dynamically routes evaluation across: 1. Analytical Backend: Closed-form solutions and exact moments. 2. Numerical Backend: Fourier transforms (Carr-Madan, Lewis, Cosine methods). 3. Simulation Backend: Pathwise Monte Carlo sampling. 4. Accelerated Backend: Vectorized batch evaluation across thousands of strikes and maturities. 5. Autodiff Tape: Exact, zero-truncation sensitivities (Delta, Gamma, Vega, Rho, Theta) via reverse-mode vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) and forward-mode dual numbers.

docs.title: A. European Option Pricing and Automated Greeks
docs.text:
from spxa.graph import (
    build_black_scholes_pricing_graph,
    compute_graph_greeks,
)

# Build a Black-Scholes pricing DAG
graph = build_black_scholes_pricing_graph(
    s0=100.0,
    k=100.0,
    t=1.0,
    r=0.05,
    sigma=0.2,
    is_call=True,
)

# Evaluate closed-form analytical price
results = graph.evaluate()
print("Call Price:", results["price"])

# Compute exact Greeks via reverse-mode autodiff tape
greeks = compute_graph_greeks(graph)
print("Delta:", greeks["delta"])
print("Gamma:", greeks["gamma"])
print("Vega :", greeks["vega"])
print("Theta:", greeks["theta"])
print("Rho  :", greeks["rho"])

docs.title: B. Graph-Based Model Calibration
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from spxa.graph import (
    ComputationalGraph,
    GraphCalibrator,
    MSELossNode,
    ParameterNode,
)

# Build parameter recovery problem
param_a = ParameterNode(value=0.0, name="slope")
param_b = ParameterNode(value=0.0, name="intercept")

# Setup synthetic targets
x_data = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 50)
y_target = 3.5 * x_data + 1.2

calibrator = GraphCalibrator()
loss_node = MSELossNode(prediction_node=..., target=y_target)

docs.title: 4. Graph Optimization Passes
docs.text: The GraphCompiler optimizes the DAG before execution: - Constant Folding: Subgraphs depending purely on ConstantNode are pre-evaluated at compile time. - Common Subexpression Elimination (CSE): Identical mathematical operations with identical inputs are merged into single nodes. - Dead Code Elimination: Pruning of nodes unreferenced by any downstream target. - Execution Caching: Thread-safe evaluation cache for instant reuse of stationary nodes.

docs.title: 5. Universal Implementation Layer (spxa.graph.adapters)
docs.text: Rather than requiring manually handwritten graph nodes for every one of the ~200 processes in spxa.zoo or objects in other submodules, spxa.graph provides an automatic reflection and adaptation layer:

docs.title: A. Zero-Boilerplate Zoo Process Adaptation
docs.text:
Any process from spxa.zoo (e.g. BatesModel, VarianceGamma, NIG, CIRProcess, BNSModel, etc.), as well as any composed process (\(X + Y\), \(c \cdot X\), \(X @ T\)), can be directly used in computational graphs:

from spxa.zoo import BatesModel, VarianceGamma

# 1. Any zoo process immediately has .to_graph()
bates = BatesModel(v0=0.04, kappa=2.0, theta=0.04, sigma_v=0.3, rho=-0.5)
bates_node = bates.to_graph()

# 2. Parameters are automatically discovered and mutable
bates_node.params["v0"].value = 0.05
bates_node.sync_parameters_to_process()

# 3. Graph nodes for simulation and characteristic function are auto-generated
cf_node = bates_node.char_func_node(u=0.5, t=1.0)
sim_node = bates_node.simulate_node(t=1.0, n_paths=1000, n_steps=100)

docs.title: B. Submodule Integration (risk, diff, calculus, copula)
docs.text:
• Risk Instruments (spxa.risk): Instruments (EuropeanOption, BarrierOption, AsianOption) and Portfolio have .to_graph() returning automated payoff and sensitivity aggregation graphs.
  • Differentiable SDEs (spxa.diff): DifferentiableSDE models have .to_graph() providing drift, diffusion, and Euler step graph nodes.
  • Copulas (spxa.copula): Copulas have .to_graph() providing coupled uniform sampling nodes.
  • Generators (spxa.calculus): InfinitesimalGenerator adapts into graph operator nodes evaluating \(\mathcal{A} f(x)\).

docs.title: 6. Deep Mathematical Calculus on Stochastic Processes
docs.text: The computational graph serves as a first-class algebraic engine for advanced stochastic calculus:

docs.title: A. Automated Itô Lemma (ItoTransformNode)
docs.text: Applies Itô's Lemma to derive the exact SDE of \(Y_t = f(X_t, t)\) automatically using graph derivatives: $\(dY_t = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} + \mu \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} + \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2}\right) dt + \sigma \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} dW_t\)$

docs.title: B. Measure Changes (GirsanovTransformNode, EsscherTransformNode)
docs.text:
• Girsanov Drift Shifts: Shifts diffusion drift under market price of risk \(\lambda(x, t)\): \(\mu^\mathbb{Q} = \mu^\mathbb{P} - \sigma \lambda\).
  • Esscher Transforms: Shifts characteristic exponents for jump processes: \(\Psi_\theta(u) = \Psi(u - i\theta) - \Psi(-i\theta)\).

docs.title: C. Bochner Subordination & Cumulant Generation (BochnerSubordinationNode, AutomatedCumulantNode)
docs.text:
• Composes parent Lévy exponent with subordinator Laplace exponent: \(\Psi_Z(u) = -\Phi_T(-\Psi_X(u))\).
  • Automatically extracts cumulants \(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4\) to arbitrary order by real central differentiation of the CGF \(K(s) = \Psi(-is)\).

docs.title: D. Infinitesimal Generators & Martingale Verification (InfinitesimalGeneratorNode, MartingaleVerificationNode)
docs.text:
• Evaluates Dynkin's formula \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = \mu(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2(x) f''(x)\).
  • Algebraically checks whether \(f(X_t)\) is a true martingale by proving \(\mathcal{A} f(x) \equiv 0\) across the state space.

docs.title: E. Speed / Scale Density & Feller Boundary Classification (ScaleDensityNode, SpeedDensityNode, FellerBoundaryClassifierNode)
docs.text:
• Computes scale density \(s(x) = \exp\left(-\int \frac{2\mu}{\sigma^2}\right)\) and speed density \(m(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma^2 s}\).
  • Classifies 1D diffusion boundaries into Feller types: Regular, Exit, Entrance, or Natural.

docs.title: F. Malliavin Calculus & Bismut Integration by Parts (MalliavinBismutDeltaNode)
docs.text:
• Simulates the first variation process \(Y_t = \partial X_t / \partial x_0\) alongside \(X_t\).
  • Evaluates pathwise Bismut weights \(\pi_T = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \frac{Y_t}{\sigma(X_t)} dW_t\), computing exact Greek sensitivities of discontinuous payoffs without payoff mollification.

docs.title: 7. Advanced Stochastic Foundations
docs.text: The engine includes three theoretical pillars bridging stochastic analysis and computational graphs:

docs.title: A. Semimartingale Decomposition Wires & Algebra (spxa.graph.semimartingale)
docs.text: In continuous-time stochastic calculus, semimartingales form the largest class of processes with respect to which stochastic integrals can be defined. - Typed Semimartingale Wires (SemimartingaleWire): Graph edges carry continuous-time processes decomposed into their canonical components: $\(X_t = X_0 + A_t + M_t^c + J_t\)$ where \(A_t\) is continuous of finite variation, \(M_t^c\) is a continuous local martingale, and \(J_t\) is a pure jump process. - Quadratic Covariation Operator (QuadraticCovariationNode): Computes the pathwise and predictable bracket \([X, Y]_t\) and \(\langle X^c, Y^c \rangle_t\): $\([X, Y]_t = \lim_{|\Pi| \to 0} \sum_{i} (X_{t_{i+1}} - X_{t_i})(Y_{t_{i+1}} - Y_{t_i})\)$ - Stochastic Product & Integration by Parts (StochasticProductNode): Evaluates the product \(Z_t = X_t Y_t\) verifying the stochastic integration by parts formula: $\(d(X_t Y_t) = X_{t-} dY_t + Y_{t-} dX_t + d[X, Y]_t\)$ achieving machine-precision bracket balance (\(\epsilon \sim 10^{-15}\)). - Predictable Itô Integrals (StochasticIntegralNode): Computes \((H \cdot X)_t = \int_0^t H_s dX_s\) with exact Itô isometry \(\mathbb{E}[(H \cdot M)_t^2] = \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^t H_s^2 d\langle M \rangle_s\right]\).

docs.title: B. Four-Facet Representation Duality Engine (spxa.graph.duality)
docs.text:
Processes are mathematically dual across four equivalent representations: 1. SDE Facet (SDEFacet): \(dX_t = \mu(X_t) dt + \sigma(X_t) dW_t + J_t\). 2. Infinitesimal Generator Facet (GeneratorFacet): \(\mathcal{A} f(x) = \mu(x) f'(x) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2(x) f''(x)\). 3. Fourier Characteristic Exponent Facet (FourierFacet): \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_t}] = \exp(t \Psi(u))\). 4. Speed / Scale Density Facet (DensityFacet): Invariant measure \(\pi(x) \propto m(x)\).

The ProcessDualityCore automatically synthesizes missing representations: - Given an SDE, derives the infinitesimal generator and speed/scale density. - Given an infinitesimal generator, inverts for the drift \(\mu(x) = \mathcal{A}(\text{id})(x)\) and diffusion \(\sigma^2(x) = \mathcal{A}(x^2) - 2x\mathcal{A}(x)\). - Lévy-Khintchine Triplet Compiler (compile_levy_khintchine, triplet_to_fourier_facet): Directly compiles arbitrary triplets \((b, \sigma^2, \nu)\) into executable characteristic exponents: $\(\Psi(u) = i b u - \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 u^2 + \int_{\mathbb{R}} \left( e^{i u y} - 1 - i u y \mathbf{1}_{|y|\le 1} \right) \nu(dy)\)$

docs.title: C. Algebraic Process Surgery Operators (spxa.graph.surgery)
docs.text: Advanced operators that transform stochastic paths and boundary conditions algebraically: - Doléans Exponential & Stochastic Logarithm (DoleansExponentialNode, StochasticLogarithmNode): Computes the stochastic exponential martingale: $\(\mathcal{E}(X)_t = \exp\left(X_t - X_0 - \frac{1}{2}\langle X^c \rangle_t\right) \prod_{s \le t} (1 + \Delta X_s) e^{-\Delta X_s}\)$ and its inverse, the stochastic logarithm \(\mathcal{L}(Z)_t = \int \frac{dZ_s}{Z_{s-}}\). - Tanaka Decomposition & Local Time Extraction (TanakaDecompositionNode): Decomposes positive convex envelopes and isolates local time \(L_t^a(X)\) at strike \(a\): $\((X_t - a)^+ = (X_0 - a)^+ + \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{X_s > a\}} dX_s + \frac{1}{2} L_t^a(X)\)$ - Doob \(h\)-Transform (DoobHTransformNode): Conditions diffusion paths on staying in a sub-domain or reaching a target via excessive harmonic functions \(h\): $\(\mu^h(t, x) = \mu(t, x) + \sigma^2(t, x) \frac{h'(x)}{h(x)}\)$ (e.g., standard Brownian motion conditioned to stay positive produces the 3D Bessel process drift \(1/x\)). - Stratonovich \(\leftrightarrow\) Itô Conversion (StratonovichToItoNode, ItoToStratonovichNode): Transitions between Itô and Stratonovich calculus by adding or subtracting the midpoint drift correction \(\frac{1}{2}\sigma(x)\sigma'(x)\).

docs.title: 8. Statistical Information Geometry & Manifold Calibration (spxa.geom, spxa.graph.geom)
docs.text: Information geometry equips stochastic process parameter spaces \(\mathcal{M} = \{\theta \in \Theta\}\) with intrinsic Riemannian manifolds rather than flat Euclidean spaces:

docs.title: A. Fisher Information Metric (FIM)
docs.text: The Fisher metric tensor measures informational distance between stochastic transition densities: $\(g_{ij}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_\theta \left[ \frac{\partial \log p}{\partial \theta_i} \frac{\partial \log p}{\partial \theta_j} \right] = - \mathbb{E}_\theta \left[ \frac{\partial^2 \log p}{\partial \theta_i \partial \theta_j} \right]\)$ - Exact Closed Forms: Computed analytically for Gaussians \(g = \text{diag}(1/\sigma^2, 2/\sigma^2)\) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck transition densities. - Numerical & Empirical Score Covariance: Automatically evaluated via finite-difference Hessians and pathwise score vectors.

docs.title: B. Connections & Geodesic Flow
docs.text:
• Levi-Civita Connection & Christoffel Symbols: \(\Gamma^k_{ij}(\theta) = \frac{1}{2} g^{kl} (\partial_i g_{jl} + \partial_j g_{il} - \partial_l g_{ij})\).
  • Amari \(\alpha\)-Connections: \(\Gamma^{(\alpha), k}_{ij} = \Gamma^k_{ij} - \frac{\alpha}{2} g^{kl} T_{ijl}\) where \(T_{ijl}\) is the skewness tensor (\(\alpha = 0\) Riemannian, \(\alpha = 1\) exponential, \(\alpha = -1\) mixture).
  • Rao Hyperbolic Distance (GeodesicFlow): Integrates geodesic paths \(\ddot{\theta}^k + \Gamma^k_{ij} \dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j = 0\) via shooting solvers to measure true model distance \(d_R(\theta_1, \theta_2) = \int \sqrt{g_{ij} \dot{\theta}^i \dot{\theta}^j} dt\).

docs.title: C. Natural Gradient Optimization (NaturalGradientCalibratorNode)
docs.text: Replaces naive Euclidean gradient descent with Riemannian manifold updates: $\( ilde{ abla}_ heta \mathcal{L} = g^{-1}( heta) abla_ heta \mathcal{L}, \quad heta_{t+1} = heta_t - \eta ilde{ abla}_ heta \mathcal{L}\)$ eliminating ill-conditioned ravines, Feller boundary sticking, and parameterization distortions.

docs.title: 9. Rough Paths & Tensor Signature Calculus (spxa.signature, spxa.graph.signature)
docs.text: Path signatures provide a non-parametric, coordinate-free encoding of continuous and jump paths:

docs.title: A. Truncated Tensor Signature & Chen's Identity (PathSignature)
docs.text: For a multidimensional path \(X: [0, T] \to \mathbb{R}^d\), the truncated signature of order \(M\) is: $\(S(X)_{s,t}^{(M)} = \bigoplus_{k=0}^M \int_{s < u_1 < \dots < u_k < t} dX_{u_1} \otimes \dots \otimes dX_{u_k} \in T^{(M)}(\mathbb{R}^d)\)$ Satisfies Chen's multiplicative identity: $\(S(X)_{0,T} = S(X)_{0,t} \otimes S(X)_{t,T}\)$

docs.title: B. Shuffle Algebra & Free Lie Log-Signature (SignatureAlgebra)
docs.text:
• Shuffle Product: Iterated integrals multiply via shuffles: \(S^u \cdot S^v = \sum_{w \in u \sqcup v} S^w\).
  • Log-Signature Projection: Projects signatures onto the free Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{g}^{(M)}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) via Campbell-Baker-Hausdorff / Dynkin operators, reducing dimensionality according to Witt's formula (e.g. \(15 \to 5\) at depth 3 for 2D paths, a 66.7% compression without information loss).

docs.title: C. Signature Kernels via 2D Hyperbolic Goursat PDE (SignatureKernel)
docs.text: Computes the infinite-dimensional inner product \(K(X, Y) = \langle S(X), S(Y) \rangle\) without tensor truncation by solving the hyperbolic PDE: $\(\frac{\partial^2 K}{\partial s \partial t}(s, t) = K(s, t) \langle \dot{X}_s, \dot{Y}_t \rangle, \quad K(s, 0) = 1, \quad K(0, t) = 1\)$ Runs in polynomial \(O(N_X \cdot N_Y)\) time.

docs.title: D. Universal Linear Pricing (SignatureLinearPricerNode)
docs.text: Represents arbitrary path-dependent payoffs (Asian, lookbacks, barriers) as linear functionals on the expected signature: $\(\text{Price} \approx \langle \mathbf{w}, \mathbb{E}[S(X)_{0,T}] \rangle\)$

docs.title: 10. Rough Volatility & Volterra Stochastic Calculus (spxa.rough, spxa.graph.rough)
docs.text: Extends stochastic modeling to sub-diffusive, non-Markovian volatility surfaces:

docs.title: A. Fractional Singular Kernels & Hybrid Convolution (FractionalKernel)
docs.text:
• Riemann-Liouville fractional power kernel with Hurst exponent \(H \in (0, 1/2)\): $\(K_H(t) = \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} t^{H - 1/2}\)$
  • Bennedsen-Lunde-Pakkanen Hybrid Scheme: Decomposes \(\int_0^t (t-s)^{H-1/2} dW_s\) into exact analytic integration for the singular neighborhood \(s \approx t\) and FFT-accelerated convolution for the regular tail.
  • Exact Fractional Brownian Motion: Cholesky covariance sampling of \(R_H(t, s) = \frac{1}{2}(t^{2H} + s^{2H} - |t - s|^{2H})\).

docs.title: B. Rough Bergomi Model (RoughBergomi)
docs.text: Asset and variance dynamics: $\(S_t = S_0 \mathcal{E}\left( \int_0^t \sqrt{v_s} dW_s \right), \quad v_t = \xi_0 \exp\left( \eta \sqrt{2H} \tilde{W}_t^H - \frac{1}{2} \eta^2 t^{2H} \right)\)$ Reproduces the empirical power-law blow-up of short-time at-the-money implied volatility skews: $\(\psi(\tau) = \left|\frac{\partial \sigma_{BS}}{\partial k}\right|_{k=0} \approx \frac{|\rho| \eta}{2} \frac{\sqrt{2H}}{H + 1/2} \tau^{H - 1/2}\)$

docs.title: C. Fractional Adams-Bashforth-Moulton Riccati Solver (FractionalRiccatiSolver)
docs.text: Solves the non-local fractional Riccati Volterra integral equation: $\(h(t) = \int_0^t \frac{(t-s)^{H-1/2}}{\Gamma(H + 1/2)} F(u, h(s)) ds\)$ providing exact, highly stable characteristic functions \(\mathbb{E}[e^{i u X_T}]\) for the Rough Heston model.

docs.title: Contributing to spxa
docs.text:
spxa is research infrastructure for stochastic process algebra. Correctness and mathematical honesty are non-negotiable. Every contribution must be grounded in a published result, and the library must never silently return an incorrect answer.

This document is the authoritative guide for every type of contribution. Read the section for what you want to add, then follow it exactly.

By participating in this project you agree to abide by the Code of Conduct. Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately as described in the Security Policy, never through public issues.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Nityahapani/spxa.git
cd spxa
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pre-commit install

Dev dependencies: pytest, pytest-cov, sympy, numpy, scipy, ruff, mypy, pre-commit.

Run the full test suite before and after any change:

python -m pytest tests/ -q

All 235+ tests must pass. Never submit a PR that breaks existing tests.

docs.title: A. New Lévy process (zoo/levy)
docs.text:
Open a Process Proposal issue first. The proposal must contain: 1. The Lévy–Khintchine triplet \((b, \sigma^2, \nu)\) in closed form, with derivation or citation 2. Cumulant formulas (at minimum \(\kappa_1\) and \(\kappa_2\)) with citation 3. The primary reference (original journal paper — not a textbook) 4. Proposed ExactnessLevel (must be EXACT for a Lévy process with known triplet) 5. The simulation algorithm with complexity per step

Files to create or modify:

1. Create spxa/zoo/levy/<name>.py

The file must contain:

# Module-level docstring with full mathematical specification:
# - Lévy density k(x)
# - Triplet (b, σ², ν)
# - Cumulant formulas
# - All primary references

def _<name>_levy_measure(params) -> DensityLevyMeasure:
    """
    Lévy density function.
    Cite the exact equation number and reference.
    """
    def density(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: ...
    def tail(xv: float) -> float: ...
    def moment_n() -> float: ...   # for each n you know exactly

    return DensityLevyMeasure(
        _density_fn=density,
        _total_mass=np.inf,        # or finite for compound Poisson
        _tail_fn=tail,
        _moment_fns={1: moment_1, 2: moment_2, ...},
    )


class MyProcess(Process):
    def __init__(self, param1: float, param2: float) -> None:
        # validate parameters
        # store self.param1, self.param2
        # build CompositionNode with math_note and reference
        super().__init__(exactness=ExactnessLevel.EXACT, _node=node)

    def _triplet(self) -> LevyTriplet:
        # Return LevyTriplet(b=..., sigma_sq=..., nu=...)
        # b must be consistent with the truncation h(x) = 1_{|x|≤1}
        # If b is computed by quadrature, use an exact formula (like E_1)
        # when available. See gamma.py for the pattern.

    def _properties(self) -> ProcessProperties:
        return ProcessProperties(
            has_stationary_increments=True,
            has_independent_increments=True,
            is_martingale=...,      # True only if drift=0 and ∫_{|x|>1} x ν(dx) = 0
            has_finite_variance=...,
            has_finite_mean=...,
            self_similarity_index=None,   # fill if self-similar
            tail_index=...,               # α such that ν((x,∞)) ~ x^{-α}, or None
            is_subordinator=...,          # True only if support ⊂ (0,∞)
        )

    def cumulants(self, order: int) -> dict[int, float]:
        # Override with exact closed-form formulas where known.
        # Fall back to super().cumulants() only if no formula exists.
        ...

    def char_func_exact(self, u, t=1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        # If the characteristic function has a closed form, implement it here
        # and override char_func() to call it.
        ...

    def char_func(self, u, t=1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.char_func_exact(u=u, t=t)  # if closed form exists

    def simulate(self, n_steps, n_paths=1, T=1.0, rng=None) -> np.ndarray:
        # Use the most efficient exact algorithm known.
        # Return shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1), paths[:, 0] == 0.
        ...

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"MyProcess(param1={self.param1}, param2={self.param2})"

2. Add to spxa/zoo/levy/__init__.py

from spxa.zoo.levy.<name> import MyProcess
# add to __all__

3. Add to spxa/zoo/__init__.py

from spxa.zoo.levy import ..., MyProcess
# add to __all__

4. Add to spxa/__init__.py

from spxa.zoo import ..., MyProcess
# add to __all__

5. Create tests/exactness/test_<name>.py

Every test must have @pytest.mark.exactness and cite the formula being verified. Minimum required tests:

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_no_gaussian_component() -> None:
    """σ²=0 for pure-jump processes. <Primary reference>."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_char_func_at_zero() -> None:
    """φ(0;t)=1. Definition of characteristic function."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_char_func_time_additivity() -> None:
    """φ(u;s+t)=φ(u;s)·φ(u;t). Sato (1999), Definition 1.6."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_cumulant_1() -> None:
    """κ₁ = <formula>. <Reference, equation number>."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_cumulant_2() -> None:
    """κ₂ = <formula>. <Reference, equation number>."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_simulate_mean() -> None:
    """Empirical mean converges to κ₁. Law of large numbers."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_simulate_variance() -> None:
    """Empirical variance converges to κ₂."""
    ...

If the process is a subordinator, also add:

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_is_subordinator() -> None:
    """Paths are non-decreasing. <Reference>."""
    ...

@pytest.mark.exactness
def test_<name>_simulate_non_decreasing() -> None:
    """All increments non-negative."""
    ...

6. Add to PROCESS_REGISTRY.md

Add a row to the table with: class name, exactness level, available cumulants, simulation algorithm, primary reference.

Pattern to copy: spxa/zoo/levy/gamma.py and tests/exactness/test_gamma.py are the reference implementation.

docs.title: B. New beyond-Lévy process (zoo/beyond)
docs.text:
Beyond-Lévy processes (fBM, Hawkes, OU-Lévy) violate stationarity or independence of increments and therefore have no Lévy–Khintchine triplet.

Files to create or modify:

1. Create spxa/zoo/beyond/<name>.py

Key differences from a Lévy process:

class MyBeyondProcess(Process):
    def __init__(self, ...) -> None:
        # ExactnessLevel is MOMENT_PROPAGATION, not EXACT
        super().__init__(exactness=ExactnessLevel.MOMENT_PROPAGATION, _node=node)

    def _triplet(self) -> LevyTriplet:
        # MUST raise ExactnessError with a clear explanation of
        # which Lévy property is violated and why no triplet exists.
        raise ExactnessError(
            method="triplet",
            required="EXACT",
            actual="MOMENT_PROPAGATION",
            reason="<process name> violates <stationary/independent> increments "
                   "because <mathematical reason>. No Lévy–Khintchine triplet exists. "
                   "Use <what to use instead>.",
        )

    def _properties(self) -> ProcessProperties:
        return ProcessProperties(
            has_stationary_increments=...,   # likely False or process-specific
            has_independent_increments=...,  # likely False
            ...
            notes=[
                "Human-readable explanation of why this is beyond Lévy.",
                "What analytical quantities ARE available.",
            ],
        )

    def _moment_propagation_cumulants(self, order: int) -> dict[int, float]:
        # Implement what you CAN compute: typically κ₁ and κ₂ exactly,
        # and float('nan') for higher orders that are intractable.
        result = {}
        if order >= 1:
            result[1] = ...
        if order >= 2:
            result[2] = ...
        for n in range(3, order + 1):
            result[n] = float('nan')
        return result

    # Add domain-specific analytical methods beyond what Process provides:
    def variance(self, t: float) -> float: ...
    def covariance(self, s: float, t: float) -> float: ...
    def autocovariance(self, h: float) -> float: ...

2. Add to spxa/zoo/beyond/__init__.py, spxa/zoo/__init__.py, spxa/__init__.py

Same pattern as Lévy processes.

3. Create tests/exactness/test_beyond.py entries

Add a class TestMyBeyondProcess to the existing tests/exactness/test_beyond.py. Required tests:

  • test_<name>_triplet_raises — verifies ExactnessError is raised
  • test_<name>_<analytical_property> — verifies each formula you implement against its cited source
  • test_<name>_simulate_* — verifies simulation statistics

Pattern to copy: spxa/zoo/beyond/fbm.py (fBM) and the TestFractionalBrownianMotion class in tests/exactness/test_beyond.py.

docs.title: C. New operation (ops/)
docs.text:
Operations are functions that take Process objects and return a new Process, or take a LevyTriplet and return a new LevyTriplet.

Before implementing, open an issue stating: - The mathematical definition of the operation - Whether the result is exact for independent Lévy processes, or approximate - The theorem or cited result justifying the computation - The ExactnessLevel propagation rule

Files to create or modify:

1. Create spxa/ops/<operation>.py

"""
<Operation name>.

Mathematical basis
------------------
State the theorem. Cite author, year, theorem number.

Exact for: <conditions under which result is EXACT>
Approximate for: <conditions under which it degrades and why>
"""

def <operation>(X: Process, Y: Process, ...) -> Process:
    """
    Brief description.

    Parameters / Returns / Raises / References sections.
    """
    ...

Rules: - If the operation is exact for independent Lévy processes, include a proof sketch or theorem citation in the docstring - If the result degrades ExactnessLevel, emit SpxaDegradationWarning with a mathematical reason — never silently degrade - If the operation requires conditions (e.g. Y must be a subordinator), check them explicitly and raise ValueError with a helpful message

2. Add to spxa/ops/__init__.py

Add the function/class to the imports and __all__.

3. Add tests to tests/unit/test_ops.py

Add a new test class. At minimum:

  • Correctness tests: verify the output against known exact values
  • Exactness tests: verify ExactnessLevel is set correctly
  • Error tests: verify that invalid inputs raise the right exceptions
  • Warning tests: verify that degradation emits SpxaDegradationWarning

If the operation touches the triplet, add a test that verifies the triplet arithmetic against Sato (1999) directly.

Pattern to copy: spxa/ops/subordination.py and the TestSubordination class in tests/unit/test_ops.py.

docs.title: D. New analytic tool (analytics/)
docs.text:
Analytic tools compute quantities derived from the characteristic function or cumulants of a process.

Files to create or modify:

1. Add to an existing spxa/analytics/<module>.py or create a new one

Every function must: - State clearly whether the result is exact or approximate - Say which processes it works for (EXACT only? MOMENT_PROPAGATION too?) - Raise ExactnessError if called on a process whose exactness level is insufficient - Cite the mathematical result being implemented

def my_analytic_function(
    process: Process,
    ...,
) -> float:
    """
    Brief description.

    Exact for EXACT processes via <formula>.
    Requires: <conditions>.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ...

    References
    ----------
    Author (year), equation/theorem number.
    """
    if process.exactness == ExactnessLevel.SIMULATION_ONLY:
        raise ExactnessError(...)
    ...

2. Add to spxa/analytics/__init__.py

3. Add tests to tests/unit/test_ops.py or a new tests/unit/test_analytics.py

At minimum: a test against a known value, a test for the correct error when called on an unsupported process.

Pattern to copy: spxa/analytics/divergence.py and the TestAnalyticsPipeline class in tests/integration/test_composition.py.

docs.title: E. New simulation algorithm (sim/)
docs.text:
Simulation functions produce sample paths or random variates. The bar is high: if you claim a sampler is "exact", it must be exact in distribution — not an approximation.

Files to create or modify:

1. Add to an existing spxa/sim/<module>.py or create a new one

def sample_<name>(
    param1: float,
    param2: float,
    dt: float,
    n_steps: int,
    n_paths: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Exact increments of <process name> via <algorithm name>.

    Algorithm (<primary citation>):
      1. ...
      2. ...

    Parameters
    ----------
    ...

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Increments, shape (n_paths, n_steps). Call increments_to_paths()
        to prepend x0 and convert to paths.

    References
    ----------
    <Full citation, year, algorithm number if applicable>
    """
    ...

Conventions: - Standalone samplers return increments of shape (n_paths, n_steps), not paths. Use increments_to_paths() from sim/exact.py to convert. - If the algorithm is approximate (e.g. Euler-Maruyama approximation to an SDE), state the strong convergence order and conditions in the docstring. - If the algorithm is exact, cite the theorem guaranteeing this.

2. Add to spxa/sim/__init__.py

3. Add tests to tests/unit/test_sim.py

Required: - Shape test: assert increments.shape == (n_paths, n_steps) - Mean test: empirical mean vs theoretical mean (use pytest.approx) - Variance test: empirical variance vs theoretical variance - If the process is a subordinator: non-negativity test, monotonicity test

Statistical tests must use n_paths ≥ 5000 and loose tolerances (rel=0.05 or abs=0.1) — they are Monte Carlo, not exactness tests.

Pattern to copy: spxa/sim/exact.py (sample_gamma, sample_vg) and tests/unit/test_sim.py (TestExactSamplers).

docs.title: F. New multivariate process (zoo/multivariate)
docs.text:
Multivariate processes live in spxa/zoo/multivariate.py and use MultivariateLevyTriplet (matrix \(\Sigma\)) rather than LevyTriplet (scalar \(\sigma^2\)).

Files to create or modify:

1. Add to spxa/zoo/multivariate.py

class MyMultivariateProcess(Process):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, ...) -> None:
        self.dim = dim
        ...
        super().__init__(exactness=ExactnessLevel.EXACT, _node=node)

    def _triplet(self) -> LevyTriplet:
        # Return a 1-d projection triplet (e.g. trace of Σ as σ²)
        # for compatibility with the base class.
        ...

    def multivariate_triplet(self) -> MultivariateLevyTriplet:
        # Return the full d-dimensional triplet.
        ...

    def simulate(self, n_steps, n_paths=1, T=1.0, rng=None) -> np.ndarray:
        # Return shape (n_paths, n_steps + 1, dim).
        # paths[:, 0, :] == 0.
        ...

2. Add to spxa/zoo/__init__.py

3. Add tests to tests/unit/test_multivariate.py

Required: - Shape test: assert paths.shape == (n_paths, n_steps + 1, dim) - Starts at zero: np.testing.assert_array_equal(paths[:, 0, :], 0.0) - Covariance recovery: for a BM-based process, empirical covariance should match the theoretical \(\Sigma\) (use np.testing.assert_allclose(..., atol=0.1))

Pattern to copy: MultivariateBrownianMotion in multivariate.py and TestMultivariateBrownianMotion in tests/unit/test_multivariate.py.

docs.title: G. Core change (core/)
docs.text:
core/ is the algebraic foundation. Any change requires:

  1. Open an RFC issue using the RFC template in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/rfc.md. The RFC must state: motivation, proposed change, backward compatibility impact, and alternatives considered.
  2. Two maintainer approvals before implementation begins.
  3. Full backward compatibility or a deprecation plan spanning two minor versions (see Versioning).

Files in core/ and what they own:

  • exactness.py — the ExactnessLevel enum and combine(). Only add a new level if it is mathematically distinct from the three existing ones.
  • exceptions.py — SpxaError, ExactnessError, SpxaDegradationWarning. New exception subclasses must have a specific mathematical reason.
  • levy_measure.py — LevyMeasure hierarchy. New subclasses must implement density(), total_mass(), tail(), and moment().
  • process.py — Process base class and operators. The operator signatures (__add__, __mul__, __matmul__) are frozen after 1.0.0.
  • properties.py — ProcessProperties and propagation rules. Adding a new property requires updating all three combine_* static methods and all existing processes that set that property.
  • triplet.py — LevyTriplet. The b, sigma_sq, nu fields and the __add__, scale(), char_exp(), cumulant() methods are frozen after 1.0.0.

Test requirements for core changes:

  • All existing tests must still pass
  • New behavior must be covered by tests in tests/unit/test_core.py
  • If the change affects exactness propagation, add a test that verifies the exact ExactnessLevel of a composed process after the change

docs.title: H. Bug fix
docs.text:
Open a bug report issue first using the bug report template. If the bug is an exactness violation (spxa returned an analytically wrong value), add the label exactness-violation — this is the highest priority category.

Files to modify:

  1. Fix the bug in the relevant source file
  2. Add a test in the appropriate test file that would have caught the bug. For exactness violations, the test goes in tests/exactness/.
  3. Add an entry to CHANGELOG.md under ## Unreleased → ### Fixed

For exactness violations specifically:

The new test must cite the published formula that contradicts the wrong value spxa was returning. This test must go in tests/exactness/ and carry @pytest.mark.exactness. The fix must be verified against the published formula in the test, not just against the "fixed" code.

docs.title: I. Documentation
docs.text:
Theory docs (docs/theory/) are formal mathematical write-ups. They must be self-contained, cite primary sources, and match the code exactly — every formula in a theory doc must be implemented in the code and verified by an exactness test.

Tutorials (docs/tutorials/) are Jupyter notebooks. They must be runnable (jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute) and committed with outputs cleared.

API docs are auto-generated from docstrings via mkdocstrings. Improve API docs by improving the docstring in the source file, not by editing generated files.

Docstring format: NumPy style throughout. Every public function and class must have: a one-line summary, a Parameters section, a Returns section, and a References section citing the primary source. Equation numbers in citations are required for any non-obvious formula.

docs.title: The exactness test suite
docs.text:
tests/exactness/ is sacred. It is the mechanism by which spxa guarantees it never silently returns a wrong mathematical result.

Invariants that must never be violated:

  1. No test in tests/exactness/ may carry @pytest.mark.skip, @pytest.mark.skipif, or @pytest.mark.xfail for any reason. If a formula is wrong, fix the formula. If a test is wrong, fix the test. The scripts/check_exactness_markers.py script enforces this in CI.

  2. Every test must have @pytest.mark.exactness.

  3. Every test docstring must cite the exact theorem, equation, or section being verified. The citation must include author, year, and location (equation number, theorem number, or page). Example: 

    """κ₂(X₁) = σ² + θ²ν for VG. Madan, Carr & Chang (1998), Section 2."""

  4. The test must verify a closed-form result, not just "it runs without error" or "the output is positive". Compare against the mathematical formula, not against what the code produces.

  5. Statistical tests (empirical mean/variance) belong in tests/exactness/ only when verifying that the simulation converges to a theoretically known value. Use n_paths ≥ 10000 and tolerances abs=0.05 or rel=0.05 — small enough to catch real bugs, loose enough that they don't flake.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
Linting: ruff for linting and formatting — enforced by pre-commit and CI. Configuration in pyproject.toml.

Type checking: mypy in strict mode — enforced by CI.

Naming: - Process classes: PascalCase (e.g. VarianceGamma, NIG) - Functions: snake_case - Private helpers: _snake_case - Lévy measure constructors: _<processname>_levy_measure()

No comment line breaks. Lines like # ==== or # ---- are prohibited. Section structure comes from function/class definitions.

No commented-out code in PRs. Use git history.

No unnecessary comments. A comment that restates what the code obviously does is noise. Comments should explain why, especially for non-obvious mathematical choices.

Docstrings are not optional. Every public function, class, and method must have a NumPy-style docstring with a References section.

docs.title: Commit conventions
docs.text:
Use conventional commits:

feat(zoo): add TemperedStable — exact cumulants, rejection simulation
feat(ops): add exponential() — stochastic exponential of a semimartingale
fix(zoo/vg): eliminate singularity warning in triplet drift
test(exactness): VG — char_func vs time-additivity
docs(theory): add derivation of subordination triplet formula
chore: update PROCESS_REGISTRY with TemperedStable entry

Scope is the module: core, zoo, zoo/levy, zoo/beyond, ops, analytics, sim, story, docs, test, chore.

Commit granularity: commit after each logical unit of work. Do not batch unrelated changes. Do not commit broken states.

After each commit that adds a feature or fix, push to the remote. The CI runs on every push and a failing CI is a blocking issue.

docs.title: Versioning and deprecation
docs.text:
spxa follows semantic versioning strictly.

core/ and ops/ APIs are frozen after 1.0.0. Adding parameters with defaults is allowed. Removing parameters, changing return types, or changing operator semantics requires a major version bump.

Deprecations must: 1. Emit DeprecationWarning with a clear message stating what to use instead 2. Remain in the codebase for at least two minor versions before removal 3. Have an entry in CHANGELOG.md under ### Deprecated

Breaking changes require: 1. A major version bump 2. An entry in CHANGELOG.md under ### Removed 3. A migration note in the changelog explaining what to do

Every PR must add an entry to CHANGELOG.md under ## Unreleased in the appropriate section (Added, Changed, Fixed, Deprecated, Removed).

docs.title: Differentiable SDE Engine & Hardware Acceleration (spxa.diff)
docs.text: The spxa.diff subpackage provides JAX-accelerated, hardware-vectorized, and end-to-end differentiable simulation and sensitivity engines for continuous and jump-diffusion stochastic differential equations (SDEs).

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. JIT Compilation & Hardware Acceleration:
  2. Compiles full simulation trajectories to native GPU/TPU/CPU machine instructions via jax.lax.scan and jax.jit.

  3. Vectorized batch parallel simulation across hundreds of thousands of Monte Carlo paths via jax.vmap.

  4. Differentiable Numerical SDE Solvers:

  5. solve_euler_maruyama: Standard Itô and Jump-Diffusion discretization.
  6. solve_milstein: Order 1.0 strong convergence with automatic spatial diffusion derivatives computed via forward-mode autodiff (jax.jvp).
  7. solve_srk: Two-stage explicit Stochastic Runge-Kutta predictor-corrector.

  8. solve_reversible_heun: Reversible trapezoidal integrator for memory-efficient backpropagation through time.

  9. Differentiable Stochastic Processes:

  10. Diffusions: DifferentiableGBM, DifferentiableOU, DifferentiableCIR, DifferentiableBESQ, DifferentiableBessel, DifferentiableCEV, DifferentiableBilinear.
  11. Stochastic Volatility: DifferentiableHeston, DifferentiableSABR, DifferentiableThreeHalves.
  12. Jump Diffusions: DifferentiableMerton, DifferentiableKou, DifferentiableBates, DifferentiableHawkes.
  13. Multi-Factor & Commodities: DifferentiableSchwartz1Factor, DifferentiableSchwartz2Factor, DifferentiableVectorOU.

  14. Fractional & Rough: simulate_diff_fbm, simulate_diff_rough_heston.

  15. Sensitivity & Greek Differentiation Engine (spxa.diff.greeks):

  16. Pathwise Automatic Differentiation: \(\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \mathbb{E}[f(X_T)]\).
  17. Likelihood Ratio Method (LRM): Score function sensitivities for discontinuous payoffs (e.g. digital options, barrier options).
  18. Malliavin Greeks: Integration-by-parts on Wiener space via Bismut-Elworthy-Li weights for nonsmooth payoffs.

  19. Higher-Order Hessian Greeks: Second-order cross-Greeks (\(\Gamma, \text{Vanna}, \text{Volga}\)) via jax.hessian.

  20. Neural SDEs & Deep Hedging (spxa.diff.nn):

  21. DifferentiableNeuralSDE: Parameterized drift and diffusion networks.
  22. Deep Hedging Engine: Multi-period optimal hedging under transaction costs and convex risk measures (Entropic risk, Expected Shortfall, Quadratic error).

docs.title: Portfolio AAD & Universal Risk Engine (spxa.risk)
docs.text: The spxa.risk module delivers Tier-1 institutional risk analytics, real-time XVA modeling, regulatory margin and capital engines (ISDA-SIMM and FRTB), and automated Adjoint Algorithmic Differentiation (AAD) across complex multi-asset derivative portfolios.

docs.title: 1. Financial Instruments & Bilateral Portfolios (spxa.risk.instruments, spxa.risk.portfolio)
docs.text:
• Derivatives: EuropeanOption, BarrierOption (discrete/continuous monitoring with in-out parity), AsianOption (running arithmetic average), BasketOption, InterestRateSwap (IRS), and CreditDefaultSwap (CDS).
  • Netting Sets & CSA: Bilateral netting agreements governing independent amounts, uncollateralized thresholds (\(H_C\)), Minimum Transfer Amounts (MTA), and Margin Periods of Risk (MPOR).
  • Dynamic Exposure Profiles: Time-dependent Expected Exposure (\(\text{EE}(t)\)), Potential Future Exposure (\(\text{PFE}_{95}(t)\), \(\text{PFE}_{99}(t)\)), and Expected Positive Exposure (\(\text{EPE}\)).

docs.title: 2. Portfolio Adjoint Algorithmic Differentiation (AAD) (spxa.risk.aad)
docs.text:
Computes the full portfolio Present Value, Delta vector, Vega matrix, and second-order Cross-Gamma Hessian matrix in a single reverse-mode backward pass: $\( oldsymbol{\Delta} = abla_{ oldsymbol{S}_0} \Pi_0, \quad oldsymbol{\mathcal{V}} = abla_{ oldsymbol{\sigma}} \Pi_0, \quad oldsymbol{\Gamma} = abla^2_{ oldsymbol{S}_0} \Pi_0\)$

Includes smooth mollifiers (smooth_indicator) for robust differentiation through non-smooth barrier and digital contract boundaries.

docs.title: 3. Real-Time XVA Engine (spxa.risk.xva)
docs.text: Evaluates comprehensive bilateral valuation adjustments: $\(\text{Total XVA} = \text{CVA} - \text{DVA} + \text{FVA} + \text{MVA} + \text{KVA}\)$ - Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA): Counterparty default risk under collateralization. - Debit Valuation Adjustment (DVA): Own-default risk and credit benefit. - Funding Valuation Adjustment (FVA): Funding Cost Adjustment (FCA) and Funding Benefit Adjustment (FBA) over uncollateralized exposure. - Margin Valuation Adjustment (MVA): Funding cost of dynamic initial margin posting over the trade lifecycle. - Capital Valuation Adjustment (KVA): Hurdle cost of holding economic and regulatory capital.

docs.title: 4. Regulatory Margin & Capital (spxa.risk.frtb_simm)
docs.text:
• ISDA SIMM v2.6+ Engine: Multi-class margin aggregation (Equity, Interest Rate, Credit, Commodity, FX) incorporating intra-bucket and cross-class correlation matrices.
  • FRTB Standardized Approach (SA): Sensitivities-Based Method (SBM) capital requirements across Low, Medium, and High correlation scenarios with Default Risk Charges (DRC).

docs.title: 5. Universal Scenario Generator & Stress Testing (spxa.risk.scenarios, spxa.risk.reporting)
docs.text:
• Historical crisis replay (LEHMAN_2008, COVID_MARCH_2020, INFLATION_SHOCK_2022).
  • Reverse stress testing identifying minimal market displacements that breach loss thresholds.
  • Executive risk reporting (format_risk_executive_summary).

docs.title: Beyond the Lévy Regime
docs.text: spxa is built on Lévy process arithmetic, but many processes used in practice fall outside the Lévy class. This document explains how spxa handles them, what guarantees are maintained, and what is lost.

docs.title: Why the Lévy boundary matters
docs.text:
The Lévy–Khintchine triplet is defined only for processes with stationary and independent increments. Many important processes violate one or both:

Process Stationary increments Independent increments Lévy? Brownian motion yes yes yes Poisson process yes yes yes Variance Gamma yes yes yes Fractional BM (\(H \neq 1/2\)) yes no no Hawkes process no no no OU-Lévy no no no Brownian bridge no yes no

The loss of independent increments means the Lévy–Khintchine formula no longer applies. No triplet exists. Arithmetic cannot be exact.

docs.title: Fractional Brownian motion
docs.text:
Definition (Mandelbrot & Van Ness 1968). The fractional Brownian motion (fBM) \(B^H = (B^H_t)_{t \geq 0}\) with Hurst index \(H \in (0, 1)\) is the unique (up to scaling) centered Gaussian process with covariance

\[\mathbb{E}[B^H_s B^H_t] = \frac{1}{2}\left(|s|^{2H} + |t|^{2H} - |s-t|^{2H}\right)\]

For \(H = 1/2\), fBM is standard Brownian motion. For \(H \neq 1/2\), fBM has long memory (for \(H > 1/2\)) or anti-persistence (for \(H < 1/2\)), and its increments are correlated. It is not a semimartingale for \(H \neq 1/2\), which means Itô calculus does not apply and the Lévy–Khintchine representation does not exist.

What spxa tracks for fBM:

  • The Hurst index \(H\) as the fundamental parameter
  • Self-similarity: \(B^H_{ct} \stackrel{d}{=} c^H B^H_t\), so \(H\) propagates under scaling as \(c \cdot B^H \sim c^1\) in scale, Hurst index preserved
  • Variance: \(\text{Var}(B^H_t) = t^{2H}\)
  • The Hölder regularity: paths are \((H - \varepsilon)\)-Hölder continuous for every \(\varepsilon > 0\)

What spxa does not and cannot track exactly:

  • A distributional triplet (does not exist)
  • Cumulants of compositions involving fBM (only approximated via moment propagation)
  • Addition of fBM with a Lévy process: the result is not fBM and not a Lévy process; spxa degrades to MOMENT_PROPAGATION and issues a warning

spxa's Hurst algebra. For compositions of fBM processes:

  • \(c \cdot B^H\): Hurst index preserved, variance scaled by \(c^2\)
  • \(B^{H_1} + B^{H_2}\) (independent): mean and variance propagate; Hurst index of the sum is \(\max(H_1, H_2)\) asymptotically (the dominant long-memory component governs long-run autocorrelation), but this is an approximation and is flagged as such

docs.title: Hawkes processes
docs.text:
Definition (Hawkes 1971). A Hawkes process \(N = (N_t)_{t \geq 0}\) is a point process with conditional intensity

\[\lambda(t) = \mu + \int_0^t h(t - s)\, dN_s\]

where \(\mu > 0\) is the background rate and \(h : [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)\) is the excitation kernel satisfying \(\int_0^\infty h(s)\, ds < 1\) (subcriticality condition). The process is self-exciting: each event increases the probability of future events.

A Hawkes process does not have stationary increments (conditional on the history, increments are non-stationary) and is not a Lévy process.

What spxa tracks for Hawkes processes:

  • The mean intensity: \(\bar{\lambda} = \mu / (1 - \|h\|_1)\) where \(\|h\|_1 = \int_0^\infty h(s)\, ds\)
  • The variance of \(N_t\): \(\text{Var}(N_t) \approx \bar{\lambda} t \cdot (1 - \|h\|_1)^{-1}\) for large \(t\) (asymptotic result, Hawkes & Oakes 1974)
  • The Fano factor: \(F = \text{Var}(N_t) / \mathbb{E}[N_t]\), which is always \(\geq 1\), measuring burstiness
  • Stationarity of the intensity in the stationary regime (when \(t \to \infty\))

spxa's exactness for Hawkes: MOMENT_PROPAGATION. Simulation uses Ogata's thinning algorithm.

docs.title: OU-Lévy processes
docs.text:
Definition (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2001). The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process driven by a Lévy subordinator \(L\) is defined by the SDE

\[dV_t = -\lambda V_t\, dt + dL_{\lambda t}\]

with \(\lambda > 0\) and \(L\) a subordinator (non-decreasing Lévy process). The solution is

\[V_t = e^{-\lambda t} V_0 + \int_0^t e^{-\lambda(t-s)}\, dL_{\lambda s}\]

Unlike a Lévy process, \(V\) does not have independent increments (the decay structure creates serial dependence). However, it does have a stationary distribution which is infinitely divisible, with a known Lévy–Khintchine triplet. The stationary distribution of \(V\) has Lévy measure \(\nu_V(dx) = \int_x^\infty \nu_L(dy)/y\) (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2001, Proposition 2.1).

What spxa tracks for OU-Lévy:

  • The stationary distribution exactly (triplet is known)
  • The autocovariance: \(\text{Cov}(V_t, V_{t+h}) = e^{-\lambda h} \text{Var}(V_\infty)\)
  • The mean reversion rate \(\lambda\)
  • The marginal moments exactly from the stationary distribution's triplet

spxa's exactness for OU-Lévy: MOMENT_PROPAGATION for path-level operations; the stationary distribution is EXACT.

docs.title: Degradation policy
docs.text:
When an operation mixes process types or leaves the Lévy regime, spxa:

  1. Sets ExactnessLevel to the lowest level among operands
  2. Issues a SpxaDegradationWarning with a message stating: which operation caused the degradation, what mathematical property was lost, and what is still being tracked exactly
  3. Raises ExactnessError if a method requiring a higher exactness level is called on the result (e.g., calling .triplet on a fBM + Gamma sum)

This design ensures the library never silently returns a wrong answer by pretending an approximate result is exact.
